Names come from the hub; home, temporary folders, the assistant and an unknown folder are named here, never after a folder, so no account name shows (`../server/machines.md` ("Token usage by project")).
  Both the sidebar's Main chat row menu and the open main chat's header menu offer **Compact context** and **New main chat…** (only when the hub's `features` include `assistant_compact` / `assistant_main_new`, #1727, `lib/compaction.ts`):
  while compacting, a **Compacting context…** line shows above the input; when done, **Context compacted** shows briefly; on failure the reason is shown and can be dismissed (it only reports changes seen on this page or just finished, not old ones every time you open it).
  Creating a new one asks for confirmation (**Bring a summary of the old chat** is on by default); on success it opens the empty main chat at `/` with the composer docked for the first message, and the old one appears under **All chats › Archived** as "Old main chat · until <month day>".
  **Clear context** (#5095, user-requested alignment with Cindy's `/clear`; hub feature `assistant_main_clear`, `lib/main-clear.ts`): both menus place it between **Compact context** and **New main chat…**, and its `/` list has `/clear` (the main chat's only command; other Persona chats have none). Sending `/clear` alone clears instead of going to Persona; anything more is a message, and so is an edit of the last message to `/clear` (its rewind already ran). On the cleared page `/clear` is listed and does nothing (there is nothing to clear, and it never becomes the new chat's first message). Neither asks first: nothing is deleted, the old chat goes to **All chats › Archived** as with New main chat (`DESIGN_SYSTEM.md` 4.4, the reversible rung). A running turn does not block it (the hub stops it). The page clears in place: the same top bar, an empty middle and the box docked at the bottom, not the centered new-chat page, and the first message starts the new main chat right there (`Starter` with `cleared`). Only the tab that cleared keeps that layout, for the manager it cleared; a reload, another manager, or another device's empty main chat shows the ordinary new-chat page. Until the new chat starts, the top bar has no ⋯ (its items act on a chat) and the box shows the new chat's launcher chip.
  In every chat, a compaction is drawn as a divider "Content above compacted · manual · N×10k tokens before compaction", and `/compact`'s **Compact context** and "Continued from compacted context" fold into that line (hover to see the original text).
  **The currently open row** (#2283): always has the `--hover-2` background (one step darker than the hover `--hover`, visible in both light and dark) and `aria-current="page"`; the sliding hover highlight only follows the mouse and no longer takes the current row's background with it. On an Agent's page opened from inside another page it is that page's row, not the Agent's (#12055, "An Agent opened from inside a page is a drill-down" above).
  Besides being measured when the sidebar re-renders, the sliding highlight's position and exact row horizontal bounds (`left`/`width`) are re-measured when the list layout changes (#2476, #17136, `useGlide`): `[data-glide]` mounts inside `[data-sidebar-scroller]` so it scrolls natively with the rows without scroll-listener wobble, snaps directly when appearing from hidden, and hides whenever the pointer leaves the list or sits over the active row (preventing overlap with `--hover-2`); a `ResizeObserver` watches the list, its sections and every row, plus the end of fold animations, measuring at most once per frame;
  the highlight covers only the visible part of the row (`lib/glide.ts` intersects the row with every enclosing `overflow: hidden` box). When the row goes into a folded group, has zero height or disappears, it fades out, and when it reappears it slides over from where it was.
  When **Recent (not running)** has more than 8 entries or there are more than 5 personal Agents and the current session is further down, it is appended after them. **最近** under Persona chats lists its setting's count (#4873, #5146): an older chat opened from **All chats**, ⌘K, the Inbox or a link joins it once it is among the most recently active that are shown.
  Its group (including ones folded by default) expands once when it opens; after that it can still be folded by hand, and the saved fold state does not change. The list scrolls it to the middle, and until the user scrolls, clicks or presses a key, it scrolls back if content loading above pushes it out of view.
  The current row's ⋯ (Agents) and pin button (personal Agents) are always shown, without hovering; the row end reserves room for them, so hints and badges no longer move aside.
  **The whole sidebar collapses into an icon rail** (#2524, wide screens only): the button right of the account row at the top, or ⌘⌥B / Ctrl+Alt+B, collapses it into a 56px column of icons (expand button, search, New chat, Persona, each page, new Agent, connection status at the bottom).
  The current page has a background, and page counts become small dots on the icon corners (the count is in the accessibility label and tooltip). An icon rail rather than hiding it entirely: pages are still one click away and the expand button is always on screen, so the collapsed state can safely be remembered;
  once collapsed, sessions and the Agents list are found with ⌘K. ⌘B is already the right panel and ⌘⇧B is the browser's bookmarks bar, so it uses Moshi's ⌘⌥B (changeable in Settings). Narrow screens still use the full drawer and ignore this state.
  The focus stays on the column: the rail is drawn in place of the sidebar (and back), so the button pressed goes away; pressed with the focus on it, or ⌘⌥B pressed with the focus anywhere in the column (`data-sidebar-column`), the collapse button drawn in its place takes the focus (`toggleSidebarColumn(keepFocus)` / `takeFocusHandoff` in `lib/layout.ts`), so Tab goes on from there instead of from the page's start.
  **The sidebar's width** (#6466; wide screens only, `views/SidebarResize.tsx`): drag the sidebar's right edge to make it 240–480px wide (default 284; below 240 the Agents filters no longer fit on one row). The width is kept in this browser (`localStorage` key `persona.sidebarWidth`, kept across reloads, other tabs follow); double-click the edge or press Enter on it to go back to the default.
  The edge is reachable with Tab: ← / → narrow / widen it by 16px, Home / End go to the narrowest / widest. It uses the same handle as the side panel's edge (`ui/ResizeHandle.tsx`: a mouse, finger or pen drags it with the pointer captured, and text is not selected meanwhile). However wide it is remembered, the page keeps at least 440px beside it, plus 360px for an open side panel; it gives way as the window narrows (never below the default) and returns to the remembered width when there is room again.
  While dragging, the width is written to the column's `--sidebar-w` CSS variable directly, so the app shell is not re-rendered on every move; the store is written only when the drag ends. The icon rail and the narrow-screen drawer keep their own fixed widths and have no handle.
  The shared handle prevents the pointer-down default action so a navigation link under a moving edge cannot start a native browser drag and cancel resizing; it focuses itself explicitly to keep keyboard resizing available.
  **The sidebar's pages** (#5026, `lib/sidebar-pages.ts`, `views/settings/SidebarPages.tsx`): with many extensions installed the **Pages** group keeps growing, so the pages can be arranged.
  In **Settings › General › Sidebar pages**, drag a row (or use its ↑ / ↓) to reorder, and use its switch to keep it in the sidebar or put it under **More**; **Reset** forgets every choice. **Settings** always stays in the sidebar (it is where this is changed).
  Pages put away sit in a **More · N** row at the end of **Pages**: folded by default, it opens in place, opens by itself while one of its pages is the current page, and when folded shows a dot if a page inside has a badge. The icon rail and the phone drawer's grid show a **⋯** instead,
  which opens a menu of those pages (the last row, **Arrange sidebar…**, goes to settings; picking a page in the drawer closes the drawer like any other page). Pages nobody has arranged: built-in pages stay in the sidebar; extension pages (`nav_page`) take at most 3 places (`EXTENSION_CAP`) and later ones go under **More**,
  so installing more extensions doesn't make the list longer; pages switched on by hand count toward the 3. A page the saved order doesn't know yet goes right before the page that follows it by default (a new extension's page still lands before **Settings**). ⌘K **Go to** still lists every page.
  **Groups** (#9071): an extension's `nav_page` may name a group (`group`, `docs/extensions/extensions.md` "UI slots"), and the user can make their own. Each group is a foldable section of its own (`SidebarSection`'s `Section`, the same fold and the same badge dots when folded, its fold kept as `fold:pages:<id>`), after **Pages** unless moved; a group with no page in the list is not drawn. In the phone's drawer **Pages** stays the grid of icons and the other groups are sections below it; the icon rail lists every page in the groups' order. A page goes in the group the user moved it to, else the one its extension names, else **Pages**; **Settings** stays in **Pages**; More collects the pages put away from every group, at the end of **Pages**. Settings › General › Sidebar pages lists the pages under their groups' headings: each group's ✎ renames it (a blank name gives an extension's group its own back), ↑ / ↓ move it, Pages too, 🗑 removes it with Undo in a toast, its pages going back to where they would be without it (their extension's group, else **Pages**; an extension's group stays away until Reset); **New group** makes one; each page's menu moves it to another group, and dragging it onto a page of another group moves it there too. With no group named and none made, the sidebar and the setting are what they were (`lib/sidebar-pages.ts` `arrangeSections`, `pageGroups`).
  **More can be hidden** (#13798): **Show More** in this settings group defaults on. Off removes the expanded sidebar's row, the icon rail's and phone drawer's menu buttons, and the badges promoted from More's pages. It does not change the pages' individual switches, close a page already open, change the start page or remove a page from quick search. Turning More back on restores its pages, including the ones later extension pages take by default. Settings stays fixed in the sidebar, so the arrangement always has a visible recovery path. This explicit simplified-navigation choice lets its hidden page badges leave the shell; the conversation, Inbox and other existing Needs-you surfaces keep their rules.
  The arrangement (order, put away, More visibility, groups) is the user's on the hub (`pages` of `GET` / `PUT /api/v1/navigation`, `docs/protocol/protocol.md` "Navigation"), so phone and laptop match: read at the hello and on each push (while a change of this browser's is on its way its push is not taken), sent on each change, and a change the hub did not take sent again at the next hello rather than replaced; a hello's read that a later hello or another sign-in overtook is not taken, nor is anything handed over from it (the start page's too). This browser keeps its copy in `localStorage` `sidebar.pages`; an arrangement made here before the hub kept one is handed over once. On a hub (or default manager) without the route it stays in this browser only, as before, and the setting's footer says so. iOS and Android don't have it yet (separate PRs); the retired native Mac app had no such setting. Check: `node web/e2e/sidebar-groups.mjs` (`web/e2e/README.md`).
  **Icon colors** (#10822, `lib/sidebar-icons.ts`): Settings › Advanced › Appearance › **Sidebar icons** (moved out of General in #13398) is **Monochrome** (the default: every page's icon in the neutral ink, as before) or **Colored**: each built-in page's icon in its own named color and an extension's page in the `icon_color` its `nav_page` names, in the list, its groups, More, the icon rail and the phone's grid; the open page keeps the open row's ink. The map, why and the contrast checks are in `docs/design/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md` "Sidebar icon colors". iOS and Android follow in their own changes.
  **Start page** (#9071, `lib/start-page.ts`, `views/settings/StartPage.tsx`): Persona opens on its main chat, as it always has, unless **Settings › General › Start page › Open on** names another page: Overview or any page of the sidebar, an extension's page (`nav_page`) included, listed in the sidebar's order with the extension's name after its page's.
  Only an opening at the root address goes there (a new tab, the installed app, the hub's address typed, `/` with no query): a reload and Back / Forward stay on the page they were on (`PerformanceNavigationTiming.type`), and a link to a page, `/persona` and the sidebar's Persona row still open what they name. It happens before the first paint, from this browser's copy of the choice (`localStorage` `persona.startPage`), so nothing is drawn first and replaced.
  The choice is the hub's (`GET` / `PUT /api/v1/navigation`, `docs/protocol/protocol.md` "Navigation"): read at every hello that did not resume and followed on its `navigation` push, so every device of the user opens on the same page; a browser that has not seen it yet opens on the main chat once and takes it from its next opening. The setting's footer says **All your devices follow.**; on a hub (or default manager) without the route (404) it says the choice is saved in this browser only, and the choice stays here. A choice kept here while there was no record is handed to the hub once it has the route.
  A chosen page that is not there (its extension removed or turned off, the default assistant changed and its extensions lack it, Messages or the workflow board switched off) opens the main chat instead, with no message: the sidebar's pages (`useNavPages`, always drawn) check it once the hub has said which pages there are (the extensions' list read after the hello, the board's switch), and only while the user is still on the page the app opened on. The choice stays; the setting lists it as a page that isn't available now and says, under the menu, that Persona opens on the main chat until it is back (`docs/design/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md` "A chosen page that is not there now").
  Screenshots and the check across two browsers: `node web/e2e/start-page.mjs` against the mock hub (`web/e2e/README.md`). iOS and Android do not read the choice yet (separate PRs).
  **Every sidebar group can fold** (#1417): **Pages** (Overview…Settings; the heading was added in #2524) and the whole Agents block ("+" stays on the title row; the grouping segments fold with the block) can fold too.
  These two do not follow "Fold / unfold all groups", so their headings stay visible when everything is folded. Persona chats, personal Agents, pinned, starting, every group under every grouping mode, idle spaces, **Other agents** and **Recent (not running)** all use the same
  `Section` (`folded` / `onToggle` are required): clicking the heading folds / unfolds, the fold state is stored in this browser (`localStorage` `fold:<key>`) and survives reload; on touch screens without hover the fold arrow is always shown.
  Right of the heading is the count; when folded it is replaced by status dots for the "needs you / done, not seen / working" items inside, so folding never hides what needs attention.
  **The top-level headings stand evenly apart** (#10637): Pages (and the user's page groups), Persona chats, personal Agents, Pending and the Agents list's title row (complete and paged) take one box, the `sidebar-heading` utility (`--sidebar-heading` in `src/styles.css`: 24 px, the fold-all button's height, and 44 px on a touch screen), whatever they carry beside their title; before, each row was as tall as its tallest control, so the title-to-title gaps were 34.25 and 38 px. A group's heading inside a list keeps its own row. `src/views/SidebarHeadingBox.test.tsx` checks the box; `node web/e2e/sidebar-heading-spacing.mjs` measures the gaps in Chrome (`web/e2e/README.md`), as iOS's `SidebarHeadingGapsUITests` does (#10561).
  **A folded group holds no rows, and a long open one draws them a part at a time** (the web usability audit of 2026-11-14, #7440): every sidebar fold (`Collapse` with `sidebarFold`, lazy unless it says otherwise) mounts its rows when it opens and drops them once it has closed, so a folded group of 400 Agents costs its heading. Before, every row stayed mounted under the fold, inert: about 8,800 elements in the sidebar and as many on the phone's Agents page, laid out again on every page switch. A group of the complete list with more than `windowHead + windowPart` rows (50, `src/ui/list-metrics.ts`) is drawn by `views/WindowedRows.tsx` under every grouping: Not on a to-do and a to-do's Agents, a status, a space, Other agents, Idle spaces, Recent (not running), a repository's or worktree's sessions, the chat-list view, and By machine a computer's workspaces, a workspace's tabs and its Other. It draws its first 30 rows and its last row always (so the previous-row shortcut from the first row wraps round to the list's real last row), then parts of 20 while they are within a screen of the list's view (an `IntersectionObserver` rooted at the scroller marked `data-row-scroller`, the sidebar's rows or the Agents page), the part holding the open Agent or the keyboard focus and the two beside it always, and for each other part one empty box of its last drawn height (never drawn: the first rows' average). The rows stay in the list's flow, so sticky headings, folds and their animation, the open row's highlight and scroll into view, Tab and the next / previous row shortcut work as before; and every row is a keyed sibling of the others under one parent, with a hidden mark (`data-rows-part`, no box) where each drawn part starts, so a row keeps its element (its focus, a menu anchored on it, its badge's animation) when an Agent comes or goes above it or the list grows past 50. A list growing past 50 keeps drawing the parts holding the rows it had and lets the observer add the rest, so 10 rows becoming 400 in one update never draw all 400. A list of 50 rows or fewer is drawn as it was. The code is part of the sidebar's own, not a chunk of its own: a chunk that failed to download (a redeploy under an open page, offline) would have blanked the whole app, which has no error boundary around the sidebar. Groups that are not drawn when **Collapse all** / **Expand all** goes out (under a folded group, in a part out of view) take the last one they missed when they are drawn, unless they were folded or opened since (`src/lib/fold-all.ts`, `FoldMissed`); a group drawn for the first time with nothing missed around it keeps its own fold. What a group missed is kept for this visit only: a group not drawn again before a reload shows, after it, the fold it had stored before that Collapse all / Expand all (before #7440 every group was mounted and stored each fold-all at once); Expand all still opens the stored folds of spaces and tab groups (below). Group headings and the pinned Persona row take their heights from a `ResizeObserver` (`SidebarGroup`, `useStickyTop`), not from a layout read when they mount. With 400 Agents at 390 × 844, 4× CPU, a production build's sidebar went from about 8,800 elements to 560 (By to-do, Not on a to-do folded) and from about 8,060 to 1,190 (By machine, the 400-tab workspace open); switching between Overview and Agents went from long tasks of 230–320 ms to none under both, and the longest task of a cold start from 167–171 ms to 74–104 ms on `/agents` and from 231–235 ms to 108–114 ms on `/overview`, where the app's own startup takes 83–88 ms with no extra Agents (`web/e2e/sidebar-many-agents.mjs`, measured against main at 70abf2b3ed). The paged list is bounded and virtualized on its own (below).
  The fold-all button on the Agents title row (the chevrons left of ⋯, `GroupFoldButton`: corners in for Collapse all, out for Expand all) is **Collapse all** / **Expand all** (#3027, matching the app's list settings; before #6447 the ⋯ repeated them): they only touch groups in the Agents block (`useFolded` subscribes per block via `FoldScope`),
  and **Expand all** also switches saved manual folds of spaces and tab groups not currently drawn (`fold:space:*`, `fold:tree:*`) to expanded, so they stay open after changing the grouping or expanding an outer level.
  They act on the list under the controls only (#6447, `agentsFoldAction` in `src/lib/sidebar-api.ts`): Collapse all folds every group to its heading, and the grouping segments, quick filters and the title row's Filter stay; Expand all opens the groups again. With the block folded under its title (a click on **Agents**), Expand all opens it and every group in it. The chat-list view, and a list with no groups (a grouping still loading, nothing listed), have nothing to fold to, so the button is not shown there. A click always changes what is on screen; on hover or keyboard focus a tooltip under the button names the action (Collapse all / Expand all), with no second line.
  **Other agents** (Agents not in any space, such as Codex or DSH sessions) follow the space rule for their default: folded when there are more than 3 and none needs attention (seen, waiting), otherwise expanded.
  They are not always folded like **Idle Spaces**, because for people who do not use herdr every Agent is in this group, and always folding it would hide the working ones too. iOS has no such group; Agents outside spaces are grouped into one space per computer, which can also be folded.
  Machine telemetry pushes keep the sidebar's grouping inputs unchanged (#3059, `lib/sidebar-machines.ts`): load, memory and a refreshed last-seen timestamp do not rebuild the To-do tree. Computer names, hub labels, online status and first-connection state still update the rows; engine notices also use the latest computer name. The filter/grouping bars, account row and closed dialogs skip unchanged parent pushes. Usage meters and notices retain their own live subscriptions.
  **Paging hubs** (#6362, #6662): one grouping bar, **To-do / Machine / Repo / Project / Status** (待办 / 机器 / 仓库 / 项目 / 状态; the complete list's `GroupingBar` in both views, its title "Agents" too), whether the list below is paged or complete, so a pin or an unpin changes nothing above the list. The bounded, virtualized list draws every grouping but **By repo**, whose worktree level needs every session, and **By to-do** only on a hub with `sessions_todo` (`docs/protocol/protocol.md` "Sessions by to-do"); any session or workspace pin, or several assistants, select the complete list, as do By repo and, on an older hub, By to-do. Paging the sidebar also requires `sessions_agents_only` (#4676), so its pages, changes, counts and catalog exclude assistant and health-space conversations. On older hubs the complete Agents list applies the same sidebar filter. Outside the sidebar the Machines page, a computer's page and a space's page read the complete list too, to count and list a computer's Agents, which such a hub pushes none of (web audit item 3); with several assistants Overview does, for the current assistant's Agents. That list's first read is the heavy one (`summary=0`, 200 rows a page; the 8,356-row test fixture is about 7.6 MB), later reads ask only for what changed, and readers share one copy, released a second after the last leaves. A lighter per-computer count from the hub would spare those pages the first read; Overview with one assistant reads none and leaves a computer's count out while the paged list has more pages. The default is By to-do; a "By pinned" choice saved before #6662 reads as By to-do, an absent or unknown one too. The chips under the bar are the complete list's quick filters on both too (All / Needs you / Unread / Working / Waiting in the background / Lark group / Terminal and the botmux switch, one `persona.agentFilter`): the paged list selects them with `state`, `waiting`, `pane_source` and `exclude_pane_source` (`sessions_quick_filters`, `docs/protocol/protocol.md` "Quick filters") and counts them from one read of the list without the chip; a hub without that feature keeps its state chips (… / Seen / Not running).
  The grouping shortcut switches a mounted list at once; pin updates are reactive, and removing the last pin returns to paging under the same bar and grouping. Before #6662 the paged list had its own "Recently updated / Computer / Project / Space / Repo" control, and any saved grouping or pin swapped the whole block for the complete list's, By to-do included (the owner's report: unpinning the last conversation turned the to-dos into another set of tabs).
  A hidden tab still gets every `sessions_list` hint; the paged list's reads on them (each open section's rows, the groups' counts or catalog, a filtered list and its counts) wait while it is hidden, and one read each follows when it is shown again (`onShownHint`, `lib/shown-hints.ts`, #7167), as the open chat's row (`lib/runtime-session.ts`) already did. A shown tab follows every hint as before. The root lists still follow hints while hidden. On a hub with `sessions_agents_only`, Overview, the sidebar summary and the tab and Dock badges use the same scoped counts as the paged Agents list (`runtimeAgents`), even if the sidebar list is closed. Until scoped counts arrive they count the available Agent rows. Older hubs without the scoped feature keep their existing count source.
  The fallback keeps a complete copy of the collection, so pinned and grouped rows beyond the first page are included (`lib/complete-sessions.ts`, #3759): its first read takes complete pages (`GET /sessions?summary=0&limit=200`, following `next_cursor`), and each later read only `since` its revision (changed and removed rows). Complete pages are read again only after `409 revision_expired` (a hub restart), when the copy was released, or from a hub that answers the paging query with its whole legacy list. Before #3759 every hint read the whole list again (about 17 times a minute, hundreds of KB each). It refreshes on session invalidation/reconnect events, except a `sessions_list` hint whose `revision` the copy already holds,
  keeps the last complete result while loading and retries failed reads after five seconds. Consumers share a credential-scoped snapshot, request and cooldown; a one-second grace after the last unmount permits sidebar/Agents-page handoff, then releases everything. Reset or credential changes invalidate immediately. Other views keep their bounded transport.
  During the first baseline, an unfiltered, grouped sidebar on a paging hub can draw the first summary page it is already reading as neutral rows under the existing **Loading…** line, once the to-dos needed by the default grouping are available. This preview has no provisional group headings or counts, Pinned or Recent sections, or empty-filter result, and it never seeds quick-filter membership or saved active/idle workspace placement. The complete snapshot replaces it atomically with the existing tree and complete counts. Filtered and chat-list views, failures, and an older hub's pushed rows keep their previous loading behavior. `SidebarPaging.test.tsx` holds the last cursor page to check the transition; `web/e2e/sidebar-refresh-loading.mjs` checks it in Chrome with light and dark captures, including a failed complete read and its existing Retry path.
  Normal invalidations coalesce into one trailing read no sooner than three seconds after the previous request finishes; new hints do not postpone that deadline. Initial reads and reconnects bypass the throttle, and quiet failure retries retain their five-second delay. A delta that changes nothing leaves the published snapshot as it is.
  Local row edits remain visible during refresh; marking fallback-only rows as seen sends each requested identity even when the detail cache has never loaded it.
  Paged state chips keep the last successful counts during refresh, scope changes and transient failures; a successful zero count still takes effect.
  The paged list's controls use the same components as the complete list, with no native `<select>` / `<datalist>`. In the sidebar its grouping is the bar above (`PagedSessionList`'s `grouping` prop: the bar first, then the quick filters (`grouping.quick`, the complete list's `FilterBar`), then the search, as the complete list orders them, no value pill, and a search lists its matches flat); elsewhere (the Terminal page's session browser) "Recently updated / Machine / Repo / Project" is its own segmented control (personal agents: "Recently updated / Account"), named as the sidebar names the same things since #6662 (its Repo is the hub's catalog project, a repository across computers; its Project the space), the state chips match the quick filters (state mark + count), and picking a value is a pill that opens the design system's menu (radio rows in a fixed name order, a count at the row's end; a project shows its folder name with the full path under it, a Windows computer's path read by its own separator, `baseName` in `lib/format.ts`). The menu is as wide as its pill, so it follows the sidebar as it is dragged wider or narrower, and never narrower than a menu is elsewhere (`SESSION_LIST_METRICS.pickMenuMin`). On a hub without the catalog (below) Space adds a "computer" pill before it. Personal agents' provider filter is a `SearchField`.
  **Browse by draws the list in that structure** (#6348, `views/agents/GroupedSessions.tsx`, `lib/session-groups.ts`; the sidebar's By to-do and By status too, #6662: a section per open to-do with Agents, read with `todo=<id>`, every one open, in the To-dos page's order without live Agent rank (`sortTodos`), its needs-you counts updating in place and its rows without the to-do tag the heading already says, and **Not on a to-do** (`todo=none`) last, folded; a section per state in the quick filters' order, the first three open, no needs-you badge beside a state's own count): with Computer, Project or Space chosen and no value picked in the pill, the list is one folding section per group, computers in the hub's order and projects and spaces in a fixed name order (No folder / No space last), each heading with its count and, while any do, how many of its sessions need you (the Earlier header's badge). The first three sections start open (`SESSION_LIST_METRICS.groupsOpen`), and so does the one holding the open conversation; the rest are folded, and what someone folds or opens is kept in this browser (`fold:sessions-by:<list>:<dimension>:<group>`). In the sidebar the Agents title row is the complete list's (#6662): **Collapse all / Expand all** folds and opens these sections as it does the complete list's groups (each opened one reads its rows, the cost of asking for all), the **⋯** holds the archived Agents and **+** starts an Agent; before, the paged list had an archive icon of its own and no fold-all. The hub pages rows newest first for its cursors. In the sidebar `grouping.rowOrder` applies the stable computer → workspace → tab → pane order to the first loaded rows. The section retains loaded identities while their candidates remain and sorts the retained union by current structural placement. Full and paged reads admit every new transport identity; deltas admit `added` identities, distinguishing a newly created tab from an older unloaded row that merely became active, and previously presented identities re-entering a filter. An older hub that omits `added` keeps legacy admission of every new transport identity. Previous positions and activity timestamps do not participate. Real machine, workspace, tab and pane changes apply directly, and identical loaded identity sets reproduce their order after a reload. The flat list, including a search's filtered `SessionList` and the shared root, uses the same deterministic union (#11801). Other paged session browsers list their newest six sessions. **Load more** shows the rest of the page read so far and reads on, 50 at a time. It is a quiet line in the look of the sidebar's own "Show N more" (`ShowMoreRow` in `views/SidebarSection.tsx`), never a button pill (#6662, the owner's report), as are the flat list's **Load more** and the more groups' line. It reads only rows (`SessionList` with `counts: false`) and stops when it is folded, so a list of sixty projects costs one read for the groups until someone opens one. "Expand all" does not open these sections for the same reason. The sections reuse the sidebar's own heading (`views/SidebarSection.tsx`: `Section`, `SidebarGroup`, `GroupCount`, passed on by `SidebarParts`). Their code is a chunk of its own (`lazyPage`), loaded when a Browse by is chosen or was the last time, and the groups are read while it loads: the first screen, whose default is the flat list, carries the read and the pill only (`FIRST_SCREEN_BUDGET`). Picking a value in the pill lists that one group as the flat, virtualized list, as before; Recently updated is the one flat list. The chosen Browse by is kept in this browser (`persona.agentBrowseBy`, `persona.personalBrowseBy`). Personal agents by Account (#16248, `views/agents/account-groups.tsx`): the hub groups them by account id, so each heading and each choice of the account pill names the account as `GET /api/v1/agents` lists it (`displayName`, else its provider's label; an account it does not list is named after its loaded sessions' provider, and only one known nowhere by its id, `accountGroup` in `lib/agents.ts`), after its provider's mark: the bundled agent mark of the product it drives (Grok Bot → Grok, Dots → the OpenAI Blossom, Claude Duet → Claude, Gemini tasks → Gemini), else `AgentMark`'s letter tile. The id is the name's tooltip. No mark is loaded from another host. `node web/e2e/personal-account-groups.mjs <web URL> <artifact directory>` checks it against the mock hub (`MOCK_SESSIONS_LIST=1`) in light and dark, with screenshots of the Agents page, the sidebar and the account menu. A row under a heading leaves out what the heading says (its computer, its space, its project's folder), and under a project that is on several computers it says which one before its title, as a tab's name comes before its agent's. **Active within** applies to the flat list only and is not offered while the list is drawn by group.
  The groups' numbers follow the search and the state chip, so a heading's count is the number of rows its section lists; narrowed to a state, the needs-you badge is not drawn (the count is of that state). Computers (and every group on a hub without the catalog) come from the counts the list already reads when no state narrows them, else from one more counts read; their badge is one more read with `state=needs_you`, made only while the scope has such sessions. The catalog names projects and spaces and counts their waiting sessions in one read. These reads are made at most once per 1.5 s however many hints arrive (`SESSION_LIST_METRICS.groupsRefresh`). An open section reads only for a hint that can concern it (#9176): one whose `changed` names a row it holds, one it cannot follow (no `since`/`changed`, a gap, a read out, pages not read yet), or a change of its heading's count or needs-you number, which is how a session joining it shows; the others it passes over, still reading `since` its last answer. Before, each open section read on every hint: seven open to-dos made about seven reads a second while agents worked. A section also holds a hint that lands while its read is out to its 2 s window's end, so it reads at most once a window (`lib/section-list.ts` `SectionList`; the flat list's `SessionList.invalidate` reads once right after a read that was out, #9042). The list's own scoped counts reads (its facets when no list page carries them, and the scope's counts behind the chips) follow hints through one reader per path for the whole page (`followHinted`, `lib/hinted-read.ts`, #15910): the first hint after a quiet stretch reads at once, the rest of a burst share one read per 2 s window with one more after the last hint, and every list following that path gets each answer. Before, each read on every hint: the sidebar's grouped list, which leaves hidden botmux sessions out, made one `counts=1` read per hint in every tab.
  **Projects and spaces from the hub's catalog** (`sessions_catalog`, `docs/protocol/protocol.md` "Projects and spaces"): when the hub advertises it, Project and Space read `GET /sessions?catalog=1` with the search and the state. A repository checked out on several computers, or in several directories, is one project: its section, and its row in the pill's menu, list its remote and each directory with its computer (`MacBook · ~/code/app`, the count beside it when there are several), and its sessions are read with one `place` filter of all its directories, newest first across computers. A directory with no remote goes by its folder's name, a Windows path by its own separator, so `Notes` on two computers is one project too. A space is one computer's and is named by its `space_name`. **By project on several computers** (#13522, as iOS's By Project): when the list has sessions on more than one computer (the whole list's computers decide it, so a chip or a search that leaves one computer's sessions changes no level), each computer is a section of its own (`ComputerGroup` in `views/agents/GroupedSessions.tsx`, `computerSections` in `lib/session-groups.ts`), in the hub's computer order. Its heading is the complete list's By machine heading in the paged list's terms: a green dot (online) or a grey one, the computer's name as the rest of the app gives it (`machineWithHub`), **Offline** or **Not connected yet** beside a computer that is away (said to a screen reader in the fold button's name), then how many of its sessions need you and how many it holds, the sums of its spaces' numbers (less the in-flight starts its open spaces leave out). It starts folded while the computer is away, and opens by itself for the open conversation; its fold is kept (`fold:sessions-by:<list>:group:computer:<id>`) and follows Collapse all / Expand all. Inside it, a level in (`sidebar-indent`), its spaces in the same fixed name order, the first three open, then its sessions in no space (**No project**, the computer's empty-id place) last; with one computer the spaces are the list's sections, as before. A space's heading no longer names its computer, and an Agent row under a space of the catalog's no longer repeats it. Two of one computer's spaces whose names are the same (ignoring case) each add their parent folder after the name, in the heading's lighter weight (`app · ~/Desktop`, `app · ~/code`), from the folder the hub says the space's rows are in (the catalog's `path`); without it (an older hub) nothing is added. **A space's +** (#13523, as desktop coding-agent apps put one on each project folder): a space's heading has a **+** (`SectionAdd`, spoken and titled **New agent in <name>**, with the parent folder where the heading shows one) that opens the one **New agent** sheet (`openNewAgent({ machineId, cwd })`, as the space menu's New agent, a space's page and a board card's do) on the space's computer and in its folder, with the launcher the sheet picks for that computer (Model settings' New agent when set, else the last one started there); with a fine pointer the caret is in the first message, and **Start** (⌘↵) opens the new conversation as from the title row's **+**. Starting with no first message is the sheet's own rule: allowed, except for a Codex that cannot open a conversation without one (on a node without `prompt_optional`, or the Codex App), where Start waits for it. It shows under the pointer and on keyboard focus, and always on a touch screen, as the complete list's space ⋯ does; while it shows, the heading's numbers step aside for it rather than being covered (on a touch screen they keep its room). There is none on **No project** (no folder), on the spaces of a computer that is away, on a personal Agent's account, or where the hub does not say a space's folder. The sessions in no directory (**No folder**) are one last section, read by the catalog's empty-path places. While the hub is still asking computers what their directories hold (`pending`), the catalog is read again after a second, then half as long again each time up to ten seconds, until it is settled. Without the catalog (an older hub, personal agents) the groups are the count maps' keys: a project is a path, a space an id.
  **Active within** (#4236, `lib/session-activity.ts`): beside the session count, a menu keeps the sessions active in the past 24 hours, 7 days or 30 days in view; the default, **Any time**, folds nothing. With a window chosen, the rows last active before it (by `updated_at`, independently of transport and presentation order) go into one **Earlier** group at the end, folded by default (`fold:sessions-earlier`, the fold remembered in this browser; it opens by itself while one of its sessions is open). Its header counts the sessions before the window (the list's `total` minus the recent rows) and how many of them need you (the scope's `state.needs_you` count minus the recent ones, the Needs you chip's rule), so a folded group never hides waiting work. Nothing leaves the list: filters, counts and the total stay the hub's, and only while Earlier is folded does the list stop reading further pages. The window is kept in this browser (`persona.agentActiveWindow`) and moves with the clock. The runtime list passes it; personal agents do not yet.
  **Side sessions live in their parent's chat** (#7944, the owner's request of 2026-11-15; `lib/side-fold.ts`): while hello lists `sessions_side_fold`, a Claude desktop app's side chat, /btw question or spawned session (`parent_agent_id`) is folded by the hub under its topmost listed parent (`folded_under`, `folded_as: "side"`; a side of a side under the same row) and is no row or count of its own anywhere: it goes through `foldRows` like any folded child ("Child sessions fold into their parent" below), and the paged list's `roots=1` leaves it out. The parent's row shows its folded state, which an unread side also makes unread (sides only), unless the parent works itself. A list that holds the side rows (the complete list, or a parent whose chat is open) takes the side part of that state from them (`countSides`, `useHeldSides`), so a side seen here stops being unread at once; `lib/side-fold.fixture.test.ts` runs the shared cases in `spec/fixtures/side-fold/cases.json` through that path; a paged row whose sides no chat holds takes the hub's `children.sides`, `sides_working`, `sides_needs_you` and `sides_unread`. **Which side keeps it Unread** (#13496, after #13299: opening the parent never cleared a dot that was its side's): while a parent row shows Unread because of a side, its second line names the most recent unread side, in the unread tint: the `sideSessions` mark, the side's title and "+N" for the others, with the lead "New side reply:" (zh-Hans 分支新回复：, ja 子セッションに新着：) before the title only where the line has room for both (a container query, about a 400 px sidebar; the title keeps the room in the default width). The tooltip and the spoken name say the whole sentence ("Side session “…” has a new reply", zh-Hans 分支会话「…」有新回复) and the others' titles. `scripts/test/web_side_unread_e2e.py` (mock `MOCK_SIDE_SESSIONS=1 MOCK_SIDE_UNREAD=1`) checks it on a complete and a paged list. When the parent's own reply was seen the line replaces the parent's own words; when both are unread both lines show. One click or Enter on it opens that side in the parent's Side sessions panel (the side's link, `askSide`), where it is seen as any chat is, and the row's dot goes in the same update. A click elsewhere on the row opens the parent, as before; rows with no unread side are unchanged. To name the side, the row reads the parent's folded rows (`HoldSides` → `useChildSessions`) while the hub's rollup or the held rows count one unread, and keeps reading until the hub's rollup drops, so the hub's older count never shows for a frame; before they are read it says only how many ("2 side sessions have new replies"). The parent's own seen mark clears only its own part, and the Unread counts (chips, the rail) take a parent out of Unread once its held sides are seen (`heldCounts`' `sidesOf`). A side whose parent is not listed (archived, another filter) stays a row. They are reached from the parent's chat (chat page, "Side sessions").
  Without the feature (an older hub) a row that names a loaded row in `parent_agent_id` is drawn right under it as before (#5935, `lib/side-sessions.ts`): a level in with a line down its side (`SESSION_LIST_STYLE.nestedRow`), always open, a side of a side under the topmost loaded one. A stable presentation sorts both the parent groups and the side rows without separating them; otherwise each group sits where its most recently active member was. **Active within** still takes the group's newest member's time. Only the order of the loaded rows changes there, and every count stays the hub's. `node web/e2e/side-sessions.mjs` checks that arrangement against the fake hub's `MOCK_SIDE_SESSIONS=1 MOCK_SIDE_FOLD=0` and takes the screenshots in `docs/web/screenshots/side-sessions/`.
  Every agent row in the sidebar ends with when its session was last active (`ago(updated_at)` in the narrow style, "16m ago" in English; the work-item row in `docs/design/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md` 3.4), after its hint, which gives way first; a row that also carries its marks (where it was opened, its to-do) leaves the hint to its tooltip, where at the row's end it would only squeeze the title. A row whose details line already shows the age does not show it twice, and a tab's row, whose end holds "N agents", shows it as before (offline or stateless, with nothing else at its end).
  Screenshot fixture: `MOCK_SESSIONS_LIST=1 MOCK_AGENT_ARCHIVES=1` enables paging and the archived-Agents menu in `scripts/mock/mock_hub.py`; seed pins through its existing `/api/v1/pins` endpoint. `MOCK_SESSIONS_CATALOG=1` adds the catalog, the `place` and `space` filters, a Windows PC, one repository checked out on two computers and a notes folder that is no repository on two; `MOCK_MANAGERS=1` keeps one assistant, since with several the sidebar reads the complete list. `MOCK_PAGE_COUNTS=1` sends a page's counts with it (`sessions_page_counts`), as current hubs do; `/mock/bump?what=last` every few hundred milliseconds stands in for a fleet at work, whose hints keep every list reading on its two-second window. `node web/e2e/agents-paged-groupings.mjs <web URL> <artifact directory>` checks the sidebar's groupings over both views and saves light and dark screenshots (`web/e2e/README.md`). Captures of that fixture, all synthetic: [by computer](screenshots/agents-browse-by/light-computer.png), by project in [light](screenshots/agents-browse-by/light-project.png) and [dark](screenshots/agents-browse-by/dark-project.png), [the project menu](screenshots/agents-browse-by/light-project-menu.png), [by space](screenshots/agents-browse-by/dark-space.png), [a 240 px sidebar](screenshots/agents-browse-by/narrow-light-project.png) and [a phone](screenshots/agents-browse-by/phone-dark-project.png).
  **Child sessions fold into their parent** (#5120; the owner asked that this follow cindy, where a child Agent is never a task of its own and a worker's state shows on its lead's row): an Agent another Agent started (a Codex subagent, an Agent a Paseo Agent created) is never a row, a dock entry or a count of its own, in any grouping, filter, Pinned, Recent, Home, the Machines page, a space's or a computer's page, the chat header's same-space menu, Forward's list or the tab badge. The hub's manager says which listed session a child folds under (`folded_under`) and gives that session `children` (how many, how many working, how many need the user, by their own state; `docs/protocol/protocol.md` "Session hierarchy"); the lists go through `foldRows` (`lib/folded-rows.ts`, with `foldedState` in `lib/child-sessions.ts`), and a paging hub that advertises `sessions_hierarchy` is asked for `roots=1`, so its pages and counts already leave the children out and count each parent by its folded state.
  The parent's row shows its **folded state**, the most urgent of its own and its children's: one child waiting on the user makes it need you, one working makes it work (unless its own reply waits to be read or answered). Needing you because of a child, its second line says what that child waits for, and its pending count holds the child's cards. While children run, a line says **Subagents running: N** (N is the larger of the subagents the session reports itself and its working children, so a Paseo lead that also lists them as background agents counts them once). Clicking the row opens the parent. A child whose parent the list does not hold (archived, another computer, another filter) stays a row of its own. A child's card belongs to its parent everywhere: it is grouped and counted under the parent (the main chat's Needs you and In progress, the Inbox, notifications, the switcher) and its link opens the parent's page, where it is answered (chat page, "Subagents").
  Session list reads: `node web/e2e/session-list-reads.mjs <web URL> --hub <mock URL>` counts the page's `GET /sessions` by kind during a quiet minute and a minute of hints (`docs/operations/testing.md`, "Session list reads").
  The grouping bar described below is both views' (see "Paging hubs" above); the trees under it are the complete list's.
  Below the Agents title and above the quick filters is a row of segments "To-do / Machine / Repo / Project / Status" (the full name, "By to-do"…, is each segment's accessible name and hover hint, #2812; it used to be the "By machine ⌄" dropdown right of the title); one click switches, and ⌘E / Ctrl+E cycles in the same order. Browsers that never picked one default to by to-do (#2812, by machine before, #1963); by to-do shows "Loading…" until the first to-do list arrives, instead of drawing every Agent under "Not on a to-do" first and moving them afterwards. When that read fails and no to-dos are known (a 500, say), By to-do has nothing to group by: the list shows By status for now, with a line under the filters saying the to-dos could not be read, why, and **Retry** (`TodosUnread` in `views/Sidebar.tsx`); the stored choice stays By to-do and comes back once a read answers, and tapping the To-do segment meanwhile reads them again, as Retry does. The **Chat list** (the Filter menu's) is on no grouping and needs no to-dos: its rows are drawn at once, with no "Loading…" before the first to-do list and no word about a failed read. Before, the complete list put every Agent under "Not on a to-do" and the paged list named every section "To-do", with no word of the failure. The list never stays on "Loading…" or blank for a read that failed or a hub out of reach: on a page that has not reached the hub since it opened (the page's **Offline**, `lib/shell.ts` `unreachable`, one flag the page and the list both read, `useHubUnreachable` in `lib/store.ts`, so a list drawn while the socket tries again agrees with the page) the list says the hub can't be reached instead of "Loading…"; a failed read of the complete list (`useFullAgentSessions`'s `error`, read again by itself every 5 s) says it could not read the Agents list, why, and **Retry** (`retryFullAgentSessions`), where it used to draw nothing; and the paged list drawn by group shows its first read's failure with **Retry** where its sections stayed on "Loading…". Both lists say a failed read in the same words, that the Agents list could not be read and why (`ListError`, `ui/ListError.tsx`; the paged list's `failureText`), whichever one the hub's features choose. A list that had loaded keeps its rows when a later read fails. Once picked (#1836) it is remembered for next time; a hub without to-dos shows no "To-do" segment, and a by-to-do choice shows by machine for now. The choice and each group's fold state are saved in the current browser.
  The segments choose the grouping; the **⋯** on the right of the title row (**Agent list options**; before #2812 it shared the "By machine ⌄" dropdown with the groupings) holds the archived Agents where the hub has them, and is not shown otherwise. The way back to the paged list it once held went with #6662, as the bar now picks the view. **Ordering is stable, not an activity choice** (#11801): computers keep the hub's order, pinned workspaces lead and the others keep herdr's `space_index`, tabs keep `slot_index`, and panes keep their layout order. `machineSessionOrder` gives the paged list, the complete list and every grouping the same row placement without changing transport pagination. Status still chooses a row's section and the To-dos page's order still places to-do groups; their pending counts, state dots and times update in place. By project keeps a workspace that was above Idle in place when its latest activity becomes quiet. With stored membership, ordinary working alone does not move an Idle workspace, while needs-you, unread, replies, Just finished, background waits and opening a row bring it above Idle. This membership survives a reload in the same browser tab; a new tab with no stored membership derives the current busy layout, distinct from a stored all-Idle set. **Opt-in activity order** (#13727, `lib/agent-sort.ts`, `lib/sidebar-engaged.ts`): Settings › Agents has **Sort Agents by recent activity**, the hub-synced `sort_by_activity` of `GET`/`PUT /api/v1/agents/display-settings` (off by default; `agents.sort_by_activity` in `manager.json` sets the value until someone saves their own; a hub without the field hides the switch and keeps the stable order). The old per-browser `persona.agentSort` key is ignored and never written. On, the complete list orders rows by time only (a working agent by `state_since`, the others by `updated_at`, ties by id) and its sections (computers, projects, repositories, tabs; the To-dos page's order still places to-dos) by their latest agent; the paged list leaves the transport's newest-first rows as they are and orders its computer and space sections by the newest session on the root's first page. By status keeps its own order either way. The order is **held still while the pointer is over the sidebar or keyboard focus (`:focus-visible`) is in it**: state dots, counts and times update in place, and the list reorders once both have left (`useActivityDates` freezes the times the complete list orders by; `useHeldOrder` keeps the paged list's rows and sections in the order they were drawn in, a new row first).

  **The Filter is a Settings switch** (#13727): **Show the Filter on the Agents list** is the hub-synced `show_filter` (off by default; `agents.show_filter` in `manager.json` sets the initial value). Off, neither list draws the Filter button or its chips, any filter set before is cleared, ⌘K offers no "Filter Agents list", and the Chat list view is not used; the quick-filter chips (All, Needs you, Working, Terminal…) are unaffected. On, both lists draw the same button and chips with every option (search scope, Pinned, harness, project, model, computer, Chat list view, Search as Code, Reset). On the **paged** list the hub can express the words (`q`) and **one computer** (`machine_id`); any other choice (a harness, project or model, Pinned, a search scope, a time window, Search as Code, several computers, the Chat list view) has no paged filter parameter, so while it is on the **complete list** draws the sidebar, which applies every one, and the paged list returns when it is cleared. The paged Filter's options come from the loaded sessions (the hub counts no harnesses, projects or models), except the computers, whose counts are the hub's (`counts=1`).
  **Search and Filter** (#6589, after #4397 / #4439): the list has no search field of its own; the sidebar's **Search chats** (⌘K, the rail's icon, and on the phone's Agents page a search button beside +) is its search. ⌘K matches Agents with the list's matcher (`src/lib/agent-search.ts`, loaded with the opened palette alongside saved-query tools): the operators `machine:` / `host:`, `project:` / `repo:` / `cwd:`, `harness:` / `agent:`, `model:`, `state:`, `is:pinned`, `is:error`, `is:<state>`, `since:24h|7d|30d` (any of them keeps the results to Agent sessions), and plain words never become filters (#4397). Results are ordered by what matched: the session's name (starting with what was typed, then containing it), then its project or computer (with its space, tab and folder), then anything the list's Full text reads (its last line, what was asked, the branch, the model, an error), which shows the line that matched as the row's second line, the match marked; newest first among equals. **Filter Agents list** under the results (⇧↵) puts the query on the list in place (`src/lib/agent-list-filters.ts`): the list keeps its grouping, shows the matches, opens if it was folded under its title, and, where the sidebar is not on screen (a narrow screen, the rail), the Agents page opens. It is offered while the query finds an Agent; the hub's paged list (`sessions_list`) has no field either and takes the query's words as the hub's text search (`q`), with the same **Search: …** chip, so there a query with an operator is not offered (the hub reads no operators). **⌘K's Filter** (filter icon at the end of the field, `src/views/palette/AgentConditions.tsx`) holds the list's filter choices: Machine / Project / Status / Harness / Model (a page each, once it has two values), Pinned, Updated within (24 hours, 7 days, 30 days), Reset. A choice is written into the query as its operator (`machine:<id>`, `is:pinned`, `since:7d`…; one window at a time, a value with a space has no spelling and is not offered), choosing it again takes it out, the button shows how many operators the query has, and Reset takes them all out and leaves the words. The **Filter** button (filter icon) is on the title row between fold all and ⋯, tinted with the number of filters on (the applied query counts as one); its menu is #4439's: Search in, Pinned, Harness / Project / Model / Machine (a section once it has two values; Harness is the agent each row runs, each of Paseo's providers one of its own under its label, never one `paseo`, #8142), Chat list, Search as Code, Reset. While something filters, one row of chips sits above the list: the query (**Search: …**, its text reopens ⌘K with it), the scope, Pinned, each facet value and `since:`, each with ×, then Reset, which clears them all, the query too; Search as Code's plan bar follows it while on. Why the title row and not the quick-filter row: that row holds state values and already wraps at the sidebar's 240 px; the title row holds the list's other menu buttons and stays when the block is folded.
  - **By machine** (following herdr's layout, `src/lib/herdr-tree.ts`): machine → Workspace (herdr's order, `space_index`) → Tab (`slot_index`). A session is an Agent pane; a lead's workers (the other Agents of a tab whose first pane is an Agent) are not listed, they are in the lead's Team panel (see "Team" below); plain shell panes are not listed.
    Machine rows have an online dot and the needs-you count, and offline machines fold by default. Workspace rows have a status dot and an Agent count (counting Agents like the machine row and quick filters; hover shows how many tabs), and ⋯ reuses the space menu. Tab rows show `#N` or the name, the title of the most urgent pane, and "N agents". Each level's status dot is the most urgent below it (needs you > working > done, not seen > seen).
    When a tab has several Agents (#2320, `docs/protocol/agent-states.md` "Several panes in one tab"), "N agents ›" at the row end expands into one row per Agent (with a status dot, Agent name and its own ⋯),
    ordered by pane position (`pane_index`; when missing, by the order herdr opened the panes, since pane ids are base-36 counters): the lead is on top, marked **Lead**, and panes it split off are indented beneath it on a thin line;
    when the top-left is a shell, the Agents are peers and unmarked. Expanded by default (so you can see at a glance which Agents belong together); clicking "N agents" folds it into one row. The fold state is kept in this browser keyed by `machine/space name/tab number` (no tab name: two tabs with the same name are tracked separately, a renamed tab (the hub renames `#2` to the task title) is still recognized, and numbers survive a herdr restart; hosts without numbers use the tab's id). Long tab names are truncated (to at most half the width) and never overlap "N agents".
    When folded, what is open is one of the Agents inside, and the tab row is highlighted (the sliding highlight and "scroll to the open row" land on it); only when expanded is it that Agent's own row: folded child rows are still in the fold container but do not register a position.
    Clicking a Tab goes to `/t/<machine>/<space>/<tab>`, selecting the most urgent pane by default; if the id changed after a herdr restart and it cannot open, it falls back to the session in the link; old `/s/` links open as usual. Hosts without a tab level (Paseo, botmux, runtime) list sessions directly under the space, and those not in a space go to **Other** under the machine.
    Folding and pinning are keyed by `machine/space name` (workspace ids change after a herdr restart).
    Spaces with `parent_space_id` (Orca child workspaces, #2073) hang under the parent space like in Orca's sidebar: after the parent's tabs there is an extra "N children" row, folded by default (`<machine/space name>/children`), with status dots for children needing attention when folded;
    the parent space's row sums the children's states (counts of needs you / working / done), and its own status dot and folded status dots include the children. When the parent has no running Agent (not in the list) or parent and child form a cycle, child spaces stay at the top level.
  - **By repo** (following Orca's "Projects" sidebar): the bar's **Repo** takes the complete list on a paging hub too (its worktree level needs every session, #6662); choosing it is remembered. `src/lib/agent-repos.ts` loads on demand when **By repo** is shown (shared `repoOf` / `showsWorktreeLevel` stay in `src/lib/agent-repos-core.ts`), keeping the cold first screen under `FIRST_SCREEN_BUDGET`. `src/lib/workspace-catalog.ts` reads `/workspaces` independently of the board setting. The catalog is partitioned by credential generation and explicit default manager; stale reads cannot replace a new partition. A visible page re-reads it every 60 s (`CATALOG_POLL_MS`, as Apple, #4685 / #5168): each read asks every online computer live, worktrees change rarely, and creating, renaming or removing one here refreshes it at once (`refreshWorkspaceCatalog`), as does coming back into view. Hidden pages stop polling, unchanged reads share their objects, and failed discovery retains the last successful inventory.
    By default (`showEmptyWorkspaces` off, persisted locally in `persona.showEmptyWorkspaces`, aligned with Android and Apple), catalog-backed rows keep workspaces with Agents, host-pinned workspaces (`pinned_at`, including across temporary disconnects or unavailability, per `DESIGN_SYSTEM.md` 3.4) and ancestors of non-empty children, hiding unpinned zero-session directories. **Show empty workspaces** in the Agents list `⋯` menu under By repo reveals live available empty workspaces while still excluding unpinned zero-session rows that are unavailable (`available === false`) or offline (`online === false` or an offline computer), and always excluding zero-session rows flagged by `hidden_agent_dirs` (`hidden_by_directory`). Project ownership and parent placement are independent: a same-machine, same-host child may appear beneath a parent from another project while keeping its own project metadata. Missing parents and cycles remain visible at the top level. Exact runtime workspace IDs and host bindings determine Agent placement; only unbound Agents may use an unambiguous deepest directory match, and only inside the Agent's Git working tree when the node reports one (`worktree`, else `repo_root`): a workspace above it, such as the home folder or a folder of repositories, never collects it. "Above" is counted in folders from the node-verified physical cwd (`workspace_cwd`), so it holds when a symlinked folder leads to the cwd. A workspace whose host names no project (herdr) belongs to the repository its Agents agree on, else to the one its own folder is, and shares that repository's section with other hosts' places and the session-only rows there, each place keeping its own row. Compatibility `session-directory` rows never authorize host actions. Worktree and project totals count real Agents once; pinned Agents remain direct title-navigation candidates without duplicate rows or counts. Active filters hide unrelated empty workspaces (including host-pinned empties) while retaining matching descendants' ancestors. A place in a folder of trees kept apart from its repository (`~/.herdr/worktrees/<repository>/<tree>`, `~/.worktrees/<repository>/<tree>`) that Git does not place names its repository only by that folder. This happens when its tree was removed after its work merged, or has not been read yet. Such a place joins the repository Git placed another tree of that folder in, else the one other section of that name on its computer. It keeps a section of its own only when Git placed the folder's trees in two repositories or two sections share the name (#13453). Only such a folder at the computer's home counts: a cwd in a folder of a tree a repository keeps itself (`/code/app/.worktrees/feature/src`, Claude Code's `.claude/worktrees/`) has the same shape, but names a tree, not a repository, so it never joins by name; without the computer's home nothing joins.
    A worktree disclosure folds its contents (empty leaf workspaces start folded and automatically expand if a new Agent arrives unless explicitly folded by the user); its title opens the first direct Agent, including a pinned one, or selects an empty workspace. Selecting a workspace from another navigation surface reveals its ancestors without opening its own contents. Selection and fold identity survive rename and never carry into another credential or manager. The **N children** chip separately folds descendants; its status counts summarize direct child subtrees with Agents. Main checkouts keep their home marker and sort first.
    When discovery is unsupported, the existing session-only projection remains available. Host-reported `worktree`, `repo_root` and `branch` determine Git placement. A tree is labelled with its branch, else its folder (the main checkout: the repository's). A linked tree whose folder carries the repository's name goes by the folder holding it instead, as in the Codex app's `~/.codex/worktrees/<name>/<repository>` (#12800). When the host place names its sessions carry (`slot_name` without a `slot_id`: a Paseo workspace's title) agree on one, a linked tree takes that name instead, with the branch kept in its tooltip and its key still its path (#4497). The main checkout and Orca's trees keep their names. Trees are ordered by the name they show, then by their key (two workspaces can have one title). Older Orca sessions teach exact `<project id>::<worktree path>` identities and same-project parent edges; other sources may join known paths on complete directory segments, except below `.worktrees/`, `.claude/worktrees/` and `.herdr/worktrees/`. Without verified placement, the existing path inference supplies repo/worktree grouping. This fallback cannot recover empty catalog entries or cross-project parent relationships.
    A repository's name is said once, on its heading (#13454). Agent rows under it carry no `<repository> › <tree>` hint: the headings above them say both (DESIGN_SYSTEM 3.4). A host's lone workspace named after its folder, which is the repository's (herdr names workspaces so), adds no row of its own: its Agents are listed under the heading, which carries the workspace's pin and unavailable marks, its ⋯ and its right-click menu, as **By project**'s space headings do. The workspace keeps its row while it has children, a branch, a name of its own or no Agents to list, the rule the session-only projection applies to a lone main checkout (`showsWorktreeLevel`). Multi-root desktop projects (`codex_app`, `claude_desktop`) whose roots repeat the project's name label colliding roots by their folder name (adding parent directories on basename collisions), while terminal/engine hosts (`orca`, `paseo`) keep their native workspace titles. A host that names no project and does not say which workspace is a repository's main checkout (herdr reports no `is_main`) has it found by its folder: the workspace at the repository's own folder wears the home marker and sorts first, while desktop project folders with `project_id` or `project_path` never infer a main checkout from folder order (#14497). That mark is the tree's only; workspace actions keep reading what the host said.
  - **By project** keeps the original herdr order (machine → workspace → tab); quiet spaces go into **Idle Spaces**. Spaces with a loop, background work or running subagents are never folded away.
  - **By status** matches iOS `AgentListOrder`: needs you → done, not seen → awaiting your reply → working → waiting in the background → just finished → waiting to wake → muted → seen; only non-empty groups are shown, and seen is folded by default.
    **Just finished** (#9751, `justFinished` in `lib/agent-groups.ts`): a turn the hub's triage found done before anybody looked, for three hours (`work.just_finished`, `../protocol/agent-states.md` "Just finished"); it is not quiet, so its space stays out of **Idle Spaces** and the idle folds; its row draws a plain unread-green dot, says "Just finished" and keeps the ✓ conclusion line; opening it or Mark all as seen takes it out at once (`lib/seen-outbox.ts`). The paged list by status draws the same section on a hub with `sessions_just_finished` (`state=idle&just_finished=1`, open by default, Seen's number without it, `lib/session-groups.ts`); in the other paged groupings its row keeps its stable herdr place, with the same mark.
    Mutes come from the hub's `/mutes`; needs-you items are not demoted by muting, and ordinary seen items still go under seen. Agents with notifications turned on individually inside a project do not count as muted.
    Within a group, items use the same stable computer → workspace → tab → pane order (#11801), or by time when the opt-in activity order is on (#13727). State chooses the section; it does not move a row within that section.
    Rows in status groups add project context, and the machine name when there are several machines.
  - **By to-do** (#6458): the top level is the open to-dos with Agents attached, each a row with its chevron, its to-do mark, its title (a click opens the to-do), its Agents' count and its state in the To-dos page's word (`todoLook` in `src/lib/todo-wait-reason.ts`: what a waiting one waits on, Follow up, Finished unseen… never Done for a to-do that is not), its Agents under it; then **Not on a to-do** (formerly **Unassigned**) and **Recent (not running)** as rows of the same kind, each with its own mark (layers, history), an ⓘ beside Not on a to-do's title (Recent (not running)'s name says what it holds, so it has none, #6447), its count and the most urgent of its Agents' states (Needs you > Working > Waiting in the background > Done; none when empty). Where that is Done the group says what its rows say instead (`agentGroupLabel` in `lib/todo-tree.ts`): **Unread** while one of its Agents finished and was not looked at yet, as By status and the quick filter call it, and **Not running** when every Agent in it stopped (Recent (not running)); before, both read Done over Agents the rest of the list called Unread or Not running. Every one of these rows is a sticky group heading (Collapse all reads them). There are no repository or folder rows anywhere in this grouping: those belong to **By repository** and **By project** (the old project › to-do › Agent tree, #2526, is gone; the Agents of a group are listed directly under it). Since #6591 **Not on a to-do** also holds the Agents opened by hand in a terminal, which had a group of their own before (**Opened in the terminal**, formerly **Started Manually**): both are on no to-do and filed the same way, and each such row still ends with the Terminal source mark, as everywhere. Both groups start folded, through `useFolded`, except one holding an Agent that needs the user (or the open one), and **Not on a to-do** with no to-do above it (it is the whole list). What a group holds and how to file its Agents (right-click a row, or its ⋯, › Link to to-do…) is behind its ⓘ (`ui/InfoTip.tsx`: the pointer resting on it, keyboard focus or a click), and is what an open, empty group says in its place; Not on a to-do stays listed while empty unless a quick filter or a search narrows the list or the list has no Agent at all; Recent (not running) is listed only with something in it, as under the other groupings. The rows that fold groups select no text: a press-and-drag over them used to leave the theme's grey `::selection` behind each line, which read as a stuck highlight (#6458). When the list has two or more kinds of host (herdr, botmux, Orca…), rows not in herdr carry a small host tag (`botmux`, inferred from the `pane_id` prefix); with only one kind it is hidden. Rules for pinning and muting match **By status**. Under other groupings, rows attached to a to-do show a to-do icon tag.
  - **Recent (not running)** is kept under all three groupings: offline sessions, or sessions whose machine is offline / no longer in the machine list, go only here and are not repeated in the live groups; the assistant is not mixed into Agents.
    Expanding shows 8 at first and can go up to the 40 most recent. Folded content leaves keyboard focus and the accessibility tree.
  - **Background commands that look stuck** (#13744, `Session.background_stalled_since`, `backgroundStall` in `src/lib/background-work.ts`): a Working Agent whose background commands the node found stalled (no CPU and no output for ten minutes under a build / tests / download, less for others) while a subagent, workflow or Monitor still runs stays Working; once stalled background commands are all that is left the Agent is no longer Working and the line is not drawn (#16418); its sidebar row and list row get a muted clock line "后台命令 3 小时没有动静", the session header a chip beside the title (wide screens), and the running bar's "Background task" line the same words at its end. The tooltip says it still counts as Working. Mock: `MOCK_BG_STALLED=1`.
  - **Waiting in the background** (#6045, `Session.background_waiting`, `backgroundWaiting` in `src/lib/format.ts`): an Agent whose turn is over and whose background commands only wait (a check loop, `gh … --watch`; the node decides, `docs/protocol/agent-states.md`) is not Working. Its mark is a clock (the one the running bar says it with) in the faded `--status-waiting`, its header pill says "Waiting in the background", it has its own quick filter and its own group "By status" (after Working), the to-do tree ranks it between Working and Done, the folded tallies count it apart, Overview counts and lists it apart (its own section after Working, #10938), and the chat draws its turn finished with a still bar: "Waiting in the background · <what it waits on>", timed from when it began waiting. `state` stays `working`, so where nothing reads the field it shows as Working.
  - **Quick filters** (#433, iOS `QuickFilterBar`, `src/lib/agent-filter.ts`): pills "All / Needs you / Unread / Working / Waiting in the background" with counts under the Agents title, below the grouping segments, showing only states that have Agents; they combine with all three groupings and are saved in the current browser. The "botmux" chip cycles through decoded (default), raw, and hidden. The transcript format is saved in this browser. The chip and **Show botmux sessions in Agents** in Web Settings › Agents share the Hub visibility setting across browsers. Decoded messages and replies can be opened to their original content (see [BotMux messages](../protocol/protocol.md#botmux-messages)). When there are no visible botmux sessions, the **Lark group** filter is hidden and uses **All** until that filter is available again. The per-computer inventory switch (**botmux · On / Off** under machine Configuration, **Also show botmux sessions**) remains independent.
    Counts match iOS (muted unread / working items do not count, muted needs-you items do). Matches are recorded when a filter is selected, so opening an unread item and turning it seen does not make it jump out of the filter; clicking the pill again recomputes. With a filter on, **Recent** is hidden and idle spaces do not fold.
  - **Mark all as seen** (iOS `AppModel.markSeen`): the top row of the list when filtering **Unread**, the space heading's menu, and the right of Overview's **Unread** all confirm first (`views/MarkSeenDialog.tsx`, a chunk of its own loaded on the first open, #17142); it marks them seen locally right away (WS `seen`, `POST …/seen` when disconnected).
  - **Pin** (`GET / PUT /pins`, keys as on iOS: `machine/space name`, `machine/session id`): a **Pin** section at the very top; pinned spaces come first in by-project grouping and never fold even when idle; local state changes first and is restored on failure.
  - **Row menu / space menu** (iOS `AgentRowMenu` / `SpaceMenuItems`, `src/views/AgentMenus.tsx`): the ⋯ shown when hovering an Agent row, or right-click (opens at the mouse position): live attach, pin, rename, mute notifications, **Hand back to Persona**, copy directory / resume command, close Agent… (the same confirmation dialog `CloseAgentDialog` as the chat's ⋯, #3405),
    followed by the group every node has (copy session ID / pane ID, new pane, Git, close pane; see "Node menu" below);
    a space heading's ⋯: **Open space page**, **Mark all as seen**, rename space, pin space, mute this space, followed by fold, new Agent, Git, copy path. On hover, hints and badges at the row end move aside so ⋯ does not cover half of them.
    **Hand back to Persona** (iOS `AgentHandoff`) sends this Agent's situation into the main chat as a context card, through the cross-page pending message (see "Persona" below); you jump there and see the bubble.
- **Todos** (`/todos`, `src/views/Todos.tsx`): list on the left, details on the right. The list is sorted by unfinished state (needs you > unread > working > to follow up > not started) and creation time, with completed ones at the bottom; each row shows the state, number of linked Agents, the last line of the most urgent Agent and the last update time (`updated_at`, as on iOS / Android, #2975). A filter button beside the search field filters by due date and orders rows inside each section, with a chip that clears the filter (#3740, `../assistant/todos.md` "List filter and sort").
