Until the first load finishes it shows loading, and the header no counts rather than zeros (audit item 83); with no todos it shows an icon + **No to-dos** + an explanation + **New to-do**, and a different text when a search finds nothing. If the list is empty and the latest read failed, it instead shows **Couldn't load to-dos**, the shared request-error explanation and **Retry** (#5173), and hides the header counts until a read succeeds or a list is available. Retry reads only `/todos` and stays disabled until that read finishes; success clears the error, while a failed refresh keeps any existing list visible. The unsupported-hub (404) behavior is unchanged. The header's counts are the status sections' in every grouping, so switching the grouping changes no number ([todo-status-sop.md](../assistant/todo-status-sop.md) "Header count", audit item 12): by folder the folders hold what the sections place outside Done (a to-do ticked in the last day stays in its folder, muted, with **Got it**, until it is seen; a folder with a to-do in Needs you says Needs you), and the folded **Done** at the bottom holds the Done section. A closed row's title is muted at normal weight; only a cancelled one is struck through, so an accepted, deployed or owner-ticked to-do no longer reads as dropped (#11677). By pinned direction the directions hold the open to-dos the hub's tree lists, a line counts the open ones it does not, the rest outside Done (closed in the last day, accepted, deployed, inactive) keep their status sections below the directions, as on Android, and the folded **Done** holds the Done section. On narrow screens (< 768px) the list and details take turns: clicking a row goes to details (URL gets `?id=`), and **Todos** at the top left goes back to the list. Taking turns, nothing is open until a row is: no row is marked current and no hidden page loads a to-do's repositories or decisions, also while a search changes the first row (#11442); side by side the first row still stands in. A row opened from the list puts the focus on that **Todos** button; Esc goes back as it does (not from a field being edited, nor under a dialog or a menu), and back on the list, by the button, Esc or the browser's Back, the list is scrolled where it was with the focus on that to-do's row, a to-do opened by a link too (audit item 74). Coming back to the page from another one (the browser's Back) brings the list's scroll back too (`lib/scroll-memory.ts`, audit item 88). On a wide window the details keep a page's reading width (760 px, `docs/design/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md` "Sizes"), centered (audit item 75). These and the date fields below are checked in Chrome by `web/e2e/todos-keyboard-layout.mjs` (`web/e2e/README.md`). Details let you edit the title and description in place, set the due date (and time), reminder, priority and project (a date or a time is saved once it is entered: on leaving the field, on Enter, or at once when picked from the browser's picker; never on each typed digit, once however soon the field is left after Enter, and no field is disabled while it saves, audit item 2), list currently linked Agents (click to open the chat; each row's × unlinks it, and for ones that failed to start it is **Remove**) and past participants; you can **Hand to agent** (open a new one or hand to an existing one, with a to-do context card and `todo_id`; on a phone the dialog keeps Cancel and Hand over in the sheet's footer, above the keyboard, and its agents are a radio group, #11511), complete / reopen, or delete. A task whose agent never started, still waiting on the owner (closed by the hub with its start error, in Needs you), reads open on its page as on its row (audit item 13): why it did not start in red, **Retry** when the hub can start it again from its plan (`POST /todos/{id}/retry`, the main chat's task card's Retry, `retryTask` in `lib/feed.ts`: one on its way at a time from either), **Hand to agent**, which reopens it only once it is handed over, and **Complete**, which closes it for good as its checkbox does. In **New to-do**, a decision's dialog and **Hand to agent**, ⌘↩ / Ctrl+↩ submits from the multi-line field, as in New Agent and Compose (audit item 70). A row's menu (#4429, `views/todo-row-menu.ts`; right click at the pointer, the menu key or Shift+F10 on a focused row) does the common ones without opening the to-do: **Complete to-do** / **Reopen to-do** (as its checkbox), **Priority** ▸ High / Normal / Low, **Due date** ▸ Today / Tomorrow / Next week (the first day of the calendar's week) / **Pick a date…** (a dialog) / No due date, a to-do due at a time keeping its time, **Remind me** ▸ In 1 hour / Tomorrow morning (9:00) / No reminder, **Hand to agent…** (open to-dos only, the same dialog) and **Delete to-do…**, which asks in the same confirmation dialog as the page's ⋯. Each acts on that row's to-do through `PATCH` / `DELETE /todos/{id}`, and the to-do open beside the list stays open; a save that fails says so in a toast. A right click on a row's PR link keeps the browser's menu. A Just finished row has **Got it** under its words (#5707, hub feature `todo_seen`): it goes to Done at once, with an Undo toast; opening one and leaving it does the same, silently (`lib/todo-seen.ts`, [todo-status-sop.md](../assistant/todo-status-sop.md) "Seen"). A **Topic** section shows the chat thread the to-do is bound to (#5279) with **Unbind** (the list row gets a chat mark); "Chat thread" in `../assistant/todos.md`. The chat page's ⋯ menu and session info show "To-do: X"; when the hub does not support the todo API (404), the entries are hidden.
  **The sidebar's badge** (#11085, `ownerBadge` / `ownerNeeds` in `src/lib/todo-triage.ts`, read through `useOwnerNeeds` in `src/lib/todo-owner-needs.ts`, drawn in `src/views/SidebarParts.tsx`): the To-dos entry counts the open to-dos that need the owner, not those Agents are on, never more than the header's Not done, which is unchanged. A to-do that waits on the owner (`waitsOnOwner`: under Waiting on you, or its work held for their OK, `delivery.unblock = user`) counts; one whose own Agent is on it (Working) does not, nor one whose pieces (`part_of`, any depth, a loop walked once) have an Agent on them or wait on the owner (the waiting piece counts by itself); the rest counts, a personal to-do with no Agent included. Quiet tasks are left out as before. The row's tooltip and every spoken form of the page (the row, the rail, the phone's grid, a folded Pages title; `pageLabel`, a page's `badgeLabel`) say what the number counts: "2 to-dos need you" ([todos.md](../assistant/todos.md) "Sidebar and main navigation"). The rule is the owner's preference behind #11085, and maintainers decide the default; iOS and Android follow. **The page marks what it counts** (#11838): each row the badge counts has **Up to you** after its title (`OwnerMark` in `src/views/Todos.tsx`, `Tag` in the accent tone the badge is drawn in), why it counts in its tooltip and said after it ("No Agent is working on it", "An Agent on it asks you something or was cut off", …: `ownerNeeds`' reason), in every list grouping; a folded status section, folder, pinned direction or "N related" says how many under it are counted (`OwnerMarkCount`, "1 up to you"). The badge and the page read one hook, `useOwnerNeeds`, over the page's own inputs (`useTodoLookup`: the Agents list's rows, an open task's Agent from the list's task rows, cards answered here; `useTodoMinute`, the page's minute tick), so a to-do the page files under Working is never counted and, with nothing filtered or searched and every fold open, the marked rows are the badge's number. A filter or a search narrows the rows, not the badge; the calendar and By request draw no mark. Check: `web/src/lib/todo-triage.badge.test.ts`, `web/src/views/SidebarTodosBadge.test.tsx`, `web/src/views/Todos.owner-mark.test.tsx`, and the mock with `MOCK_TODO_BADGE=1` (a goal whose two pieces Agents are working on, and an errand: Not done 4, the badge 1, the errand marked under Other open).
  **A to-do's steps** (#11858, `stepsWords` in `src/lib/todo-steps.ts`): a to-do others are `part_of` says the hub's count of them (`view.steps`, the web counts nothing itself) on its row and its page: with no Agent of its own "Steps 1/3" in place of Not started, or "3/3 steps done · Next step not arranged yet" once all are closed, in place of "Not handed to an agent yet"; with one, "· Steps 1/2" after its Agent count. No view, no steps or closed: as before. Check: `web/src/lib/todo-steps.test.ts` (with the `spec/fixtures/todo-view` cases that have steps), `web/src/views/Todos.steps.test.tsx`, and the mock with `MOCK_TODO_STEPS=1`.
  **A waiting to-do's label** (#11090, `todoLook` / `waitReason` in `src/lib/todo-wait-reason.ts`): where a to-do's state is Waiting (its Agent ended its turn and something brings it back) the row, its page, Overview's task cards, the main chat's trays, the sidebar's By to-do rows, a space's page, the calendar and Link to to-do say what it waits on instead of one "Waiting": **Waiting on you** in the attention color only when `waitsOnOwner` holds, the badge's own predicate, so the label and the badge agree; a neutral word for the rest (background work, a retry, a prerequisite, a merge or deploy, something external); **Paused (nothing needed from you)** when nothing says ([todos.md](../assistant/todos.md) "State calculation rules", row 4.5). Check: `web/src/lib/todo-wait-reason.test.ts`, `web/src/views/TodoWaitLabels.test.tsx`, and the mock with `MOCK_TODO_WAITS=1` (one to-do per wait).
  **Check completion** (#1373) appears in details for tasks created by the assistant (`origin` is present), including closed or reopened tasks. An explicit click reads the existing completion diagnostic once, with a visible wait of up to a minute and a half and a client deadline five seconds past the hub’s 90-second limit. The result belongs to that check: assessment, reason, check time, automatic-completion exclusions and any delivery blocker. It changes no task state, starts no agent and never replaces supervised review. **Check again** / **Retry check** are deliberate; there is no polling or automatic retry. Requests and local results belong to the task, its stamped manager (or the default) and the credential generation, and are retired on replacement or navigation. Route-level 404 means the hub needs an update; a task-specific 404 says the task is missing. Read-only access, sign-in, service, network and timeout failures show localized explanations.
  **By request** (a fourth grouping beside Status, Folder and Pinned, offered while some request is in pieces (`hasRequestPieces` in `lib/todos.ts`: a to-do is `part_of` another listed one, or two to-dos came from one plan; a saved choice falls back to Status otherwise, as Pinned does), kept in `persona.todos.grouping`; `views/TodoRequestGraph.tsx`, loaded when chosen, pure parts `lib/request-graph.ts`): the list column becomes a graph of every request, drawn left to right, and the search and due-date filter (which have nothing to narrow there) are left out. It takes the page's whole width; picking a piece opens that to-do's own detail beside it, as a row does (a close button gives the width back; on a phone the detail replaces the graph, as it does the list). A request is a block, most active first (what needs the user, then work going on, then what waits; latest change first). Its root card is headed by the sentence the work was filed under (the request to-do's title; for a request of one piece, that piece's title) with the owner's own words quoted under it in small type when they say something else (**Your words: …**; `brief.request.text`, else a line of the request to-do's notes such as `用户原话（…）：…` / `Your words: …`), so an answer like "Go ahead" never becomes the heading; a plan of several tasks, which has no sentence of its own, is headed by the owner's words. The card says when they were said and how many pieces are done; each piece is a card in layers (layer = 1 + the deepest layer among what it waits for; layer 1 waits for nothing), joined by thin connectors with a hollow dot where they leave a card, dashed into a piece still queued. A card says its state (queued behind named pieces, ready but nobody took it, working with how long, needs you with what it asks, waits to be accepted, done, did not start with why; a task of an open plan waits for Start), its title and the Agent on it (mark, model, effort and computer; none: **No Agent yet**). A piece with more than one Agent (the ones it had before aside) grows its **Agent tree** under its card, open at first and folded to one line by its heading ("7 Agents · 5 working"): the piece's own Agents, under each first the workers it handed out (open and closed), then the Agents it spawned, then its in-session subagents nested by the subagent that launched each, the earliest first, joined by the graph's own connectors; the ones it had before come last. Each line gives the Agent's name, its state and what it is doing (or last said), and opens its session (a subagent: its own link `<launching session>@<id>`, which opens the launching chat at that subagent's card, expanded; never the Agent that launched it). One that finished while the piece goes on stays, grey with a check (**Ended**); under one parent, ended subagents beyond the latest three fold into one **N more ended** line. A row of the graph is as tall as its tallest card, tree included, and connectors stay on the cards' heads. Subagents come from the complete session rows (a list's summary row has none), read while the graph is shown, with the direction tree filling in missing subagents and their running or ended status; how long an ended one stays is the node's to say (Claude Code's: a day after it finished), and an Agent session the hub no longer lists drops out with what it ran. With one Agent the card is as before. Hovering or focusing a card lights it, what it waits for and what waits for it, and dims the rest; the hover card (`views/TodoRequestGraphTip.tsx`, no `title` attributes) lists who is on it and what it waits for. A card with a to-do opens it on the page; a task of a plan not started has none and only shows its hover card. A request of one piece whose title is the request's words is that piece's card alone, as long as the request's own to-do and the piece are both closed or both open as stored (`done_at` without `start_error`, `mergesWithRoot`), and a card drawn done never stands for a request's to-do still open. A piece can be drawn otherwise than it is stored: closed by the hub and not looked at yet it is drawn waiting to be accepted, accepted and then reopened with nothing running it is drawn done while open. On any split the root card stays, so the request's to-do can still be opened, completed or reopened from the graph (every root × piece combination is a case in `lib/request-graph-merge-cases.ts`, checked in `lib/request-graph.test.ts` and `views/TodoRequestGraph.test.tsx`). Finished requests fold to one line each under **Done**. Under the graph, **Queued** lists the pieces nobody took yet and those waiting for others (what needs the user is on the Overview and the to-do rows, not repeated here). Everything is the hub's own data.
  The graph reads the hub's own fields (`docs/assistant/todos.md` "Requests in pieces"): a to-do's `part_of` makes it a piece of that request (the to-do named is the request's root) and its `after` names the pieces it waits for. The manager checks them when they are written (one level, no cycle); the web still skips edges to missing to-dos and a `part_of` that names a piece, and drops an edge that would close a cycle. Requests come from a to-do others name in `part_of`, from the to-dos of one task plan (`plan_id`; an open plan shows its tasks waiting for Start), else a to-do is a request of one piece; `part_of` wins over the plan, and a worker a leader's Agent handed out is drawn among the leader's Agents, not as a request of its own. One rule places every to-do once (`placement` in `lib/request-graph.ts`): a worker that is itself a piece keeps its own card and is not repeated in its dispatcher's tree, a worker the request root's own Agent handed out is drawn as a piece of that request (a root's card has no Agent tree), a worker whose ledger names a supervisor follows the supervisor, and to-dos whose dispatchers name each other in a loop each keep a card. For an unstarted piece, `prerequisite_blockers` decides whether it is queued: an empty list means Ready, and a nonempty list names what it waits for by title or by ID when the to-do is missing. This does not add connectors or change the state of work that already started. When the field is absent, the graph only waits for existing `after` pieces that are not done (`done_at` without `start_error`). A piece that waits keeps its to-do until its turn, so the graph never has to match a replacement to it.
  **Waiting for you** (#2056, `views/TodoAsk.tsx`): a to-do whose result waits on the user carries the hub's `ask` ("Waiting for the owner" in `../assistant/todos.md`), and the web shows it wherever the to-do is: under the status line of its row, on the main chat's task card, over its agent's chat in the task panel (the chat's `banner`), and as a **Needs you** box on its page. Each says the verdict line as the hub words it (it starts with its own ✅ / ⛔ / 🤔), "Recommended: …" for a decision that has one, and one button: **OK** on a row or a card and **Take recommendation** on the page for a decision, **Got it** for a conclusion that only tells, **Accept** for a deployed to-do's "Please verify". It posts `POST /todos/{id}/accept` with the ask's `asked_at`, the briefing's route (`acceptBrief`); clicks on it never open the row. Taken, it says so and the to-dos are read again (the ask is gone); an earlier round's 409 (no code of its own, `conflict`) says **Already handled** and reads them again; any other failure (502 when the recommendation did not reach the agent, a 423 the Agent's node refused with its own code such as `dialog_open`, or a 409 with that code from a hub built before 423) toasts the hub's reason and leaves the button to try again. On a decision's row in the Needs you tray a `dialog_open` refusal is said on the row instead (#7343, `DecisionRow.tsx`): the dialog blocks the Agent's terminal, its first line when the hub sent `dialog`, and **Open terminal** for the Agent the hub named (`machine_id` / `session_id`); the buttons stay and the next press clears it (mock hub: `MOCK_DECISIONS=1 MOCK_TODO_ASKS=1 MOCK_ACCEPT_DIALOG=1` refuses every answer that way); a newer round offers it again. A decision that recommends nothing has no button: the page says to answer it in its conversation and, for a task from one, **Answer in chat** opens it. A stopped to-do with an open ask sorts and groups with **Awaiting review** (`awaitsReview` in `lib/todos.ts`). Screenshots: the mock hub with `MOCK_TASKS=1 MOCK_TODO_ASKS=1` (a decision on "检查 PR #42", a conclusion that cannot be done on the blog, the release notes' "Please verify"; Accept takes each off once, then 409).
  **Opening a personal verification** (#16313). Everyday Assistant users open the task report in the side panel or on the to-do page according to their existing opening preference. The report shows the goal, verification summary, available deliverable link and checked criteria. **View raw Agent session** opens the worker in one click. Back returns to the report. Standalone Agent rows open the session directly. The verification card and report offer **Follow up in chat** when the task has an origin. It brings a removable task quote to that conversation, preserves the draft, and leaves Pass available.

  **A decision answered on its Needs you row** (#3804, `views/assistant/DecisionRow.tsx`): in the main chat's **Needs you** tray, a to-do whose `ask` is a decision with `options` (two or more) is a row that can be answered without opening the task. From top to bottom: the task's title (opens the task), the question (`question`, else the verdict line), the hub's one-line background (`background`: where it came from, when, where it stands; two lines at most on a narrow screen), one line per option saying what it leads to with a **Recommended** tag on the first, what happens when nobody answers (**Taken by default at 14:00** from `deadline` in the browser's time zone when `default` is `taken`, **Never taken by default** when it is `never`, nothing otherwise) with what waiting costs, then one line of buttons: the options in the hub's order, the first (the recommendation) the only solid one, **Other…** and **⋯**. **Other…** answers in words (#10760): it opens the conversation the task came from with its composer addressed to this decision round (`setRoute(origin, id, asked_at)`, the same route as the to-do page's **Answer in chat**), so the next message — a condition on an option ("Resume, but move the reminder to Thursday") or an answer of the owner's own — goes to the Agent as the owner's decision through `POST /assistant/conversations/{id}/route` and is recorded on the task; a to-do with no originating conversation opens the task instead. Button text never wraps: the options that do not fit beside **Other…** and **⋯** move into the **⋯** menu (`useFitting` measures the row; the first always stays and, alone and still too wide, cuts its label), which also holds the hub's fixed `responses`, never drawn as buttons: **You decide**, **This isn't what I asked for**, **Tell me the background first**. An option posts `POST /todos/{id}/accept` with `{asked_at, option}`, a response `{asked_at, response}` (`acceptBrief` in `lib/feed.ts`); one answer is admitted at a time, the button spins and the rest are disabled; 409 says **Already handled**, any other failure toasts the hub's reason and leaves the buttons. The row is not part of the first screen: its code is a lazy import of the tray (the task's title on the row's surface until it is in) and its strings are the namespace `assistant-decisionrow`, which loads with the rest of the catalog. A decision that still waits after a fixed answer (`response`, after **Tell me the background first**) says **Sent back to Persona** above its buttons, which still work. An ask without `options` (an older hub, a conclusion, a "Please verify") keeps the row it had (`AcceptRow`). Browser check with synthetic hub traffic only, wide and phone width, light and dark, three languages: `node web/e2e/decision-row.mjs <loopback web URL> --shots <directory> [--chromium <executable>]`.
  **Repositories and work** (`ui/TaskRepositoryBindingsEditor.tsx`, "Repository associations" in `../assistant/todos.md`): a to-do's page reads `GET /todos/{id}/repositories` as it opens and draws the saved repositories as per-repository rows with their issues and PRs as links (`lib/task-repositories.ts` `repositoryLinkView` reads a pasted URL or a saved kind + number with the manager's own rule), so the library an Agent maintains is visible without an editor; a successful answer is authoritative even when empty (the manager imports the legacy history once and honours an explicit removal), so `pr_url` is drawn only as a fallback on a hub without the route, never a second time beside saved links. **Manage links** (a compact text button, `+` when empty) opens the shared `Dialog` and always re-reads the store and catalog first, because an Agent may have added a link since the page loaded; the editor adds repositories through a search picker (name, path or host, `SearchField`) and links through one URL field per repository (`Enter` adds, `Escape` cancels, another repository's URL is refused inline), keeping directory aliases and refs in **Source options**. `removed` / `identity_changed` / `unlisted` are explained under their repository while the saved source is kept. Saving sends the shown revision and catalog revision; a conflict keeps the draft and **Discard edits and reload** reads both again. Creation has the same editor folded under its optional button and still sends one POST. A provider extension's repository (#10330, `../extensions/repository-providers.md` "In the apps") needs no extra request: the to-do's own answer carries its `provider_name`, `provider_state` and `link_kinds`. Its row has the extension mark (`RepositoryMark`, `data-repository-mark="extension"`) and, after the address, its source's name as saved with it (`provider_name`; the page reads no providers list), its saved links open at their stored `canonical_url` (never rebuilt from GitHub's or GitLab's layout) as `#N` in the source's own words, and a draft's `{kind, number}` links are drawn from the saved ones they came from. A pasted address strictly under the repository's (https, same origin, plain path segments, no query, hash or credentials: `underRepository`) is a pending row, "Checked when you save", sent as `{url}`. With the source `off` or `missing`, the row adds an **Unavailable** pill and a note and turns off **Add issue or PR**; its links still open. Browser evidence with synthetic hub replies: `web/e2e/todo-repositories-browser.py`.
  **A task's brief** (#3822, `views/assistant/TaskBrief.tsx`, `lib/brief.ts`; "Briefs" in `../assistant/unified-entry.md`): what a task is held to, shown where the owner meets the task. On the **plan card**, under each task's chips, before **Start** confirms it, the brief is folded: **You asked on <date>: <their own words>** in two lines, or, when the owner did not ask, who started it and why (**Started by the assistant on <date>: <why>**; a leader conversation, a routine, Persona itself; **Started on <date>. Who asked for it was not recorded.** when the hub could not tell), then one line that counts the rest, **2 criteria · about 45 min · 1 out of bounds**, with the brief's one control beside it: **Show all** opens the whole request and the label / value rows in place, **Goal** (left out when it is the task's title), **Done when**, **Expected time** (**About 45 min**, **About 2.5 h**), **Out of bounds**; **Show less** folds them again. The brief must not put **Start** out of reach: the plan card's buttons (`data-plan-actions`) stay at the bottom edge of the tray the card scrolls in whenever the card is taller than it (several tasks, an opened brief), and a card that fits looks as it did. On the **to-do's page**, a **Brief** box above the criteria: the same first line (four lines before **Show all**), the goal and what is out of bounds; the criteria and the expected time stay in the review box under it (a task without one lists them in the brief). A brief made later says so plainly, **Reconstructed: the original request was not recorded**, and shows the **Hand-over prompt** labelled as that, never as the owner's words. While the task is open and past its clock (`overdue_at`), the box has an **Overdue** mark (the caution color with a clock, and a sentence: **Past its expected time since <date>. Its supervisor was told.**). The criteria themselves have one list, the review box's own (`ReviewChecklist`, each criterion's state and evidence from the supervision ledger, #3635); the brief does not draw a second one. Once the work ended against the brief (`brief.result` of this to-do, the to-do done), that box adds under its list only what the list cannot say: each criterion a scope change **dropped**, struck through with the change that dropped it (the undo mark and the word, not color alone), then **Also done**; nothing when no criterion was dropped and nothing else was done. Under the criteria, **Scope changes** (what changed, why, what it added and dropped, the expected time it left, **Approved by you** when the owner's message allowed it) and **Who worked on it** (the lineage, oldest first: the to-do's title, the Agent and computer, from when to when, **Stopped: <why>** or **Still going**, the page's own to-do marked **This task**); nothing for a task whose scope never changed and that nobody took over. A to-do without `brief` (not a task, or an older hub) looks as before. The review line and the done receipt are not drawn in the conversation (`FeedLineView` leaves them out), so the result has no feed item on the web; the receipt's `criteria` and the review's `result` are there for the clients that draw them. None of it is on the first screen: the code is a lazy import of the plan card and of the to-do's page, and the strings are the namespace `assistant-taskbrief`, which loads with the rest of the catalog. Mock: `MOCK_TASKS=1 MOCK_BRIEFS=1` (the open plan's task with a real brief; the widget fix with a real one taken over twice, one scope change and an overdue mark; the blog move with a reconstructed one; the release notes done with one criterion dropped by a scope change and something done beyond the brief). Browser check with synthetic hub traffic only, wide and phone width, light and dark, three languages (it also asserts that **Start** is inside what the tray shows, unscrolled, on a two-task plan with the briefs folded and with one open): `node web/e2e/task-brief.mjs <loopback web URL> --shots <directory> [--chromium <executable>]`.
  **Recommended setup on the briefing card** (#5085, `views/assistant/Brief.tsx`; "Recommended setup" in `../assistant/assistant.md`): on the first briefing of a week whose `brief` item carries `setup`, the card (the `brief` item of a routine with `facts` on, `../extensions/bots.md` ("Morning and evening briefings")) ends with one more section, **Recommended setup**: a line saying the numbers come from the last 7 days of Persona's own records unless a row names its own period, and that nothing was changed, then one row per mechanism with the hub's line as it came (its count, its cost, where it is turned on; in the hub's language, like the card's other rows). A row whose mechanism has a settings page here (Session triage's switches, the standing authorizations, the remembered kinds of task) has **Open settings**, which opens the assistant's settings page and calls nothing on the hub; the others say where in their text. The row for a lower tier of the background supervisor's model (`supervisor_tier`, #5805) has the same button, which opens the purpose **Background supervisor** in Model settings (`/settings?tab=models&purpose=assistant.supervise`) and changes nothing. No section without `setup` (every other briefing, an older hub). It is the card's existing section and row, with no new component; the strings are in the namespace `assistant-brief`.
  **List | Calendar | Board** at the top right (#2029, `views/TodoCalendar.tsx`, the rules in `lib/todo-calendar.ts`): the calendar shows the to-dos with a due date by day, week or month, kept in the address (`/todos?view=calendar&mode=week&date=2026-11-09`, `&id=` the to-do open beside it) and the choice per browser (`persona.todos.view`, `persona.todos.calendar.mode`, `persona.todos.calendar.showDone`); `/todos` with no view opens the one last used. A block's top edge is its due moment, all-day ones sit in the row above the axis, overlapping blocks side by side, a red line at the moment; the month shows three lines a day ("N more"). Clicking a to-do opens its detail beside the calendar (on a phone instead of it, **Back to calendar**); dragging it moves it to another time or day and saves it at once (#2045: the axis snaps to the quarter hour, the All day row makes it all day, the month keeps its time; a touch drags after a press held still, Escape or a failed save puts it back); today's date is the filled accent badge of the design system's buttons (`--accent-ink` under `--surface`, at least 4.5:1 in light and dark, audit item 79); clicking the empty axis (or the all-day row) opens **New to-do** due there (snapped to the half hour), **New to-do** in the header due on the day shown. ← → turn the page, T is today. A phone's width has day and month only. Those without a due date are counted under it, with a link to the list. "Calendar" in `../assistant/todos.md`.
  **Download deadlines** saves the dates on screen as an iCalendar file for another calendar app. It follows **Show done**, includes the whole date grid in month view, and is disabled when there are no visible deadlines. The download uses the loaded entries, including cached ones. The file keeps each deadline’s date or time and leaves availability free. It omits private fields and replaces credential-bearing Persona API links in titles with an ellipsis. Event identifiers are scoped to the source hub and manager and survive edits. The revision timestamp comes from the to-do so a later download of cached entries keeps their original revision.
  **Progress board** (#12713, `views/TodoBoard.tsx`): **Board** is a read-only display of every open to-do (`countsAsOpen`, including the Developing Persona hub-view path), never a filter on the List's hidden search or due-date controls. It groups by the stored `project` alone, with **No project** last rather than inferring a repository; each heading counts its displayed rows as **open / waiting on you / stale**. A row shows the title, the stored `responsible` name (else the linked worker's title, else **Unassigned**), and the latest progress summary with its own timestamp: the supervised `progress.at` + `progressLine`, an active session's current words/step and time, or, only for an external responsible party with neither linked-Agent nor supervised progress, its `updated_at` + notes. Without one of those pairs it says **No progress yet** and uses `created_at` for age. **Waiting on you** means the existing triage rule `owner_decides`, not every unattended row. The positive, finite stale-hours value defaults to 72 and is kept only in this browser's `localStorage` (`persona.todos.board.staleHours`); invalid input leaves the last valid value unchanged, and exactly N hours is not stale (strictly longer is). The address is `/todos?view=board`, with `&id=` for the existing detail beside it; browser Back closes that detail and returns to the board. Opening and changing the board reads only the list the page already has: no new endpoint, model call, Agent start, to-do write or automatic follow-up, and no editing, completion, assignment or follow-up control on its rows. The List and Calendar behavior is unchanged. Check: `web/src/views/Todos.board.test.tsx` and `node web/e2e/todo-progress-board.mjs <loopback web URL> [--shots <directory>] [--executable <chromium>]` (synthetic data; desktop / phone, light / dark, default / large text).
- **New Agent**: the model is picked with the model pill at the right of the first message box's bottom row, in the unified model panel ("New Agent's model choice (#5104)" below). Claude Code launchers have **Permission mode** (follow launcher / ask manually / auto-edit files / plan only / auto / allow everything; picking allow everything shows a red risk warning below), sent as `permission_mode` at launch and remembered per computer (`new.mode.<machine>`, as on iOS); not shown for Codex. A launcher that lists its own permission modes (#8261, the node's `permission_modes`: Paseo's Grok, OpenCode, Codex and its other providers; `lib/launcher-models.ts` `listedModes` and `effortRule`) follows one rule on every client instead: **Permission mode** offers **Launcher default** (no mode sent) and **Full access** (with the red warning) only where it lists both, picked on the sheet and never remembered, so a mode left from a Claude Code start never reaches it; its effort is only one its model lists (none while that is not known). The first message supports picking, pasting or dropping images or files; attachments are previewed locally first and can be removed. Images are sent with the message; other files are uploaded to the chosen computer in the background and their paths are put into the message.
  The folder list follows the folder field (#9452, `lib/typed-folder.ts`). A folder filled in (the last start's when the sheet opens, a recent setup's, a recent folder picked) lists its subfolders under the recent folders; one since removed lists where browsing starts. A full path typed there (`/…`, `~`, `~/…`, `C:\…`; a relative one is left alone) is followed once typing pauses (250 ms): it lists that folder's subfolders, and a path that names no folder yet lists the folder its last part is in, keeping the subfolders whose names start with that part (ignoring case), as a shell completes a path; the recent folders hide meanwhile. A row picked from the list fills the field without moving the list, browsing from the list (a row's ›, the header's ‹) takes over until the field changes again, and an empty field brings back the recent folders and home. A temporary session's empty field is not followed. Tests: `lib/typed-folder.test.ts`, `views/NewAgent.folder.test.tsx`.
  New Agent in a desktop app (#5480 Claude's desktop app, #5726 the Codex App; `lib/desktop-start.ts`, `views/NewAgentDesktop.tsx`, the same rules as iOS's `DesktopStart.swift`; the computer's side: `docs/integrations/claude-integration.md`, "New sessions in the desktop app"): when the launcher that runs (the one picked, or Model settings' default) has `source` `claude_desktop` or `codex_app`, a folder not picked in this opening (the last start's, filled in, does not count; a row, typing, a card or a page's own folder does) is a **Temporary session**: the row above the folder field says so, Start is ready, and the start carries no folder, which the computer turns into the app's scratch folder (the Codex App: a chat in no project, still with its required first message). **Use a temporary session** goes back from a folder picked. Browsing starts in the folder holding most of this computer's sessions of that app (`projectsFolder`, worked out when the computer or the launcher changes; the Codex App's own folders for chats in no project left out), and **New folder…** in the list's header names a folder in the one browsed, which the computer makes when the session starts. The engine host choice is not offered (the app is where it opens), the worktree switch is not offered for a temporary session, the last real folder stays remembered for the next start, and a recent setup of a temporary session reads **Temporary session**. Run agent here never lists these launchers (`launchableHere`). The parts and their words load only when such a launcher runs (namespace `newagent-desktop`), off the first screen. Tests: `lib/desktop-start.test.ts`, `views/NewAgent.desktop.test.tsx`.
  A launcher whose latest check failed is not in the list the hub sends (#4437; `docs/server/launcher-health.md` "In the App"); since #14535 it arrives in `unavailable` with the hub's reason (code `launcher_unhealthy`) and is drawn as the providers below are. The exceptions are `not_in_terminal` and the configured default, which still arrive with `health` (`#1643`, `lib/launcher-health.ts`): the model panel lists them as groups whose rows are off, with why under the group's name and **How to fix**;
  that opens the fix panel under the box (`LauncherBlockedHelp.tsx`: why, what to do, Details, **Add model provider** → the provider wizard, **Try anyway** picks that launcher with its default model), and a computer's first pick skips them; when what runs this time (the pick, or Model settings' default) can't start here, a line under the box says so, tagged "Used this time", with **How to fix**. Run agent here and a to-do's hand-off follow the same list (`docs/server/launcher-health.md` "In the App").
  A Persona-managed provider whose own-service rule leaves it out on this computer (`own_service: skip` where Claude Code or Codex has a sign-in of its own, #8109) arrives in the hub's `unavailable` rather than not at all: the panel lists it after the computer's launchers as a group with no rows and the hub's reason, and its **How to fix** closes the dialog and opens the provider's page in Settings › Model providers (`/settings?tab=models&launcher=<name>`), whose Computers has the switch. Tests: `lib/new-agent-panel.test.ts`, `views/NewAgent.launcher-health.test.tsx`.
  Clicking **On** closes the dialog and opens a local session right away, with the first text and attachments visible immediately; the real session is created with `async:true` and then `/messages` is sent, without waiting for the remote launch to finish before navigating.
  **Starting** in the sidebar keeps the background task; it continues when you switch to other pages, and does not force-navigate you when done. On failure the content is kept and can be retried; once a real session exists, only the upload or send is retried.
  Creation and the first message each go through `apiOp` with an op id kept on the launch (`lib/new-agent.ts`): a gap (no network, a proxy's 502/503/504, a hub restart) is waited out and sent again with that id, so a lost answer starts nothing twice and asks nobody anything. Retry after a gap repeats the start unchanged, so the form stays closed. After a refusal the hub keeps its answer to the id, so Retry goes under new ids and the form can be edited.
  Only when the hub itself says it doesn't know how it went (`delivered: unknown`, a 5xx, `202 {"state":"unknown"}`) does it suggest checking the list / session, and Retry asks first and then goes under new ids. The first message can still be empty; Codex text launch is kept for compatibility, but its creation protocol does not support first-message attachments, which the UI states explicitly.
  A start whose new terminal tab stopped on a question of the shell's startup files (`shell_waiting`, #10365; hub feature `start_continue`) shows the question under the failure, on the launch's page and in the chat (`views/ShellQuestionCard.tsx`, loaded only then): the design system's notice (`ErrorNotice`) with the terminal's mark in `--ink-2` instead of the red one, "Your computer's terminal is asking: “…”", what helps and until when the tab stays open, one 28 px button per answer the computer offers (`start_error_args.choices`, worded by what it does where the question says, with the key: **Update (y)**, **Not now (n)**, **Enter (yes)**; a password prompt gets **Cancel (Ctrl-C)** alone, an ssh host key no trust) and the tab's last lines under **Error details**. A tap sends `POST …/start/continue`, shows the session starting at once, and sends again the messages that start refused (`lib/start-continue.ts` `resendRefused`: the launch's first message first, then the outbox's entries with code `shell_waiting` once it went, one after another; one refused again keeps them back); a refusal (the tab expired, an answer not offered) stays on the card in the hub's words. A question answered at the computer meanwhile is no refusal: the computer types nothing and starts the session in that tab. The card goes once the tab is no longer kept. A planned task's failed start with the same question (its plan task's `error_code` / `error_args`; hub feature `todo_start_answer`) shows the same card on its failed row, in the task panel and on the to-do page, beside Retry, which stays: a tap sends `POST /api/v1/todos/{id}/start/answer` and puts the reopened to-do in place (`answerTaskStart`); the hub then starts the task in that tab. On a hub without the feature the task offers Retry alone, as before.
  Text drafts are saved in localStorage; attachments and background tasks live only in the current page's memory, so reloading the page does not restore unfinished tasks.
- **Overview**: **Needs you** (interaction cards for you to handle), **Stuck, take a look** (Agents that need you but have no card for you to handle; formerly "Stopped on the computer"), **Working** (with timers), **Waiting in the background** (Agents whose background commands only wait, #6045: with the clock mark and timed from when the wait began, never in Working or its count; a tab with one Agent really working stays under Working, that Agent speaking for its row, #10938), and **Unread** (**Mark all as seen** on the right), one row each (Task Rows), with the computers below and the extensions' cards (`overview_card`) last (#11147). The sentence at the top counts Agents ("5 agents need you", then the working ones, the ones waiting in the background apart from them, and the unseen ones; `stateCounts` / `useCounts` in `lib/sessions.ts`, which take the hub's `background_waiting` out of its `state.working` on a paging hub), while **Needs you** counts cards: when one Agent has several cards there is an extra gray line under the heading explaining it; **Stuck, take a look** also has an explanatory line (#2956).
  Rows are compact (#5599): the title alone on the first line, then the computer / space / tab as small tags and the latest words (one line of plain text: their Markdown marks are left out through `plainMarkdown` in `lib/plain-markdown.ts`, as on the sidebar's row line, a computer's Agent rows and a knowledge entry's Agents, #10939); a tag that only repeats the title (a tab named after the agent's first words) is left out, and a session's source is a tag rather than a prefix of the latest words. The page grows to 1920px on wide screens and its agent sections go into columns by container width (two from 60rem, three from 100rem; rows with one-tap answers from 84rem / 120rem); phones and narrow windows keep one column. For screenshots use the mock hub with `MOCK_OVERVIEW_DENSE=1` (many finished rows, long titles, tabs named after their titles, one untitled).
  When tags and the latest words share a line, the words get at least half its width. Long tags truncate within the remaining space (#16465).
  **Computers** has a `Segmented` **Cards / Rows** switch beside **Monitoring** on its heading. The choice lives in this browser's `persona.overview.machines.view` preference through `storedValue` / `storeValue`, survives reloads, and defaults to **Cards**; if storage is unavailable it falls back to Cards on read and keeps the current page's choice in memory on write. **Rows** is the original hub-ordered compact-row grid and mounts no metrics reader. **Cards** keeps the existing identity, Agent count, connection guidance and whole-row machine link, and adds the exact `MachineMetricsSummary` used by Machines: current CPU / load, memory, network, optional Tokens and their one-hour SVG plots, with the same formatting and colors. Offline, pending and never-reporting computers keep a self-sized compact row, with no empty metric cells; battery, thermal and token-only reports count as monitoring, while disk-only and empty samples do not. `OverviewMachineCards` owns one visible 10-second `/metrics` read per online assistant through the same loader as Machines, keeps last-good partial results, shows Machines' alert for a total failure (load failure without numbers, or last-good numbers marked stale while retrying every 10 seconds), and has no per-card effects or requests; its metric state does not redraw the Agent and task sections. A local error boundary keeps a failed summary chunk inside its computer card and retries it when the next sample arrives. Switching to Rows unmounts that reader and stops its timer at once. The metric summary lazy-loads after the row, so it does not add Machines' charts or translations to the first screen. `OverviewMachineCards.test.tsx` covers the switch, persistence, request-free Rows, exact summary charts, compact fallbacks and navigation.
  After the initial load, if there are no computers and no Agents or interactions needing attention, the summary asks you to connect a computer first. The **All set** card becomes **No computers yet**, explains that a computer must connect to the hub before you can create an Agent, and offers **Open machines** (#3729). The overview header also hides **New agent** when there are no computers. Before the first load the summary says **Connecting to the hub…** while the socket is not connected and **Loading…** once it is (the hub's first answers are still on their way); with any existing computer, including an offline one, the usual overview and actions remain.
  On a hub that pages its Agents list (`sessions_list`) the socket pushes no sessions, so how many Agents there are is known only once the list they come from has been read over HTTP: the list's first pages with one assistant, the complete list (`useFullAgentSessions`) with several. Overview takes that status from the same source as its counts (`useScopedAgentListStatus` in `lib/current-assistant.ts`, over `useAgentListStatus` in `lib/sessions.ts`). Until then the summary says **Loading…**; when the read failed it says **Couldn't load what your agents are doing.** with **Retry** (which reads that list at once; the hub's next change of the list, and the complete list's own retry every 5 s, do too), and neither claims that nothing needs you nor shows **All set**. A read that the hub's next change of the list (or the 5 s retry) starts after a failure keeps the failure line and its Retry in place until one succeeds, so they never turn into **Loading…** under the pointer; **Retry** itself says **Loading…** until the answer, as the Agents list's Retry does (`retryFullAgentSessions`). The summary line holds one live region (`role="status"`), mounted throughout, with only its state in it (**Connecting to the hub…**, **Loading…** or the failure), so a screen reader hears the failure; the counts sentence that replaces it is plain text, so the counts are not read out again each time an Agent starts, stops or finishes. Meanwhile each computer's line leaves out its Agent count (its system name, or **Online**) rather than saying "0 agents", while **Needs you** still lists the cards, which come from their own read (web audit item 30). A computer's count also needs a list that holds every Agent: with one assistant the first pages hold only the newest Agents while the list has more pages (`hasMore`), so the line leaves the count out then too, rather than reading the complete list on the landing page; the Machines page counts every computer from the complete list. The summary is never an empty sentence: with no Agent needing you, working or unseen but cards waiting (a Persona conversation's, whose Agent is not counted), it says how many requests are waiting.
  Several Agents in the same herdr tab collapse into one row (#2320, `homeTaskGroups` in `lib/herdr-tree.ts`; since #5180 only peers, a tab whose first pane is a shell, as a lead's workers fold into the lead's row): placed under the most urgent state among them, titled with the lead's title (or the first pane's when there is no lead),
  with the latest line of the representative Agent below it (prefixed with the Agent name if it is not the lead). The row end has a status dot per Agent and "N agents" (only dots on narrow screens); clicking opens that tab on the representative pane.
  **Tasks in progress** (#6450, the web side of the Lark bot's `/tasks`, #5432) sits above **Working**: every open to-do, manual ones too, in the Tasks page's order and with its status read the same way (cards answered on the page count at once), each with its stage bar and PR link, a delivery held short of live and then who works on it (#10904): the computer, model and effort of its working Agent, else of the one that moved last ("MacBook · Opus 5.5 · XHigh"), named as that Agent's model pill names them (the model list's name once the pill has read it, else the short form of the id; no effort reported, none said), and "+N" for its other Agents, kept when the line is cut short; until a row of its Agents is read it says how many there are, as before. A concern keeps the same neutral **Concern** tag as its To-dos row beside that status (#3582); six at most, then **See all ›** to the Tasks page; no section without open to-dos.
  Each **Unread** row has **Continue** (#6449, the web side of the Lark bot's "reply to the done card", #5438): it opens one line under the row and sends it to that Agent through the chat's outbox (`queueToSession`), so the chat shows the same message. The Agent is the one the row named when the line opened (in a tab of several, the placeholder names it). Sent, the row says so and moves to **Working** with the hub's next push; not sent, the line keeps the text and shows the outbox's reason, and sending it again is the outbox's Retry of that message (a changed line replaces it). Not offered on read-only sessions; an input method's Enter is not a send; Escape closes it and focus returns to the button.
  The representative is the one ranked first, by this group's ordering, among the Agents in that state: for working, the longest-running (timer and sorting follow it); for needs you / done not seen, the newest (time, preview and sorting follow it); ties go to the earlier pane.
  An Agent that already has an interaction card is counted in the cards above and no longer decides which group its tab goes into; when only cards are left, it does not say there is nothing that needs you.
  **Needs you** rows can answer simple things in place (#4090, the same scope as the quick buttons on iOS "Needs you" cards, `lib/quick-answers.ts`): permissions (that need no input) get Allow / Deny; single questions with one choice and at most 4 options, and terminal dialogs the hub read, get option buttons, and the row shows the tool and command. Plans, multi-question, multi-select, typed answers and MCP forms still open the chat. Answers go through the same `resolve` as chat cards; the button spins while sending; once answered the row says "Answered: …" in place for about 1.6 seconds before collapsing (so the next row does not slide up and get clicked by mistake); on failure the row and buttons stay and a toast gives the reason. While an answer to the card is on its way from anywhere (this row, its chat's card, a notification; #2793 `usePendingLine` in `lib/card-answer.ts`), the row's buttons are disabled, also after leaving Overview and coming back, and the row says which answer waits with the card's own line (**Sending: …** / **Sends when connected: …**).
  **Mark all as seen** still marks every done-but-not-seen Agent (the confirmation shows the actual count), including those collapsed into the **Stuck, take a look** and working rows: when there is an **Unread** group it sits right of that heading; when there is no such group but there are done-not-seen Agents, it sits right of the summary sentence at the top. Search (⌘K), todos, and groupings other than by machine in the sidebar / Agents page (by repo / project / status / to-do) still show one Agent per row.
- **Chat page** (`src/lib/turns.ts`, `src/lib/work-groups.ts`, `views/chat/`): the Persona main conversation, ordinary conversations and Agent sessions share one compact execution presentation (#2602), regardless of visual style or the page used to open the conversation.
  While a turn runs, tools, thinking and intermediate narration stay behind one **Working…** summary line with a timer, collapsed by default. Only the latest assistant text segment is visible outside it; a newer segment replaces that text in the same DOM slot. Streamed text supersedes the persisted latest text rather than adding a second answer.
  At completion the final result occupies that slot, and intermediate text/tools stay in one **Worked for Xs** summary (**Work details** when its times are unknown). The completed label starts at the prose edge and its disclosure arrow follows the words. Text length, headings, lists, tables and inline images do not exempt intermediate narration from folding. A manual open/close choice holds during the run; completion collapses the summary, and manual inspection remains available afterwards and after history reload. Even a single running tool can be opened. Open summaries fetch the hub's `fold_work` ranges by `from_seq` / `through_seq`, the inner summaries' too; folded summaries do not fetch them just to preview tools.
  **Inside an opened summary, a flat work timeline** (#10247): the manually opened outer summary retains its collapsed default, whole-exchange clock and one latest-text slot. Narration and action groups share one indentation and one rail. Each action group names up to three kinds in first-seen order, joined by middle dots, with the first kind's icon: read, edit, search and command calls use localized counts; other tools keep their existing labels. File actions count distinct known paths (a call without a path counts once); edits combine Edit/Write/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit paths, and other kinds count calls. During execution earlier action groups start collapsed and the current group opens only inside the trace the reader chose to inspect; a superseded current group closes. Each remains manually inspectable. Completed history uses the same flat sequence and retains group disclosure choices; newly loaded completed groups start open. The current run previews non-error edit diffs through the existing renderer (first 40 lines; the edit row still opens all changes). Search and jump-to-step explicitly open every group holding the target, and opening the outer summary fetches folded history even in closed action groups. Without intermediate narration, rows stay directly in the outer summary. Compaction and history gaps retain their existing boundaries. Latest narration and the final reply each appear once.
  Held back by super rule 2: cindy's running preview of the latest five activities, its narration in the open while the turn runs, and its inner summaries folded by default (exception requested in #5162).
  **A long summary opens a screenful at a time** (web usability audit 2026-11-14, item 90; `views/chat/work-budget.ts`): a finished summary's steps, its inner summaries' included, are drawn in order up to a budget that starts at 60 steps when it opens and grows by 60 whenever the page is idle (`requestIdleCallback`, at most 250 ms later; each batch its own interruptible render), so the tap is answered at once and a fold of 650 commands (about 8,000 elements) no longer blocks a phone for most of a second. Rows already drawn stay; steps a fetched fold brings in follow in the next batches. A live summary draws everything (its newest step shows at once), and stays that way after the run ends while it is open. A summary asked to show a row in it draws all of it at once, so the row is there to land on in the same update: a search hit inside it (`revealItem`, `useReveal`) and a jump to a call in it ("Jump to the step that started it", a subagent's or a child session's link: `seekCall` → `openToCall` → `openExpanded`, which the budget listens to through `onOpenedOutside`); ChatView's `jumpToCall` gives the row 40 frames to appear, which drawing batch by batch did not meet (MOCK_BIG, a dev build at 4x CPU throttling: step 600's row 52 frames after the jump opened the fold, now in the first). Measured on a production build at 4x CPU throttling (MOCK_BIG, 1440 x 900, five runs each): the long tasks after the tap went from 4–5 (256–515 ms in all, the longest 75–120 ms) to none in most runs and at most one of about 60 ms, and the slowest of the taps made during the next second from 88–120 ms to 48–56 ms.
  **Durations** (`workDuration`, cindy's `formatSessionDuration`) read `6s`, `1m 5s`, `2m` in every language (from each catalog), at least `1s`; from an hour on, the language's form with the minutes always kept: `1h 0m` / `1 小时 0 分` / `1時間0分`, `1d 2h 5m` / `1 天 2 小时 5 分` / `1日2時間5分`. Summaries, their clocks, subagent and workflow cards use it; the run bar keeps its own format (`lib/format.ts` `duration`).
  Tool-backed plan, subagent and workflow cards are inspectable inside the summary, a running subagent's card too (super rule 2; cindy keeps a running subagent's card and a workflow card in the open, which waits on the rule's amendment, #5047). Question and approval panels remain directly actionable. Compaction dividers and unloaded history gaps retain their boundaries. Browser regression: `node web/e2e/compact-execution.mjs <loopback web URL> <screenshot directory>` checks main/ordinary/Agent conversations at desktop and phone widths, light and dark, including live replacement, completion, manual inspection and reload using synthetic HTTP/WebSocket data only.
  - **Tool rows** (`ActionRow`): `[status][verb][argument][+N -N][›]` (an ASCII minus, as cindy's, also in the diff overlay's header); verbs are Edit / Create / Run / Read / Search / Visit / Call. Persona's own MCP tools (`mcp__persona__*`, #2896, the same table as iOS `PersonaToolNames`, `personaToolVerb` in `lib/turns.ts`) use their own verbs (read Agent chat, search knowledge base, remind, control computer…; `phone_*` / `mail_*` are "iPhone" / "Mail" + what was done); unmapped ones still read "Call Persona · <tool name>". Another server's MCP tool reads "Called <Server> · <Tool>" in words ("GitHub · Create issue", `toolDisplayName`); Claude Code's newer tools (task list, `SendMessage`, `Monitor`, `LSP`, worktrees, `Cron*`…) have done-form verbs of their own (`DONE`, iOS `ToolPresentation.knownVerb`), and any other call opens to its arguments as `key: value` lines rather than JSON (#2986). Command rows lead with the command on one truncated line, with their description in the tooltip and expanded detail; search rows show the query and available path or glob; file arguments are small chips with just the file name. Command-type rows expand in place (input, a divider in the tool ink at 20 %, output, untruncated); Edit / Write / MultiEdit open a diff overlay. Only calls with reliable transcript spans of at least 30 seconds show a duration (on compact layouts, in the tooltip); the run bar and collapsed summary retain the total turn clock. A call that ran and failed keeps its red ✕ and red output (#4303), which cindy's rows do not have.
  - **Thoughts** (`ThinkingRow.tsx`, cindy's `ThinkingActivityRow`, #5155; loaded with an opened summary, off the first screen): a thought with words is one row in the tool rows' chrome (`ROW_CHROME`: the 16 px status slot with the sparkle at 13, the 18 px chevron slot), its words in italic in `--chat-secondary` and `text-thinking-ink`, on one line with the whole thought as the title; paired `**strong**` reads in medium weight and backtick code in monospace, as cindy's `ThinkingText` (`lib/thinking-text.ts`; nothing else is interpreted, and the title drops the markers). It opens in place to the whole text (`whitespace-pre-wrap`, top-aligned) only when it does not fit or has a line break (measured with a ResizeObserver), remembered per chat (`useExpanded`); a search hit opens it. The row is a `div` with the button role (Enter and Space toggle it), so opened words can be selected and copied, and a click that ends a selection does not fold it. A thought without words is no step at all (`work-groups.ts` leaves it out before grouping, as cindy draws none): Claude Code mostly writes thoughts without words, and "Thought for 1s" said nothing, so a turn of nothing else has no summary and such a thought never splits a run of rows. While the agent thinks, the last line of the innermost live summary shows **Thinking** + three dots + a clock (from live status), once.
  - **Plan** (`PlanCard`, TodoWrite, #5156: the owner asked on 2026-11-12 that the plan follow cindy's `InlinePlanCard` and `TodoListCard` exactly): one card per exchange, where its latest list of two or more items was written (`planCardStep`, the same rule as the pill's `latestPlan`, `isPlanList` in `lib/work-groups.ts`; the earlier updates and lists of one item are ordinary rows, each inspectable: cindy drops them, super rule 2 keeps every tool call inspectable; a plan update, row or card, keeps a group from being titled "Read N files"). A 12 px rounded (`rounded-xl`), bordered card whose head reads `› ☰ 2/5 · <the step in progress, else the last>` (done / total in monospace; the chevron turns down while it is open). It starts open on the whole list (`Collapse`, as every fold in the chat), not remembered: done steps a check in a circle, dimmed; the one in progress an arc on the same circle, its text medium, turning only while the turn runs and never with reduced motion; pending ones an empty circle. Clicking the head closes it to the head and a 2 px bar of how many are done. There is no side panel for the plan. Like every tool call it stays inside the folded summary (super rule 2; cindy draws it in the open, the exception is asked in #5162).
    While that card is out of view (scrolled away, or not drawn because its summary is folded), a pill above the input shows a still ring of how far along the current step is and "Step 3 of 5" (step / total, the same words in every language). Hovering it opens the whole list in a flyout above it, centered on the input's column (at least 220, at most 420 px wide, scrolling past 280 px; the step in progress semibold; drawn on the page's body so the box over the input does not clip it); leaving closes it. A click pins it open; a second click, a click outside or Esc closes it: pinned, it is a dialog on the overlay Escape stack (`useEscapeClose`), so Esc closes a menu or dialog opened over it first and never stops a running turn. Tab goes from the pill to the flyout's ✕. The pill keeps one place in the dock whether "Jump to bottom" sits beside it or the phone is on its side, so a pinned flyout stays. The ✕ (**Close Plan**) hides the pill for this plan until the plan changes (a step done, a new plan), kept per chat for the page's life, as cindy's. As in cindy, the pill is gone once every step is done, and once a later message of the user's started another turn (`latestPlan` `superseded`; what Persona typed in, another session's message, a supervision round or a queued message start none). The card and the pill load on demand, off the first screen (`views/chat/PlanCard.tsx`, taken lazily by `WorkGroup` and `ChatView`); what the chat reads on every render, the newest plan, whether its card is in view and Close Plan, is `views/chat/latest-plan.ts`. Screenshot fixture: `MOCK_PLAN_CARDS=1`.
  - **Subagents** (`SubagentCard` on the shared `TaskCard`, #5030: the owner asked that this part of the chat follow cindy's `AgentTaskCard` exactly): each Task / Agent call is one full-width card where it was launched, stacked in launch order; no grid and no "Running N agents" wrapper. A subagent is never a conversation of its own: no side panel, no page, no sidebar row.
    The card has two lines. First: a 20 px round avatar, the small word **Subagent**, the title (the call's description, else the subagent's, else its prompt, one line of at most 96 characters; "Subagent task" without any), and the status word with its mark: **Running** (spinner) / **Completed** / **Failed** (the only red one) / **Stopped**, then the chevron. Second, in the tertiary color: **Claude Code** (left out in a Persona conversation, whose reader does not work with the tool), a chip with the model it ran on as a short name ("Haiku 4.5", `modelChipLabel`; the node reads it from the subagent's own transcript, `Subagent.model`, and the model its call asked for is never shown in its place, so an older node shows no chip), "23.4k tokens" (`Subagent.tokens`), "12 tool uses" (`steps`), and how long it took; while it runs, "Running for 1m 5s", counted each second in its own leaf.
    The head opens the card in place, remembered per card under its call (`subagentCardKey`): what it was asked (one line of at most 260 characters), its latest result as plain text (Claude Code's `agentId` line and hand-back frame dropped; past 320 characters or 4 lines it shows 4 lines until **Show full result** / **Collapse result**; a report the hub cut keeps **View full text**), **Last tool: <name>** and **Output: <file>** (a background one's notice names it). Only the latest result shows: a background subagent's interim report until its final one. No list of recent steps.
    Like every tool call, a card sits in its exchange's folded summary, running or not (above). A background subagent's call returns at once with a launch receipt, which is never its result: its card stays **Running** until its report comes back as a notice. Status goes by the call's result (`lib/tasks.ts` `agentStatus`); a background one follows the session list. Subagents a subagent launched are not a tree: each is a card of its own among the exchange's steps by when it started (`withNestedSubagents`; status from the list alone).
    Old links to a subagent's conversation (`/s/<machine>/<parent>@<agent>`, an "agent" panel or a link in a message for one) open the parent's chat and bring that subagent's card into view, opened (`lib/subagent-link.ts`); a workflow agent's link, its run's card. cindy's **Stop** on a card and **Stop all** on the bar are not shown: the node cannot yet stop one subagent of a Claude Code running in a terminal (#5044).
    The screenshot fixture is `MOCK_SUBAGENT_CARDS=1` (finished and nested cards, a running background one, and a second chat whose turn ended while a background subagent runs); `scripts/test/web_chat_trace_e2e.py` checks them at desktop and phone widths, light and dark.
  - **Child sessions** (`ChildSessionCard` on the same `TaskCard`, #5120, after cindy): a session another Agent started (a Codex subagent, an Agent a Paseo Agent created; `folded_under` names this chat) is a subagent card in this chat, never a conversation of its own. Its parent's transcript names no call for it (a Codex parent's has only "Codex event" notices), so the card is built from the child's own row (`lib/use-child-sessions.ts`: the store's rows, or on a paging hub `GET /sessions?machine_id=&parent_session_id=&summary=1`, read only while the parent has `children`) and placed by when the child started (`started_at`, `lib/child-cards.ts`): in the exchange that was going on then, after the last step that started before it, inside that exchange's work summary (super rule 2). One that started after the last exchange goes into the latest; one that started before the loaded history shows once that history is loaded. Grandchildren are cards of their own, as nested subagents are.
    The card's lines are a subagent card's: **Subagent**, the child's title, its status (**Running** while it works or waits for you, **Failed** with a turn error, **Stopped** when interrupted, else **Completed**), then what runs it (Codex, Claude Code…; left out in a Persona conversation), a chip with its model and effort ("GPT-5.5 · High") and how long it took, or **Running for …**. A child row carries no token total, so no tokens show. Opened (remembered per card), it reads the child's transcript then, and only while open: what it was asked (its first message), its latest words (four lines until **Show full result**) and **Last tool: …**; the row's last words stand in while that loads. No link opens the child's own conversation.
    A child's requests (its approvals and questions; `folded_under` on the card) are on this chat's page with its own, answered there, each saying **From subagent · <its title>**. Old links to a child (`/s/<machine>/<child>`, an "agent" panel for one) open this chat with the child's card opened and in view, loading earlier history if the card is not placed yet. The screenshot fixture is `MOCK_CHILD_SESSIONS=1` (a Paseo lead with four created Agents, one waiting for you, one with a Codex subagent of its own, one done, one failed, and an Agent whose creator is not listed); `scripts/test/web_child_sessions_e2e.py` checks the list, the cards, the request and an old link at desktop and phone widths, light and dark, and with `--paged` on a paging hub.
  - **User bubbles** are right-aligned, at most 488 wide, and anything over 14 lines collapses to 10. Your own messages (input, dictation, quick commands) use iOS Agents' pale blue `--user-bubble` (`#dceaff` light, `#1d3557` dark, #2672 / #6451); messages forwarded from another Persona chat via conversation_send keep `--neutral-bubble` (`isOwnMessage` still controls alignment and actions in `lib/turns.ts`). Replies have no bubble; body text is 15 / 1.6, code blocks are highlighted with highlight.js (loaded on demand) and wrap. A table has the same kind of copy button as a code block (`web/src/ui/Markdown.tsx`): hidden until hover or keyboard focus, and shown on a screen with no hover. It puts tab-separated cells on the clipboard, so they paste into a spreadsheet as cells, and the table's HTML, so a document keeps the table. The button never covers header words (web usability audit 2026-11-14, item 77): the last header cell keeps room for it (`.md-table th:last-child`), and it sits on a cap the header row's height and `--inset` color with a short fade on its left, so the header words of a wide table scrolled under it fade out at the edge; the cap shows and hides with the button. The table's margins and scroll do not change. The button is placed from the table's ResizeObserver, so opening a long chat does not measure every table (#2905). Columns are as narrow as their words: headers never wrap and have no minimum width, a cell whose words fit on one line in about 5.5em (`cellFits`: a CJK, full-width or emoji character counts 1em, any other about half; never one with a line break or a picture) is marked `data-fit` and stays on one line with no minimum, and only longer cells keep the 7em minimum, so a squeezed table does not stack a sentence a word per line while a "#" column takes 28 px instead of 91.
  - **The hover bar beside your bubbles** (with a pointer: the time when it is not the latest, Copy message, Quote, Edit, ⋯): to the left of the bubble, 6 px away, where it fits inside what shows the chat; where a narrow window leaves a wide bubble no room there, the same buttons sit under the bubble, right-aligned, as a small floating bar (`rounded-control`, `bg-surface`, `shadow-hairline`) over what comes next (web usability audit 2026-11-14, item 73: at 390 px Copy and Quote sat at x = -50 and -24, and Tab focused them out of sight). Where it goes is measured when the pointer comes or focus moves into the bubble's row (`sideBarFits` in `views/chat/MessageActions.tsx`), not for every bubble as a chat opens, and only its classes change, so the button Tab reached keeps the focus. Hidden, the bar under a bubble takes no clicks (`pointer-events-none` until the bubble is hovered or the bar has the focus); a transparent bridge over its 4 px gap keeps the hover while the pointer goes down to it. The chat column is 880 wide; its items stand 14 px apart under 28 px of top padding, and an exchange's blocks 14 px apart too, as cindy's stream (`msg-stream-items gap-3.5`, `pt-7`; #5155).
  - **Model change divider** (#5034, `lib/model-change.ts`, `views/chat/ModelChangeDivider.tsx`, after cindy's model-only switch chip at the user's request, 2026-11-12): when an exchange's reply came from another model than the previous visible reply, a line across the chat with a centered chip `⇄ Opus 5.5 → Sonnet 4.5` (11 px, `--ink-3`, a `--line-strong` hairline and border, `bg-page/50`) stands between that exchange's message and its reply, as cindy puts it after the message that started the turn.
    The model is what the transcript says wrote the reply (`Item.model`: Claude Code's `message.model`, a Codex turn's `turn_context`; `../protocol/protocol.md`), never the model picker: a switch shows once the new model has answered, and only then. A reply's model is that of the exchange's latest assistant item that names one (its answer and every step, tool calls included, by `seq`), so work a fallback model did after the last words counts; a reply whose model is unknown (an older node, Claude Code's own `<synthetic>` lines such as API errors) gets no line and does not end the run, so the next known reply is compared with the last known one. Folded rounds (supervision, background) are not visible replies and are skipped; nothing is drawn inside an exchange, so a fallback halfway through a turn shows once, before that exchange's reply. Only the loaded pages are compared: the first exchange of a page after a switch gets its line once the older page is loaded.
    Names: Claude ids read as Claude Code names them (`claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929` → "Sonnet 4.5", `modelShort` capitalized), raw GPT ids as the model lists show them (`modelName`), any other id as it is. Models are compared by a canonical id: lowercase, without a gateway's vendor path (`vendor/glm-5.1`), Bedrock's region and vendor prefix and `-v1:0` suffix, Vertex's `@<date>` or a trailing `-YYYYMMDD`, so an alias, a pinned snapshot and Bedrock's or Vertex's form of one model are no change (`us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-v1:0` reads "Sonnet 4.5"); a `[1m]` suffix stays, as it names another model ("Opus 5.5 1M"). Two ids the chat names alike are one model too. Each id is worked out once (`modelIdentity`, at most 256 kept). The exchange's guessed height off screen ("Long chats") includes the divider (`MODEL_DIVIDER_HEIGHT`, 42.5 px as drawn, plus the 14 px gap). The ids are in the chip's hover text; screen readers hear "Model changed from … to …" (`role="separator"`). It is not a control. Deviation from cindy: names instead of raw ids, as Persona never shows raw model ids on primary screens.
    Mock: `MOCK_MODEL_CHANGE=1` gives the recipes agent two exchanges answered by Opus, then Sonnet.
  - **Engine switch divider** (#5054, `lib/engine-switch.ts`, `views/chat/EngineSwitchDivider.tsx`, after cindy's agent switch card at the user's request, 2026-11-12): above the first message the conversation's other engine got (its text carries the `<persona-context kind="engine-switch">` handoff block, "Switching an Agent between Claude Code and Codex" below), a line across the chat with a centered chip `⇄ Switched from Claude Code to Codex · 5.5 · Continued from summary ›`: the same row as the model change divider (two `--line-strong` hairlines, 11 px `--ink-3`, a `--line-strong` border, `bg-page/50`, padding 10 × 4), the model the new engine runs as the chat names models (its id on hover), a badge, **session resumed** when the conversation's earlier session of that engine was resumed (the block's `resumed="1"`), else **Continued from summary**, and a chevron that turns when open. The block is never a context chip, and that exchange gets no model change line (the next one is compared with it); only a block that moves between the two known engines (`from` and `to` are `claude` and `codex`, different) draws the divider, any other stays an ordinary context chip. The chip is a button ("View handoff context") when the block has text: it opens a panel under the line (a `rounded-card` box, `--line-strong` border, `bg-inset`, 16 × 12 padding; an 11 px medium title "Handoff — the context summary sent to the new engine at switch time (not part of the chat transcript; shown only here)", then the handoff in 12 / 1.55 monospace `--tool-ink`, at most 16 rem high and scrolling, selectable), open or closed remembered per divider; a handoff the hub cut for the page (over 24 KB) offers **View full text**. Screen readers hear "Switched from Claude Code to Codex" (`role="separator"` on the line) and the chip as a button with `aria-expanded`. Under 640 px the chip reads "Claude Code → Codex · <badge>" (no model), so the badge keeps room. Its folded height (`ENGINE_DIVIDER_HEIGHT`, 42.5 px) counts in the off-screen estimate. Deviations from cindy: the model's name rather than its raw monospace id (as the model change divider), the badge always shown (cindy shows it only on a resume or a fallback), the separator role on the line rather than around the button, and the narrow form.
  - **Live status and streaming**: while an Agent works, the run status bar above the input follows cindy's `RunningStatusBar` (#5312; the owner asked on 2026-11-12 that this part of the chat follow cindy, and where this doc said otherwise, cindy wins; layout and words in `docs/design/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md` "Run status bar").
