  **Declarative UI** (#1330, `settings/ExtensionView.tsx`, logic in `lib/extension-ui.ts`, `docs/extensions/extensions.md` ("Declarative UI")): extension details add a Pages group (its `ui`); opening one goes to `&extension=<id>/ui/<page>`.
  One component renders all eight item types: text (four styles), metric (consecutive items side by side), progress, row (badge, clickable), button (consecutive buttons in one row, destructive in red text, submit as the primary button), link (https only, opened with `openLink`), field (text, secret without echoing, number, toggle, choice), divider.
  Tones map to role colors (neutral → accent / body color, positive → green, caution → orange, danger → red). Buttons with `confirm` first open a confirmation dialog; `submit` sends every field value on the page (toggles as `"true"` / `"false"`; no request if a number is not numeric).
  A new view in the response replaces the old one, `toast` shows a toast, and `open_url` uses the web's link-opening behavior; with none of these, redraw. A rendering failure shows an empty state with Retry.
  In launcher details under Model providers, when the hub has the extension foundation, `GET /extensions/-/ui?placement=launcher_section&launcher=<name>[&machine=<first online computer>]` adds one section per extension (titled with the name supplied by the extension).
  If the extension returns 404 `{"code": "unsupported"}` while rendering (a section without `hosts` is listed on every launcher, and the extension says this is not its gateway, #1339), hide the whole section; it is not an error and shows no error message.
  **UI slots** (#1451, `docs/extensions/extensions.md` ("UI slots"); list and badges in `lib/extension-slots.ts`, rendering for the three placements in `views/extensions/ExtensionSlots.tsx`, charts in `views/extensions/ExtensionChart.tsx`, logic in `lib/extension-ui.ts`):
  Only queried when hub features contain `extension_ui_slots` (`plugin_ui_slots` on old hubs). `GET /extensions/-/ui` (without placement) fetches all slots at once; fetch again on reconnect (hello), after enabling / disabling / changing settings / installing / upgrading / removing an extension here, and when the tab returns to the foreground after more than a minute.
  `nav_page` adds one sidebar row per page between Machines and Settings (every name of the fixed icon set, `NavIcon`, is mapped to the web icon a row draws for it, from the one table in `views/extensions/icon-map.ts` (#16281); unknown ones use the extension icon. Badge color follows tone; `extension_ui` events (`plugin_ui` on old hubs) update it in place without refetching), opening `/extension/<extension>/<page>`.
  `overview_card` is a row of cards at the end of Overview, under the agents' sections (Needs you, Stuck, the tasks, Working, Waiting in the background, Unread) and **Computers**: the owner's own agents and computers stay on the first screen however many cards there are (#11147; #11092 first moved the cards under Needs you and Stuck) (one fills the width, multiple cards use two columns; once the page is wide enough for two columns of rows, 60rem as the agent sections above it, a lone card takes one of them, so its chart is not stretched across a wide page: 540 px of a 1440 px window, 780 px at 1920, web audit item 76), rendered compactly (`context.size: compact`), under a heading like the page's other sections (**Extensions** and the number of cards) with **Collapse** / **Expand** at its right: the fold is kept per browser (`useFolded`, `fold:overview-cards`), open until the owner folds it, and folded no card is mounted or asked for (#11148); clicking the blank area or title opens `opens`, while buttons, rows, and charts within the card remain clickable. A card that opens a page shows at most 18.75rem of its view (`CARD_MAX` in `views/extensions/ExtensionSlots.tsx`: a stat grid with its chart, or a stat grid and three rows; in rem, so it follows the text size): a taller view is cut there, its last 2.75rem fading out, with **See all** at the card's foot opening the page, so one long list does not make its whole row twice as tall; whether a view is taller is measured (a `ResizeObserver`), and a card without `opens` is never cut, since nothing else would show the rest (#11149). A card's heading has its title and, at the right, the extension's name, left out when it only says the title again (`nameBesideTitle` in `views/extensions/ExtensionSlots.tsx`, case and surrounding spaces ignored; the same rule as an extension page's top bar and a machine section's heading, #10940). The cards come in the hub's order (by extension, then the manifest's) unless the user arranged them (below).
  **Overview's extension cards** (#9745, `lib/overview-cards.ts`, `views/extensions/OverviewArrange.tsx`, `docs/design/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md` "Arranging cards in place"): the user arranges the cards on Overview itself, and Overview's own sections with them (#10905, below). **Arrange Overview** (the grid button beside **New agent** in Overview's top bar, there always: there are always the sections to arrange) turns the page under the greeting into its edit state (folded rows of cards open, without their **Collapse** / **Expand** until **Done**): a heading says what to do and where the arrangement is kept, with **Reset** (once something is arranged; Undo in its toast, which leaves an arrangement changed since, here, in another tab or on another device, even one reset again, alone and says so) and **Done**; each card shows a handle and its name in place of its head, its width (**Half row**, the default, or **Full row**), ↑ / ↓ (earlier / later, for the keyboard and touch) and a switch (on: shown). A card dragged onto another takes its place, as the sidebar's pages are dragged (Settings › General › Sidebar pages).
  While arranging, a card's content stays drawn (nothing is asked again) but takes no click or focus (`inert`); a hidden card is drawn in its place as its outline, "Hidden: not loaded", and outside the edit state not at all, so its `render` is never asked for (nor is it counted in its row's heading). A full-row card takes every column; half-row cards go two a row from `md` once two of them are drawn, and a lone one keeps item 76's rule (the whole row until the page has 60rem, one column after). Cards the arrangement does not name (an extension installed since) come after the named ones, half a row and shown, in the hub's order; an entry for a card that is not there now is passed over, and dropped only when the user changes the arrangement. With nothing arranged, Overview is what it was.
  Overview's own sections (#10905, `views/OverviewBody.tsx`): Needs you, Stuck, Tasks in progress, Working, Unread and Computers are entries of the same arrangement, so the user can put Tasks in progress right under the greeting, above Needs you, and every device keeps it. While arranging, each is drawn in its place as a bar the row's width (its handle and name, ↑ / ↓, its switch; even with no rows now), dragged and moved like a card and among the cards; a hidden one is its outline, and outside the edit state not drawn. Needs you and Stuck have no switch and say they are always shown: their rows need the user (`docs/design/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md` 3.4). The greeting and its summary stay first. With nothing arranged, Overview is its default (#11147): the sections in their order, then the cards. A section the arrangement does not name (one added since) comes right after the one before it by default (Needs you: first), so a section the user put first stays first; cards it does not name, when it names none, come at the end, where the cards are by default. The cards between two sections are a row of their own, laid out as above, with its own heading and the number of its cards shown; the rows fold as one (`fold:overview-cards`, held by `views/OverviewBody.tsx`), so folding one folds them all; "Loading" comes where the sections begin and the card that says all is quiet (or how to add a computer) after Unread's place, drawn or not. A change writes the sections only once one is moved or hidden (then all of them, until Reset), so arranging only the cards still suits a default manager from before the sections; one from then refuses a list that names one, and the web then sends the cards on their own, at once and with each change, so they still follow on every device, while the sections' order stays in this browser (noted per hub and sign-in, laid over the cards the hub sends by the manager's own `keepSections` rule) and the edit heading says so; each hello that did not resume asks again with the sections, and once the manager takes them (or the hub sends a list that names one) they go with every change again. A section this web does not have (a newer web's) stays where it was in what it writes.
  The arrangement is the user's on the hub (`overview` of `GET` / `PUT /api/v1/navigation`, `docs/protocol/protocol.md` "Navigation"), carried as the sidebar's is (`lib/start-page.ts`): read at the hello and on each push, sent on each change, a change the hub did not take (403, 5xx, the network, any other 400) sent again at the next hello rather than replaced, by that hello's read or by a push heard before it; one taken but answered after a hello that did not resume (its push may have gone with the old socket) lets the newest push heard since be taken. A push heard while a change of this browser's is on its way is settled once that change is answered and the hub's push of it is heard (the answer can come first): the hub pushes every change, this browser's too, in its order, so one pushed after ours is newer and is taken, and one before it is not. Ours is found among the pushes card by card, since the hub passes a push on with each card's keys in its own order; a hello that did not resume ends the wait, its read standing for the pushes that went with the socket. Changes go one at a time: one made while another is on its way goes once that one is answered, the newest as this browser has it then, so the last answer says whether the newest reached the hub; and a hello's read that a change made or sent here overtook is not taken over it, nor one a push or another tab's change overtook (nor is this browser's handed over then), nor one a later hello or another sign-in overtook. This browser's copy is kept per hub and sign-in (`overview.cards` under `lib/feed-cache.ts`'s `scopedKey`, removed at sign-out), so another hub or account in the same browser neither draws it nor hands it over; so is what is on its way: when the sign-in changes (`feedCacheScope`), a change sent, queued or not taken under the earlier one is dropped, its answer or failure changes nothing and sends nothing under the new one, whose own hello reads its own arrangement, and a push the earlier one's socket passes on before that hello is not taken; an arrangement made here before the hub kept one is handed over once. It is sent on its own, so a hub (or default manager) without the route (404), or a default manager from before the field (its own 400 for a PUT of only it, `start is required` or `start or pages is required`, or an answer without the field), leaves it in this browser, and the edit state's heading says so in the sidebar setting's words; the next hello that did not resume asks again. iOS and Android show the cards above Settings › Extensions in the hub's order; following the arrangement there is a separate change. Check: `node web/e2e/overview-cards.mjs` (`web/e2e/README.md`).
  `machine_section` adds one section per extension at the end of the machine page (after launchers), with `context.machine`. Every render and action carries `context: {tz, locale, platform: "web", ui_version: 11, …}`.
  Unknown items are skipped; a section emptied by skipping is removed (kept if it has a footer). Only failure to read the whole View shows an error. `chart` renders SVG bar charts (grouped / stacked, bars at most 24px wide, rounding on the free end, 2px gaps between stacked segments) and line charts.
  Hover or arrow keys show each series' value under that label; x-axis labels appear at intervals without overlapping, with only the first and last labels in compact mode. Series without a tone use `--series-1…4` (the first is the primary color, avoiding the green / orange / red role colors, with light and dark sets).
  `stat_grid` uses 2 items per row when narrow, 3 when wider, and all items in one row when very wide; selecting a `segmented` item immediately sends `ui.action` (`values: {name: selected value}`). `refresh_after` redraws on schedule only while the page is visible and the component is present; if overdue on return to the foreground, redraw immediately.
  Screenshots use the `MOCK_EXTENSIONS=1` mock hub (`example-gateway`'s usage page, today's usage card, and Gateway calls on the machine page).
  **UI version 4: code hosting** (#2951, `docs/extensions/extensions.md` ("UI version 4: code hosting"); rendering in `views/extensions/CodeViews.tsx`, logic in `lib/code-view.ts`): `diff` supports unified / side-by-side (side-by-side only at ≥1024px,
  preference stored in this browser), inline comment threads, clicking a line number to open a comment editor, and Expand between hunks. `code` and `diff` are highlighted with lowlight (highlight.js's common languages, loaded on the first code render), using the page's color tokens.
  `layout: split` uses a left column on wide screens (kept in view) and an expandable "Files · N" bar at the top on narrow screens; `tabs` is a row of tabs below the title. When the View contains `split`, `code`, or `diff`, extension pages opened from the sidebar use full page width (`max-w-[1680px]`; others remain 880).
  Long files and diffs off-screen use `content-visibility: auto` and do not incur layout work.
  **UI version 5: code review** (#3136, `docs/extensions/extensions.md` ("UI version 5: code review"); diffs rendered in `views/extensions/DiffReview.tsx`, logic in `lib/code-review.ts`, page state in `views/extensions/review-context.ts`):
  word-level highlighting, fetching lines via `context` to expand between hunks (cached per file, without redrawing the page), viewed state (`mark_viewed`, or stored as `path@revision` in this browser), generated / large / viewed files initially collapsed, drag-selecting line numbers to comment, drafts and a bottom review bar, suggestions,
  ignore whitespace (stored in this browser), "Viewed x / y" and "N unresolved" at the top, and shortcuts (`?` to see all). `context`, `mark_viewed`, and automatic `load` when scrolled nearby use `ExtensionView`'s quiet requests (do not take busy); response `items` replace components in place.
  **UI version 3** (#1850, `docs/extensions/extensions.md` ("Declarative UI"); rendering in `views/extensions/ViewBody.tsx`, loading and navigation in `settings/ExtensionView.tsx`, parsing in `lib/extension-ui.ts`):
  `markdown` renders only a safe subset (headings, paragraphs, lists, emphasis, code, quotes, https links; no HTML or images, links open inside the web app). `table` scrolls horizontally when narrow and cells do not wrap; `empty` is an empty state with a button; `loading` is a one-line spinner.
  Rows can carry a fixed icon (`icon`, mapped to a web icon), avatar (https image, falls back to initials on load failure), or thumbnail (https, no credentials). Component `key` becomes the React key, keeping the list in place on redraw.
  A View's `search` is the search box at the top (sends `values: {q}` after a 0.3-second pause); `filter` is the adjacent dropdown (sends immediately on selection, together with `q`). A section's `more` is a final Load more row, automatically queried once when scrolled into view (once per new View), and also clickable.
  An action's `push` does not ask the extension; it directly pushes a page on this view's own page stack (renders that `ui` with `state`); `push` / `pop` in responses work the same way. The stack is at most 8 levels; on full pages, browser Back returns to the previous page, with "‹ Previous page title" at the top.
  Cards and sections embedded in other pages (Overview, machine page, launcher page) have no stack: push opens the extension's full page `/extension/<extension>/<page>?state=…`. `extension_ui {invalidate}` redraws the currently visible page (at most once per second); off-screen pages wait until visible again.

The cards reach the renderer through `views/extensions/view-sections-lazy.tsx`: `ViewBody.tsx` is a chunk of its own, fetched once the browser is idle after start or by the first card drawn before then, which shows its sections' boxes meanwhile (#3614).

  **Transitions on redraw** (#2757, `ui/motion.ts`, `ui/Rolling.tsx`, shared with the workflow cards since #3434): when an extension draws the same page again, a `metric`, `stat_grid` or row value under the same key whose numbers alone changed counts from the old number to the new one (600 ms, the `EASE` curve; only the digits move, so `2/8` and `¥1.20` keep their shape, and every frame keeps the value's decimals, thousands grouping and zero padding).

  "Usage · <gateway name>" (for non-direct API integrations, #1326, `settings/LauncherQuota.tsx`, logic in `lib/quota.ts`, matching iOS `LauncherQuotaSection`: budget, each account / provider's windows and progress bars (orange at ≥ 70%, red at ≥ 90% or exhausted), collapsed by model, this Key's usage, top-right refresh with `refresh=1`, `docs/integrations/launchers.md` ("Quota")),

Adding first lists the hub's provider presets (built-in and extension-provided; select, paste only a Key, test automatically, `assign` on save); Custom compatible gateway comes last (launcher or direct API, Messages / Responses): its Connect step starts with a **Display name** in any language (at most 64 characters; left empty, a hub with `launcher_auto_name` names it after the address's host) and keeps the **Startup ID** under More options, where the hub makes one up when it is left empty and its format is checked only once something is typed (an older hub still needs the ID, shown under the display name). **Next** with something missing or wrong says it under each field it is about (`aria-invalid`, a red edge; `connectProblems` in `lib/providers.ts`), opens More options when the startup ID is among them, and focuses the first such field and scrolls it into view inside the dialog (audit item 19); a problem no field holds still shows above the buttons. The gateway's sign-in method (Bearer or x-api-key) is found by the step's own check and named in one line of its check box; the choice sits under More options too, and editing names and tests the stored one (#5329, `docs/integrations/launchers.md` "Authentication method"). The optional **Request headers** editor is visible on **Connect** before the automatic/manual connection test and model discovery, for add and edit and for every direct protocol. It shows configured `header_names` without saved values, supports replacement and explicit removal, explains each runtime's support or limitation before checks, and rechecks after a header-only edit. Reserved protocol/credential fields and unsupported runtime combinations stop checks and saves. The real-Chrome add/edit, replacement/removal, runtime, no-header, light/dark, phone/desktop and large-text matrix is `node web/e2e/provider-headers.mjs <artifact-dir>` (screenshots and results stay outside the repository). Editing renames a provider; its startup ID is read-only with the reason (#5029, `docs/integrations/launchers.md` "Display names"). Every place that names a provider leads with its display name and shows the ID as secondary text (`lib/provider-names.ts`, `docs/design/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md` "Provider display names (#5029)"). **Import** sits in the header between the search field and **Add provider** (icon only at phone width) and opens **Import from your computer's aliases** (#5024, `settings/ProviderImport.tsx`, logic in `lib/providers.ts`): pick a computer, then each provider its claude aliases in `~/.zshrc`, `~/.bashrc` and `~/.bash_aliases` add up to, under the name it will be saved as (`create_as`: an alias Persona already lists becomes `<alias>-2`), with the file each alias came from, the environment variables it carries over and the ones it leaves out by reason; a group whose aliases set more than the model differently says what differs and offers **A provider for each alias** (the default, listing what each becomes) or **One provider**. Below the list, **Hide the imported aliases in Persona** (on by default; shell files are not changed) names the aliases it hides and why each other one stays; the note that merging only adds models shows only when the picked groups, as chosen, merge into a provider that is there. With no computer the dialog explains instead of showing the picker (`docs/integrations/launchers.md` ("Adding from extensions")).
  Import links (#5420, [launchers.md](../integrations/launchers.md) "Import links"): opening `<web address>/settings?tab=models#import=<data>` takes the fragment out of the address bar and the Back list at load, first thing in `main.tsx`, before the language catalog loads (`takeImportLink` in `lib/import-link.ts`, kept apart from the link builder `lib/provider-link.ts` so only it is on the first screen; a link on another path or tab lands on `?tab=models`, and other fragment parameters such as a sign-in `token` stay for `takeToken`). A link pasted into the address bar of a page already open fires only `hashchange`: it is taken then, through the router when the address changes. It is kept in memory only, and opens Add provider on the paste view in its link mode (`ProviderPaste.tsx`): no text box, a line that it was opened from a link and that nothing is saved until Save, **Paste something else**, and the link read at once by the parse route; its drafts, matches and notes show as a paste's do. Signing in first keeps it in memory until Settings opens; `reloadForSignIn` (a sign-in layer in front of the hub) puts a held link back in the address bar before it reloads; any other reload before Settings takes it drops it. A link arriving while the wizard, the copy dialog or the alias import is open waits until that closes (a toast says so) rather than throw away what is in it. Without the hub's `launcher_import_link` the view says the hub can't open links yet. A Persona-managed Claude Code gateway's or direct Responses / Chat Completions API's dialog has **⋯ › Copy import link** (`ProviderLinkCopy.tsx`): the link carries the name, address and models, no key unless **Put a key in the link** is on and a key is pasted there, under a warning; the hub never returns a stored key. Its strings and the ⋯ menu's are in the lazy `settings-providerlink` catalog, the link view's in `settings-providerpaste`.
  Gateway discovery and connection tests belong to the current wizard opening and connection inputs. Closing, switching providers or changing the URL, type, authentication, key or headers retires pending results and releases their busy state for retry. A late success, error or cleanup cannot alter the current form or its active request. Valid discovery merges into the latest model edits, preserving checked choices and an intentional default; changing only the test model retires its connection test without canceling discovery (#1314).
  Model configuration groups / searches the hub's real purpose catalog, edits provider, specific model, and supported thinking effort, and shows inheritance and currently effective values. Save failures preserve the draft; revision conflicts require reload (`docs/assistant/model-config.md`). A use the hub sets apart from its category (the two meeting uses, #7980) sits right after it ("Meeting uses in Model settings (#7980)" below).

  stored in this browser (same key names as iOS AppStorage). Not synced to the hub: hub translation preferences are tied to the phone's push device id (`/devices/{id}/prefs`, sent by iOS and Android; the hub pre-translates incoming messages accordingly), which the web does not have.
  The web translates on demand when opened, and directly uses any hub-pretranslated content.
  Devices lists each device's token (this browser first), with inline confirmation for revoking. The hub also returns revoked devices (with `revoked_at`); these are not counted in "Devices N",

Settings › Assistant profile (`?tab=persona`, formerly `?tab=assistant`) is the current assistant's identity and behavior, then agent triage; the avatar is Settings › Avatar (`?tab=avatar`), the workflow-board switch is on the hub page, and agent-display preferences, hub connections and this-browser information are under General.   Browser (QR code of the sign-in link `<page address>#token=jp_…`, opened directly by scanning with a phone camera + copy sign-in link), remembering the last choice. At countdown 0, show Expired and Generate again.

  The code expires after 10 minutes and can only be redeemed once. Closing the dialog does not invalidate it (the hub has no endpoint to invalidate temporary codes); it expires naturally.
- **Machines**: a card per computer, with current CPU / memory / disk values and CPU chart for the last hour (`/api/v1/metrics`, refresh every 10 seconds; gaps mean disconnections). Offline machines can reconnect; clicking the name or Details › opens the machine page.

  A wide detail pane keeps a computer list alongside the selected view. Narrow panes use a stack. The Back link retraces in-app navigation, including entry from Overview. Direct links have a parent destination. Browser Back and Forward restore the subview and list position.
  Load is load per core everywhere, one decimal (`perCoreText` / `perCoreLabel` in `src/lib/machine-alerts.ts`, #12519): the card's line under CPU ("Load 1.4 per core", the raw value only without a core count), the chip, the alert sheet and the machine page's Load tile (the raw value, the per-core figure under it).

    At narrow widths the controls can wrap below the phase description as a group. An update that starts elsewhere
    withdraws the open confirmation and shows the current step. The card, detail and alert sheet admit one request per
    computer until the request and its refresh settle. They check the latest machine state again before posting.
  - **Alerts and what fixes them** (#8037, `src/lib/machine-alerts.ts`, `src/views/machines/MachineAlertSheet.tsx` and its `Alert*.tsx` sections): each card has one chip per alert, worst first (offline with its classified reason, a failed update, memory, disk, CPU, load per core, failing launchers, the version), from the thresholds in [machines.md](../server/machines.md) ("App"), the latest metric sample and `GET /api/v1/launchers/health` (kept current by `launcher_health`, read again every minute). A chip is a `<button>` with icon and words (the icon's color says how bad, red only for critical; its `aria-label` starts with the severity), so the card's own click leaves it alone. Pending and never-connected computers keep their notices and get no chips; an offline card keeps its one red notice and its chip reads "Offline · What to check"; the version and a failed update stay in the deployment strip, which gains **Details**. Cards are ordered as the apps' `MachineConcern`: pending, offline, critical, warning, needs you, version, then the hub's order.
    A disk chip opens contextual Storage in reclaim mode. Other chips open the alert sheet (one `Dialog` for the page, outside every card: a centred card on a desktop, a sheet on a phone), with the computer's alerts as tabs and three parts in a fixed order: what is wrong, why, what you can do. Memory, CPU and load: the numbers, the node's largest process groups (`GET /api/v1/machines/{mid}/diagnosis?sections=processes`, share of memory or of the cores, tagged Agent / engine / Persona / other; read only when the sheet opens, so the cards never shift), the computer's Agents as needs you / working / idle with how long; **Stop idle Agents** (a confirmation lists each one; only idle or finished Agents with nothing running, never working or needs-you ones; one at a time through `POST /sessions/{mid}/{sid}/close`, the conversation stays; then "Stopped N of M" with each failure) and **Hand work to another computer**. On computers too old to return a map, Storage uses the earlier disk diagnosis: volumes, the largest folders under home (and that the scan was cut short), the rebuildable caches by name with their path (in-use ones disabled, the rest picked); **Clean selected** → a confirmation naming every folder and the total → `POST …/cleanup {ids}` → the bytes the volume really gained (`freed_bytes`) and each item's outcome, then the diagnosis again. Version / failed update: the hub's build (hello `server_version`) and the node's side by side with their build times and how far apart they are, how many Agents are working; **Redeploy** behind a confirmation, then a stepper the pushed `deploy_phase` drives (waiting for idle → transferring → waiting to restart → restarting → confirming → done with the node's new build), or the error and **Try again**; the hub's reason when it cannot deploy. Offline: the reason, last seen, a numbered checklist per reason, the raw error under **Details**, **Reconnect** and, for a version reason, Redeploy. Launchers: each failing or blocked one (kind, error line, when checked, failures in a row, a usage limit's reset), the ones that work there, **Test again** (`POST /api/v1/launchers/health/check?machine=&launcher=`, the new record in place); the hub has no per-computer default launcher, so the sheet links to Settings › Models instead of switching it.
    A diagnosis the computer or hub cannot give says why and keeps every other action: 409 `node_outdated` "update Persona on this computer" (with Redeploy when the hub can), a 404 without a code "update the hub", 403 "only a fully trusted device", and Retry for the rest (`src/lib/machine-diagnosis.ts`).
    **Hand work to another computer** is the sheet's second step: pick the Agents (the working and idle ones that belong to a to-do are picked), pick a computer from a ranked list (`rankTargets` in `src/lib/machine-capabilities.ts`: offline, unconfirmed and critical ones are not eligible; then fewer alerts, more free memory, the same OS family, the source's tools; each row says why; the best eligible one is picked and marked, none when none is eligible), confirm (source, target, Agents), and one message goes to Persona's main chat through its own send path (`sendToSession` with the chat's launcher and model; with no main chat yet, `askPersona` starts one): continue these to-dos on the target with `continues`, stop the source Agents only after the new ones started, with every computer, session and to-do id. A toast says "Sent to Persona" with **Open chat**.

  Both read Screen Sharing from the machine list, as the top bar does. On page open, query `GET …/computer` once, and every 2 seconds during installation / authorization. The hub has no actions such as reboot (`…/computer/reboot` is 404), and neither does this section.
  Screenshots use the `MOCK_COMPUTER=permissions|missing|ready` mock hub.

### Meeting uses in Model settings (#7980)

Settings › Models lists the two meeting uses the hub sets apart from their categories
([model-config.md](../assistant/model-config.md) "Meeting minutes and the in-meeting conversation (#7980)"):
**In-meeting conversation** in Persona chats · Background process, right after Main chat and the background supervisor,
and **Meeting minutes** in Background processing · Direct API, right after Information processing.

- **Found by data** (`setApartFrom`, `withUsesAfterCategories` in `lib/model-config-execution.ts`): a purpose with fields
  of its own, no `uses`, a `category_id` other than its id and a `parent` that is a category listed in the same group.
  The hub lists them last among its own purposes, so the installed apps keep their order; the page moves each up to its
  category, behind the uses already there.
- **Its row**: the hub's description, the model in effect, and **Follows Main chat** / **Follows Information processing**
  (the background supervisor's words, `follows`, with the category's name as the catalog sends it; an English hub calls
  Information processing **Processing**) while its record is empty,
  **Separately configured** once it has a provider, model or effort of its own (`followedCategory`). The editor says the
  same at its top.
- **Its editor**: the provider list's empty choice and the reset are **Follow Main chat** / **Follow Information
  processing**, and a stale revision keeps the draft and blocks Save and the reset until reloaded, as for every purpose.
  It offers the hub's `provider_ids` only, no Runtime, and effort only for a provider that takes one. For the In-meeting
  conversation a line under the provider list says it runs on Claude Code only. The page knows that by the purpose's id
  (`claudeCodeOnly`, `meeting.room`): it is a fact about that purpose, and the hub sends no field that says it.
  Its reset is longer than **Inherit**, so where the three actions do not fit on one line (日本語's メインチャットに従う at
  320 px, also with Large text; in English, a category name as long as "Information processing" at 320 px, or 360 px with
  Large text) it takes a line of its own above Cancel and Save, its words whole (button labels never wrap); where they
  fit, all three stay where every other editor has them.
- **What every editor of a use with a record of its own does** (the two meeting uses, the AI twin, Lark /agent, the
  background supervisor, an extension's purpose; `ownRecord`, told by the purpose's own `fields` and `category_id`, not
  by the group it is listed in): its reset sends explicit `null` for provider, model and effort with the purpose's
  revision (`resetPatch`), also when the page's catalog did not load, so an effort saved on an earlier provider goes too.
  With its provider cleared, the draft previews what it will follow: the category's provider from the catalog
  (`parentCategory`), with that launcher's model list, the category's model as its **Default**, the backend chip and
  whether it takes an effort. Effort goes by the provider the draft runs on (`effortOffered`): a current hub lists `effort`
  for Messages, Responses and Chat Completions connections and marks Chat providers `chat_effort`. A hub that already
  lists `effort` for the effective Chat provider keeps it available without that mark. Against an older hub that omits
  both for Chat, Meeting minutes offer choices again once a Messages or Responses connection is picked, and Save sends
  them. If an older hub supplies `effort` for Messages or Responses but no Chat provider mark, switching to a different
  Chat provider hides the field and Save omits it. For Chat, both the direct editor and an editor of a use with its own
  record read the selected model's stored `providers[].models` capabilities; the direct editor uses discovery as the
  fallback when no entry is stored. `providers[].model_aliases` resolves legacy Chat tier aliases to the stored model
  IDs used by real requests and named probes before either editor reads capabilities. The control uses `all_efforts`
  when present, else `efforts`, limited to levels a direct-purpose Save accepts; `none` and `off` appear as **Off**, without
  duplicating a current `none` value. Efforts-only Chat metadata keeps **Off** as a separate control. If none of the
  exact reported levels can be saved, only the default remains and the editor says those levels are unavailable; it
  does not substitute projected levels that Chat's exact runtime list would reject. Responses and Messages keep their
  projected `efforts` behavior, including the Responses unknown-metadata `minimal` and `ultra` choices. Chat treats
  absent metadata and an empty effort list as unknown and uses the direct-purpose options (`off`, `low`, `medium`,
  `high`, `xhigh`, `max`); only stored or fallback-discovered `no_effort: true` marks the model unsupported.
  The launcher's model list is inert while a save is on its way, and the page shows only its latest catalog request's
  answer, so an older one still on its way never puts back what a save's reload replaced.
- **Unchanged in look**: the background supervisor (its **Follows Main chat** comes from the hub's `inherited_from`, its
  reset is **Inherit**), the AI twin, Lark /agent and the extensions' purposes. Against a hub before #7980 there are no
  such rows and nothing is asked by their ids.

Tests: `lib/model-config.test.ts`, `views/settings/ModelConfiguration.meeting.test.tsx`. Screenshots: the mock hub with
`MOCK_MEETING_MODELS=1 MOCK_SUPERVISE_LISTED=1`. The editors' footers on a phone, measured in a browser (320 px, 320 and
360 px with Large text, wide; English, 简体中文 and 日本語; the background supervisor's as the unchanged reference): against
that mock and `npx vite`, run `node web/e2e/meeting-models.mjs <web URL> [--shots <dir>] [--executable <chromium>]`
(the mock names its categories in Chinese in every language; the script gives the page their names as a hub sends them).
For the Chat effort editor, also start the mock with `MOCK_CHAT_EFFORT=1` and pass `--chat-effort`. The script selects the
Chat Completions connection, checks its reported options, and saves light/dark screenshots at default and Large text.

### Standing authorizations

**Settings › Persona › Standing authorizations** lists the current assistant's registered grants next to its default task permissions.
The component uses the existing lazy-page loader when Persona settings opens. The search index loads with Settings; its page-only namespaces, including this group's labels and help, load through the non-startup client catalog.
Each grant shows its computer, repository/directory, actions, conditions, original user quote, grant time, source and whether the authorized actions can be undone.
This last field describes the work, not whether the grant can be revoked: every grant has **Revoke…**.
Known action and condition identifiers have localized labels; other values and user-authored conditions remain visible verbatim.
The source is words, not a code: the hub's own sentence for a suggested rule confirmed with Always (in the owner's language when it was made) and the usual words for the main chat, a chat and Settings are worded in the page's language whichever of en, zh-Hans or ja they were written in (`sourceLabel`, #7181, the same rule as the apps' `StandingAuthorizationText.source`); any other source is shown as written.

The group reads `GET /api/v1/assistant/standing-authorizations` and sends `DELETE /api/v1/assistant/standing-authorizations/{id}` only after a confirmation naming the scope and effect.
Both requests explicitly select the current assistant manager, and changing manager or credentials retires the old view's responses.
Revocation removes the entry only after the server acknowledges success. Failed reads show a refresh action instead of an empty registry; failed revocations retain the grant and confirmation for safe retry.
Revocation affects future tasks and approvals, not work or instructions already delivered. There is no web creation route; users request new grants in the main conversation through its existing approval flow.
The interface requires the companion backend from #4443; an older server's missing route is shown as a load failure.

### Remembered conversation permissions (#5867)

In a Persona conversation, **⋯ › Session info › Always allowed in this conversation** lists its saved permissions with the tool name and grant time. Each row has **Revoke**. The database stores hashed permission keys, so the list does not invent directory or command details for existing records. A failed read offers Retry; a failed revoke keeps the row. Revoking clears the saved grant and asks the node to stop the current response to remove process-local grants; the next message resumes the conversation. If that reset cannot be confirmed, the dialog keeps a restart warning, including after reopening or reloading the same browser tab.

Permission cards state the actual scope before approval: Claude Bash covers every command in this conversation; directory-scoped Read/Edit keys cover that directory. Unscoped file tools say every call to the tool. Other runtimes keep their own scope description; unknown key formats get a neutral scope statement. These strings ship in English, Simplified Chinese and Japanese.

A server card with `editable_text` also offers **Edit text** and **Deny with note…**, both collapsed initially. Allow remains the primary action and the initial body stays read-only. Only an actual change sends `edited_text`; an unchanged Allow and cards without the field use the ordinary resolution, and Always disappears once the text differs. Blank replacement text disables Allow. A non-empty denial note is trimmed and sent as the ordinary denial `message`. Drafts reset for a new interaction and survive a failed submission. This round is web-only: iOS and Android retain ordinary Allow/Deny, while Codex, remote/non-`assistant_environment` runtimes and ineligible Lark cards never show the editor. `MOCK_EDITABLE=1` supplies the synthetic editable Lark fixture.

An edited send in **Records sent as you** carries an **Edited** pill. Its detail shows **Original text** (`let_through.edited_from`) and **Sent text** (the row's actual `text`) separately, each with its own copy action; rows without an edit are unchanged.

For browser checks, run the mock hub with `MOCK_ALWAYS_SCOPE=1`. It adds a Bash permission card and two saved grants to the main conversation, with a working per-row DELETE endpoint. Native permission-management screens remain follow-up work.

### Main conversation on browser reload (#5025)

The main conversation shows this browser's last successful latest page immediately, using the existing chat renderer, while the hub refreshes it. `/assistant` applies as soon as it answers, independently of slower session or sidebar reads. Its main-conversation reference is authoritative: changing or removing the main conversation discards the old cached reference. Other conversations and Agent pages do not use this persistent cache; they have the memory cache below.

`lib/feed-cache.ts` keeps one page in localStorage, partitioned by hub origin plus proxy prefix and a fingerprint of the device token id and credential (a token fingerprint alone on older hubs). Cache keys and values never contain the authentication token. Signing out or replacing credentials removes cached pages and invalidates in-flight writers. The page records its manager selection so a different manager cannot reuse it. The extensions' places and pages are kept under the same scope and cleared with it ("Extension pages on reload" below).

The conversation's feed (briefs, dispatch cards, receipts) is loaded whole, but the transcript only page by page. While older pages remain, feed items dated before the oldest loaded item stay out (`displayLines` `from`) and appear as the page that covers them loads. Drawn above the newest page, days-old cards and their day lines read as the conversation's start with every message between them gone. Older pages load when the view nears its top, and again after each change while it is still there: a view that cannot scroll, or a page that landed without moving it, sends no scroll event, so the top would otherwise never load more.

**Urgent calls** (#8734, `../assistant/urgent-call.md`): a Persona conversation's calls (`GET /api/v1/assistant/calls?conversation=<id>`, read again on the `urgent_call` message and after a connection that did not resume) are feed items of kind `urgent_call` at the time each first rang, so `displayLines` places them among the lines and the day lines like the rest of the feed; a call that could not ring is left out. Each is a pill like an answered card's, **Urgent call: <title> · answered · 2 min 5 s** (or missed, missed (rang twice), declined, settled elsewhere), opening to why Persona called, what came of it and what was said. The reading and the row are lazy imports (`views/assistant/urgent-calls.ts`, `UrgentCallLine.tsx`) with the namespace `assistant-urgentcall`; the first screen carries only the effect that loads them and the row's `lazy` case. A manager without urgent calls, or a device without full access, shows none. Mock: `MOCK_URGENT_CALL=1` (an answered call with its transcript and one missed twice, in the main conversation).

### Switching between chats

Every other conversation and Agent page keeps its newest page in the same module's memory cache, for the 20 most recently opened chats (least recently used out). It is never written to disk, so it does not survive a reload. Opening one of those chats shows the kept page at once and refreshes it from the hub in the background through `mergeItems`; pushes keep it current while the chat is open. A failed refresh leaves the page up, with the Reload pill instead of the error page. When the refreshed page starts after everything the kept one holds, turns may be missing between them, so it replaces the kept page and older history loads on scroll. A fold in the refreshed page replaces the raw steps the kept page held for that range. A push that arrives after lost items is not kept until the gap is filled. Keys start with the same hub and credential scope as the main conversation's cache, and sign-out or a credential change empties it.

Only the latest two user turns are eligible, matching the latest-page request. Older pages and expanded folds remain in memory. The cache is limited to 200 items and 256 KiB of UTF-8 JSON; a page exceeding either limit is not retained. Image bodies and inline base64 image URLs are removed, leaving lazy image metadata. Storage restrictions, corrupt entries and quota failures fall back to the usual loading behavior. This is local conversation storage, not an offline sync queue; no configuration is required.

Fresh items replace matching ids; a changed transcript history or a confirmed empty transcript replaces stale content. A failed refresh keeps the last page and shows the existing chat status capsule with **Couldn't refresh** and **Reload**, localized in English, Simplified Chinese and Japanese. Reload retries both the main-conversation reference and its transcript without blanking the cached page.

### Extension pages on reload (#9283)

An extension's sidebar entries and its full page are drawn from what this browser last saw, at first paint, while the hub is asked again (principle 7). Before, every load waited for a request the hub relays to the manager (about a second through a hub): no entries, an open page's header with the generic icon and the page's id, and then its body on the loading state until the extension drew it.

- **The places list** (`lib/extension-slots.ts`): the last `GET /api/v1/extensions/-/ui` answer, badges included, is kept with the default manager it was read under. It is drawn from the first paint, before the hello: the sidebar's entries with their titles, icons and badges, an open page's header, the Overview cards and the inbox items' pages. The hub's answer, asked for as before once the hello says the hub has UI slots, replaces it and is kept; an `extension_ui` badge changes the kept one too. A list kept under another default manager is dropped as soon as the roster names this one, and a hub whose hello has no UI slots shows none.
- **A page's last view** (`lib/extension-view-cache.ts`): the full page (`/extension/<id>/<ui>`, ExtensionUI's `remember`) draws its first page's last view at once, as wide as that drawing was, while the hello, the roster and the extension's drawing are on their way. It is marked by **Updating…** in the page's top margin (a 10 px `Spinner` and `text-label` words in `ink-3`, `role=status`), so nothing moves when the drawing replaces it, and it is `inert`: nothing in it can be pressed or focused, so no action is ever sent from a stale view. Each view is kept per extension, page, first state, UI version, default manager and language, and shown only when drawn with a UI version the page may be drawn with now (over HTTP 8; over the app socket 7, or 8 for a page that falls back to HTTP; before the hello, either) and by the roster's default's extension (before the roster, the last one drawn; withdrawn when the roster names another). Pushed pages, sections and inbox items keep their loading state.
- **An Overview card's last view** (#11091): a card (`OverviewCard`, ExtensionUI's `compact` with `remember`) draws its last view the same way, from the same cache and under the same rules, keyed by the card's own id, so a page's view is never a card's. A card drawn before is on screen at first paint, as tall as it was: the sections under the cards do not move while the cards draw, and a card whose extension takes seconds shows what it last showed instead of **Loading**. The kept view is drawn where the drawing's own sections go (no box of its own: `contents`), `inert`, with **Updating…** for screen readers only; what is seen is a 10 px `Spinner` in the card's heading, faded in after 600 ms, so a card that redraws at once never shows it. A card never drawn in this browser starts from **Loading** as before.
- **Storage**: localStorage, under the main conversation cache's scope (`lib/feed-cache.ts` `scopedKey`: hub origin plus proxy prefix and a fingerprint of the device id and credential), so another hub or sign-in never reads them, and signing out or replacing credentials removes them with the cached page. A view is at most 64 KiB of UTF-8 JSON and at most 24 are kept, the least recently drawn going first. A larger view, one holding the sign-in token, a secret field's value, and a view drawn while its fields hold what was typed and not sent are never written. Storage errors fall back to waiting for the hub. Like the cached conversation page, this is never a source of authority: the hub's answer always replaces it.

To see it in a browser: `web/e2e/extension-first-paint.mjs` (`web/e2e/README.md`) against the mock hub with `MOCK_EXTENSIONS=1 MOCK_EXTENSION_COLUMNS=1`, the relayed requests delayed.

### Dashboards (#15017)

Pages the assistant keeps up to date are drawn as the default manager's extension pages under the reserved id `-pages`
(the index `index`, each page `pg_` and 16 hex), at the extensions' own path (`POST /api/v1/extensions/-pages/-/ui/<id>`),
so the sidebar entry, the full page (`/extension/-pages/<id>`), the deep link, the sidebar ordering key
(`p:-pages/<id>`) and the first-paint caches above work as for any extension page. What is particular to them:

- **HTTP only**: an id that starts with `-` is a manager's own and never opens the native UI stream, nor waits for the
  hello to decide (`lib/extension-ui.ts` `httpOnlyUI`, `views/settings/ExtensionView.tsx`); the subscription and health
  pages were already drawn that way through `RESERVED_UI_PATHS`, which `-pages` is not in.
- **Places**: the hub lists the index while a page is kept or one waits in Recently removed, then each pinned page (at most
  three), after the extensions' places; `assistant_pages` (a page kept, pinned, unpinned, renamed, removed or restored, or
  the switch turned) asks for the list again (`lib/extension-slots.ts`). A page's content change is the ordinary
  `extension_ui {extension: "-pages", id, invalidate: true}`.
- **Phase 2 watch pages and Overview cards (#13020)**: `uiPlaces` adds `?pages_overview=1` when asking for all slots or
  `overview_card` (`lib/extension-ui.ts`), so kept watch pages marked **Show on Overview** are listed as ordinary
  `overview_card` places (`id: g_<16 hex>`, `opens: pg_<16 hex>`). They render, arrange, resize and hide on Overview like
  any other Overview card, reload on `assistant_pages` (places list) and `extension_ui {extension: "-pages", id: "g_…",
  invalidate: true}` (card content), open `/extension/-pages/<pg id>` when tapped, and never appear in the sidebar or
  Settings › Extensions. `uiContext` reports `context.platform` as `desktop` inside the Electron desktop app
  (`window.personaDesktop`) and `web` in a browser so the watch page footer includes **Show on Overview**. In
  `views/extensions/ViewBody.tsx`, a lone `metric` allows long watch questions and details to wrap instead of truncating,
  a `row`'s `value` caps at `max-w-[45%]` so long status texts truncate instead of squeezing out the row's title, and
  `views/settings/ExtensionView.tsx` reconciles view-returning row switch actions (`persona.alert`, `persona.overview`)
  against concurrent `extension_ui` redraws so the switch never snaps back.
- **Sidebar**: the index and pinned pages are extension pages in `useNavPages`. The hub puts their keys in the navigation
  record's `shown` on the first Keep and on a pin, so `EXTENSION_CAP` never sends them under More: they count toward the
  cap first, and with three extension nav pages installed the extensions' pages past it wait there instead (two of the
  three beside the index and one pinned page).
- **Top bar** (`views/extensions/ExtensionSlots.tsx`): titled by the drawn View's `title` (the page's title, written by the
  hub), then the place's, then **Dashboards**, never the `pg_…` id, so an unpinned page opened by a deep link reads right.
  Every page but the index has the ownership line under its title at every width (`docs/design/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md`
  "Ownership line (#15017)"); the extension's name is not written beside it. A row of the index that pushes a page opens it
  as a page of its own (its address, title and line), not on the index's stack; a push within a page (Rename) stays on its stack.
- **Settings › Assistant**: **Let Persona make dashboards**, off by default, shown only when the hello lists
  `assistant_pages` and only for the default manager; it reads and writes `dashboards` of `/api/v1/assistant` and shows
  the value the hub confirmed.
- With the switch off, or on with nothing kept, nothing on the sidebar, the phone's page grid or Overview changes.

To see it: the mock hub with `MOCK_DASHBOARDS=1` (`scripts/mock/dashboards_mock.py`; `off`, `empty`, `removed`, `pinned`
and `watch` for the other states) and `npx vite`. `node web/e2e/dashboards.mjs` (its header says how to start both) checks
phase 1 in light and dark at 1280 and 390 wide in each language, compares the sidebar with the switch off and on with
nothing kept against a build of `origin/main` pixel by pixel (`--before`), and, with `--extensions`, that Dashboards stays
in the list beside three extension nav pages. `node web/e2e/dashboards-watch.mjs` checks phase 2 against
`MOCK_DASHBOARDS=watch`: the four displays (empty, normal, alert), index rows, footer states, Overview watch cards,
`zh-Hans` / `ja`, desktop platform context, and pixel-identical sidebar and Overview against `origin/main` in `off` and
phase-1 (`1`) modes.

### External sources (#15518)

People who follow work in Inbox can connect updates from a chat, repository, mail account or subscription to a
direction or to-do. On To-dos, **Direction details** opens any current direction, including one with no to-dos.
The Pinned conversation's sidebar menu reaches the same detail. Directions and both to-do layouts show
**External sources**. The section lists explicit connections and uses **Repositories and work** for the to-do's
projected pull requests and issues, so each saved repository link appears once and keeps its work role.

**Connect external source** opens the same editor from work and Inbox. Work preselects its destination. Inbox
preselects the hub's most specific source on the message's `external_path`. The scope picker offers its parents
and the same editable fields are available from each entry. A source already in Inbox can be picked by name.
Expanding **Source details** shows the exact identity when needed. Older or internal Inbox items without a
canonical path have no direct connect action.

Forwarding is off until the owner opts in. The editor shows the inherited value and its source for each policy
field when the hub supplies one. Choosing **Inherit** clears the override. The digest interval can be set while
inheriting the forwarding mode, and choosing custom filters with their three lists empty clears an inherited
filter. Explicit connections can be edited or disconnected on the destination. Use **Manage links** for saved
repository links.

Legacy Sources, Channels and Extensions and unified Integrations detail and Data Flow offer **Channel defaults**
and **Connected work** links. The settings editor writes only the service and account scope, and **Restore defaults**
followed by Save sends an empty policy. Connected work includes repository projections and opens the matching
direction or to-do for the same assistant. The browser uses `/todos?direction=<id>` for a direction and can
carry `manager` on either work link. The capability works in both presentations. The binding editor, channel
policy panel and HTTP client load on demand. See [External source bindings](../protocol/protocol.md#external-source-bindings).

### Message sources (#2125)

Relayed conversations, scheduled patrols, follow-ups and supervision use the optional `Item.source` contract in
[the protocol](../protocol/protocol.md). Their model-facing role can remain `user`, but the chat renders a left-aligned
neutral source block with an `@` title, never a user bubble. Consecutive messages from the same source share the title;
a reply, user input or different source resets it. Long content folds to three lines with an accessible Expand / Collapse
control. No group-chat header, member list or per-source avatar is added. Quiet supervision rounds retain their existing
folded trace, now labeled with their source mention.

**Background rounds** (#4314, leaders in #6595, `docs/assistant/assistant.md` "Background rounds"): in the main
conversation and the leader conversations (`AssistantInfo.leaders`), while `main_background_folded` is on
(Settings › Assistant › **Fold background rounds**, `settings/AssistantSettings.tsx`; gate `lib/background-fold.ts`
`foldsBackgroundRounds`), a round whose first input's source is `conversation`, `followup` or `patrol` folds into the
same line as a quiet supervision round, `@<source> · Background round` (`chatLines`' `background` option, `lib/turns.ts`;
`SupervisionLine` in `views/chat/Lines.tsx`). An ordinary side conversation keeps showing every round. The hub's
interject note (`<persona-context kind="context" title="插话">`) is stripped in `parseUserText` and never becomes an
owner-bubble quote chip; `e2e/leader-background-rounds.mjs` checks the leader chat with synthetic data and takes the
before/after screenshots.
Opened, its inputs are source blocks, not raw model input; a scheduled task's or follow-up's input shows only its line,
never the prompt (`promptHidden`), folded or not. The supervision visibility rule (`supervisionVisible`) keeps rounds that
asked or told the user shown. By default, a completed, nonempty reply from another conversation appears in the main chat
and receives its ordinary finished notification. Settings › Assistant › **Fold routine replies from other chats**
(`fold_routine_relay_replies`, #11899) keeps those replies in the expandable record and quiets that notification when
**Fold background rounds** is also on. A hub that omits the opt-in keeps the default and hides the new switch. Changing
either setting preserves the other. Explicit user promotions (including P0, requested results and decisions) remain visible
and notify. On Web, an explicitly promoted main-conversation relay keeps its incoming handoff behind a collapsed source
row; expanding that row reveals the original while the answer and interaction cards stay visible. Leader conversations keep their completed replies visible. Needs you groups rows by the task's supervising conversation (`needsYouBySupervisor`,
`lib/assistant-entries.ts`) when more than one has rows. `e2e/background-rounds.mjs` checks it in a real browser with
synthetic data and takes the screenshots; with the switch off the chat is pixel-identical to a build without the feature.

In the main conversation, a completed, non-live round with a successful silent finish and no promotion instead leaves
no timeline row and adds no unread count or badge. Its inline tools and its `task`, `routed` and `answered` feed cards
inside the same half-open round interval stay out too; plans, message cards, notices and other decisions always remain
visible. **Background activity**, from both the conversation menu and Inbox, reuses `SupervisionLine` and the same
paged transcript to retain the complete round and those feed cards without creating an InboxItem or marking anything
seen. A successful `task_review accepted` receipt with hub-issued `background=true` follows the same split: the whole
review round and its original tool trace stay in Background activity. The hub derives that marker only from the current
plan's `user_requested`, `parent` and the supervision ledger's current `auto_review` / `round`; unmarked, `user_check`
and `needs_user` reviews remain visible. Full-history APIs are unchanged. `e2e/quiet-supervision.mjs` checks silent and promoted boundaries and captures
synthetic before/after evidence; promoted tools are inspected after opening their work summary.

The cache retains the source metadata. Unknown nonempty source kinds still use the source presentation. Old hubs fall back
to injected metadata and complete canonical relay contexts; genuine app inputs and protected quoted templates are never
reclassified. Source messages cannot settle an identical pending user message or become user-navigation ticks.

Browser regression: run an isolated mock hub and Vite, then
`node web/e2e/message-sources.mjs <web URL> --shots <directory>`. It checks the real transcript renderer, consecutive labels,
fold toggles, one genuine user bubble, console errors and wide/narrow light/dark screenshots. `--cdp <CDP URL>` leaves the
inspection pages in an existing browser. All transcript content is synthetic; this check does not test live delivery.

### Forwarding a message (#3899)

The web's side of iPhone's Forward (#3807; [the protocol](../protocol/protocol.md), "Forwarded messages"):
**Forward** in a message's actions opens **Forward to** (`views/chat/ForwardDialog.tsx`, a dialog on a wide screen and a
sheet from the bottom on a phone): the message, then **Persona** (the main chat, unless the message is from it) and
**New agent…**, then **Recent** (`lib/forward-memory.ts`: at most 8 targets kept and 5 shown, ids only, in this browser
for this hub, forgotten on sign-out) and each computer's live Agents, latest first, by the order of the computers
(`lib/forward-targets.ts`, as iOS `ForwardTargets`: a chat that takes messages, its computer online, never this chat,
Health's or an archived one). Search matches titles, Agents, projects and computers, and also finds ended Agents and
Persona's other conversations. The lists are the sessions the page holds as the dialog opens; nothing is fetched. No
confirmation: picking a target reads the whole message when the page holds it cut (`GET …/items/{id}/full`) and the
photos of your own message, then opens that chat with the forward over its composer (`addContext`, a `ContextRef` of
kind `forward`, drawn by `views/chat/ForwardBar.tsx` with the line "From MacBook · to Codex on Mac Studio"), its photos
in the tray; the note is typed there and goes with the usual send, the block before it (`lib/forward-block.ts`,
`lib/context-xml.ts`; with no note, "Please look at the forwarded message above."). **New agent…** opens New agent with
the card over the first message. Persona with no main conversation yet: the new conversation's box. Nothing is written
to the original chat. In a sent bubble the block is a card at the top (`views/chat/ForwardCard.tsx`): the forward arrow,
"Forwarded from Claude · chat", the computer and time, four lines; a click opens the original chat and brings the
message into view, or shows the whole text when this page does not have that chat. A reader that does not know `forward`
folds it like other contexts. There is no Share as Image of one message on the web, so the dialog has no such row
(picked messages have Export image, below).

**Several at once** (#3838, #9469, as iOS; [the protocol](../protocol/protocol.md), "Forwarded messages"): the message
menu's last row, **Select messages** (under a divider, with the check icon, as Telegram's menu ends in Select), or Forward
to's first row, **Select messages…**, opened for one message, hands the chat its picks (`lib/message-pick.ts`) with that
message already picked; `ChatView` holds them while it picks. The menu's row goes through Forward to's chunk without
showing it (`ForwardBatch.now`), so the first screen carries only the row. Each message with a Forward then has a
checkbox over it with a tick before it (`views/chat/Picking.tsx` `PickRow`), and a click anywhere on a message picks or
unpicks it (its contents are inert; its menus and bars are off). A bar takes the composer's place (`PickBar`):
**Cancel**, "2 selected", **Include questions** when it means something, then **Forward**, **Copy** and **Export image**,
off with none picked; on a phone the actions are a row of their own, an icon over each word, as the iPhone draws them.
Cancel or Escape leaves the chat as it was, the draft kept. At most 30 go, the questions brought counted: one more says
"Up to 30 messages at a time". None of this is on the first screen: `Picking.tsx` comes with Forward to, which hands it
to the chat (`views/chat/picking-parts.ts`) as it starts picking, and the picked message as a forward is
`lib/forward-draft.ts`, which only the chunks that forward, copy or export load; not picking, a message is drawn as it
always was. **Forward** opens Forward to with what goes in the chat's order (not the order they were picked) as one
card and no Select messages… row; picking a target puts one forward per message over its box, each cut at its share
(`forwardLimit`: the smaller of 20,000 and 60,000 / N characters), and the photos of all of them up to the composer's
limit. Forwards of one chat next to each other are one bar over the box (`ForwardGroupBar`: "2 forwarded messages ·
chat", a line each, the first three and "N more", the route, one × for all) and one card in the bubble
(`ForwardGroupBlock`: a line each over two lines, each opening its original; past three, "N more"); another chat's
forward or any other block starts a new one (`forwardRuns`). Both are a chunk of their own
(`views/chat/ForwardGroup.tsx`): the bar comes after Forward to, which loads it, and until the card is in, the bubble
says "2 forwarded messages" in a line of plain words. With no note: "Please look at the forwarded messages above.".

**Include questions** (#9469, iOS `PickQuestions`; `lib/pick-export.ts` `pickQuestions`): a reply's questions are its
turn's messages from your side (a turn that got no reply hands its questions on to the next reply), never a `/loop`
tick, an injected line or another source's message. While a picked reply's question is not picked, the bar offers
Include questions as a chip (`role="switch"`); on, Forward, Copy and Export image take those questions too, and their
ticks are lighter (`bg-accent-tint`, "goes with its answer" to a screen reader). On by default; the last choice is kept
in this browser (`persona.pickIncludeQuestions`, read when picking starts). Turning it on is refused when what goes would
pass 30.

**Copy** (#9469, `copiedText`): what goes as plain text, each whole (an item the chat holds cut is read with
`GET …/items/{id}/full`, as a forward reads it) and cut at a forward's 20,000 characters, "Me:" or the author's name
over it, a blank line between; picking ends once it is copied.

**Export image** (#9469, `views/chat/ExportImage.tsx`): a dialog (a bottom sheet on a phone, its ✕ kept) with a preview
of the picture, **Include questions** when it means something, **Title and date**, and **Copy image** (one page only,
`ClipboardItem`) and **Download PNG** or **Download N** (`Persona-1.png`…). What goes is drawn off screen as the chat
draws it, 390 px wide at the screen's 2× or 3×, light or dark as the page is, the text at the reading size: on top the
chat's title, the day (or days) and who answers, never the computer or project; then your bubbles with your photos, and
each reply under its author with the chat's own Markdown (formulas, diagrams, cards as the chat draws them; a code
block's Copy and a diagram's tools left out); pictures laid out as a reply's (`ReplyImages`, #9474), all of them (no
"+N"); at the foot of each page Persona's mark (the assistant's face, its name and "(Persona)") and "2/3" when there are
several. Pages break between messages and cut one taller than a page, at most 16,000 px and 64 MB to decode each
(`pagePlan`, `pageHeight`, as iOS `ExportPages`). The dialog is a chunk of its own, loaded on the first press of Export
image, and the library that draws the page into a PNG, `html-to-image` (MIT), is imported only by it, so it loads only
when Export image is pressed and is never on the first screen. Every web picture in it comes through the hub's
remote-image route (`remoteImageURL`, `GET /api/v1/remote-image`); a hub without the route gets a tile naming the
site, and a picture inside a line of text keeps the tap-to-load gate: nothing is read from another site.

`src/lib/forward.test.ts` writes and reads every case of `spec/fixtures/forward` byte for byte, and
`src/lib/forward-several.test.ts` those of `several.json` (the budget, the blocks and note, the cards they make);
`src/views/chat/MessagePick.test.tsx` checks picking and its bar, the message menu's Select messages and Include
questions, `src/lib/pick-export.test.ts` the questions, the 30, Copy's text and the pages, `ForwardCard.group.test.tsx` and
`ForwardCard.pending.test.tsx` the group's bar and card. Browser check (wide and phone width, light and dark;
`--shots` saves the menu, the dialog, the composer and the sent bubble, and the steps of several at once):
`MOCK_ECHO_SENT=1 PORT=<port> python3 scripts/mock/mock_hub.py`, `npx vite` against it, then
`node web/e2e/forward-message.mjs <web URL> --hub <mock hub URL> [--shots <dir>] [--channel msedge | --executable <chromium>]`.
It forwards a reply to another computer's Agent (searching "Astro") and to Persona, checks the route line, the block and
note the hub got (`GET /mock/sent_to`), the card in the sent bubble and that it opens the original, and New agent's card;
then several at once: Select messages…, Cancel, the message menu's Select messages, none picked, your message and the
reply forwarded together to the blog's
Agent, the two blocks in the chat's order before the note, and the one card in the sent bubble.

### Saved prompts (#7329)

The user's own `/` prompts: the instructions they send again and again ("review this diff for security issues…", a team's
PR checklist), kept on the hub as the current assistant's settings (`assistant.saved_prompts`, the routes in
`docs/protocol/protocol.md` ("REST (App → hub)")), so every device and browser has the same list. No assistant tool reads
or writes them: the main chat's fixed payload stays as it was.

- **In every chat's `/` list** (Agent chats, Persona chats, the new-conversation and health boxes): after the chat's own
  commands and before extensions' quick prompts, in the list's order, with **Saved** where a row says where it comes from,
  ranked and filtered with the rest (`rankCommands`). Picking one puts its text in the box and never sends it, as a quick
  prompt does; the card beside the list shows what it types. A box with no commands of its own still opens the list for
  them. The rows come from `lib/saved-prompt-rows.ts`, a few lines on the first screen; the list, its reads and words are
  `lib/saved-prompts.ts`, a chunk loaded the first time a box has the focus or a `/`. One list per page, read again on
  `hello`, on `assistant_saved_prompts` (another device changed it; only the shown assistant's, `PAGE_EVENTS`) and when
  another assistant becomes the current one; until it is in, a box shows none.
- **Settings › Saved Prompts** (`views/settings/SavedPrompts.tsx`, in the current assistant's group): each prompt's
  `/name` and the first two lines of its text, **New Prompt**, and per row Move Up / Move Down (the `/` list's order,
  `PUT …/order`), **Edit** and **Delete** (confirmed in the row). An empty page says what they are for. An assistant from
  before them (404) says it does not keep them yet; a failed read offers Try Again, and a list read before stays.
- **The editor** (`views/settings/SavedPromptDialog.tsx`): Name (one word, shown after a fixed `/`) and Text (several
  lines; ⌘/Ctrl-Return saves). It says a rule before asking the hub: a name another prompt has at once, the name and text
  rules once there is something to check or Save was pressed; the hub's own refusal shows in the dialog and keeps what
  was typed. A count appears past 80% of the 8,000 characters.
- **Save as Prompt…** on your own message's menu (right click, a long press, the ⋯ beside the bubble) where the chat
  can send: the editor over the page, filled with the message's words and a name from its first ones (lower case, joined
  by `-`, moved past a name taken). Not on replies, and not in a read-only chat.
- iOS (#9436, `docs/apple/ios.md` "Saved prompts") and Android (#11667, `docs/android/android.md` "Saved prompts") share the hub list.
- Checks: `lib/saved-prompts.test.ts`, `views/settings/SavedPrompts.test.tsx`, `views/chat/Composer.saved-prompts.test.tsx`,
  `views/chat/MessageActions.save-prompt.test.tsx`; end to end against the mock hub (`MOCK_SAVED_PROMPTS=1`), wide and phone,
  light and dark: `node web/e2e/saved-prompts.mjs <web URL> --hub <mock hub URL> [--shots <dir>]`.

### Starred messages (#7524)

Starred is off by default. **Settings › General › Appearance › Starred messages** turns it on for this browser
(`persona.starredMessages` in local storage, like Reply animation). While it is off, the sidebar has no Starred
page and the message menu has no Star or Unstar, and no saved marker shows; saved messages stay on the hub and
reappear when the switch is turned on again.

Use **Star** from a text message's menu in an Assistant or Agent chat. The menu opens with its More
button, a right click, or a long press. A small star marks the saved message. **Unstar** is available in
the same menu and on the **Starred** page. Removing a star offers **Undo** in the notification. It saves
the same snapshot again with a new star ID, even if the original message has gone away.

**Pages › Starred** shows the current assistant's saves, newest first. Its count is the number of saved
messages for that assistant. Search matches words in the saved text, conversation title, and speaker.
**Copy** copies the saved text. **Open original** opens the conversation at the saved message with the
existing message-link behavior. Workers and side chats open in their panels at the message. A link into a
compact child card or an earlier engine opens the original transcript so the message can be shown. When the
runtime supplies only a line position, it checks a fingerprint of the
original transcript record before opening and reads it again at the final jump, even when the visible page
has not detected a same-size rewrite. If a rewrite reuses that line, the replacement can be starred separately. The old snapshot stays available for Copy and Unstar and shows that its original is
unavailable. Older snapshots without a fingerprint for a line position also stay readable. Star is offered for
positional messages only when their node supplies the fingerprint.

The manager keeps up to 300 text snapshots, at most 4,000 Unicode characters each, with a count of text
left out. New saves retain the visible message text, title, author, and original time when available.
If a user message was shortened for the chat page, Star fetches the full text blocks and applies the same
user-message formatting before deciding which characters to save and how many were left out.
Edits and deletion of the original do not change the snapshot. The browser asks for identifiers alone
to mark the chats and show the sidebar count. It reads snapshot text while the Starred page is open,
refreshing on reconnect, after a write, and on notifications from the selected assistant. An older hub
or assistant hides Star from the menus and explains the missing capability if someone opens `/starred`
directly. The protocol is in `docs/protocol/protocol.md` ("REST (App → hub)").

To verify the web flow, run the mock hub with `MOCK_STARRED=1` and follow the commands in
`web/e2e/starred-messages.mjs`. It drives two isolated browser contexts and verifies cross-device changes,
search, copy, Undo, exact links, and a snapshot whose original is absent.

#### Back up starred messages (#12061)

Open **Backup** on the Starred page. Download a JSON backup to restore later or choose
Markdown for a copy you can read and edit in a text editor. Exports include the selected assistant's
saved text, title, speaker, source category and timestamps. They omit device and conversation identifiers.

Choose a JSON backup and select **Preview restore** to see how many messages would be added, how many are
already saved and how much space is available. Select **Restore messages** to save the batch. If another device changed Starred after you
previewed it, review the current counts and confirm again. A backup that would exceed the 300-message limit
stays in preview until you make room.

Restored messages are archival snapshots. You can search, copy or remove them. They retain the saved words
and timestamps independently of the original conversation. An older manager can still supply the snapshots
for export. Restore appears when the connected manager supports it.

Run the browser test with `MOCK_STARRED=1 MOCK_STARRED_BACKUP=1` and `node web/e2e/starred-backup.mjs`.

### Exporting a conversation (#7375)

**Export Conversation…** in every chat's ⋯ (Agent chats and Persona conversations) saves the whole conversation as one
Markdown file, or copies it, whatever the page has loaded (`views/chat/ExportDialog.tsx`, a chunk of its own; the rules
in `lib/chat-export.ts`, checked against `spec/fixtures/chat-export`).

- **Reading**: from the latest page back to the first (`GET …/items?turns=10&lazy_images=1&fold_work=1&before_seq=`),
  the dialog saying how many items are in. Each message the pages carry cut (`full_size`) is read whole
  (`…/items/{id}/full`, three at a time, at most 200; one that fails stays cut and the file says how much is left out).
  A history rewritten while reading (the pages' `history` changes: a rewind, a compaction) starts over once, then says
  the conversation changed. It stops at 20,000 items or 400 pages; it also stops if a promised older page cannot move
  the cursor. The dialog and file say when history is incomplete, with its first readable timestamp when available;
  rows outside the requested older range do not replace already read messages. Closing the dialog stops it.
- **The file**: the title, the agent, the computer, the folder and when it was exported; then each part under
  `## <who> · <time>` (local time): You, the assistant's name for a message Persona typed in, another session by its
  name, the agent (or, in a Persona conversation, the assistant) for its replies, replies in a row under one heading. A
  notice is an italic line; pictures are `[Image]`; folded work and the while-you-were-away recap are left out. Fences
  are longer than any run of backticks inside them.
