Integration addresses accept an independent `manager` parameter. An address without one or a legacy owner follows the
sidebar's current assistant. The linked assistant's Labs setting selects the unified or legacy page, keeping the object,
filter, push-source state, and proposed `set` values. Shareable object URLs carry the legacy owner suffix during the trial.
When the two owner spellings disagree, Settings shows Back and leaves the integration unopened.
Under the trial, Assistant settings shows the state of `inbox_todo_forward` and links to its single editable switch in
**Data flow** (#16190), preserving the assistant named in the link. GitHub detail opens saved Repositories in Assistant
settings. Mail, Feishu and sources with history link to the sync scope in Knowledge. Turning off the trial restores the
original forwarding switch. See the [split layout](../design/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md#integrations--extensions-in-web-settings),
[channel settings](../extensions/channels.md#7-ui) and [connector overview](../extensions/connectors.md).

An assistant that advertises `integrations_projection_v1` in the hub roster supplies the rows, filter counts and
detail sections through its read-only Integrations projection (#17762). The Web view loads these reads only inside
Settings and keeps them scoped to the named assistant and hub credential. A failed read can be retried on that
assistant while readable sections remain usable. Older hubs or assistants that lack the announcement use the legacy
catalog, and existing settings endpoints still handle edits.

Built-in services, standalone channels and connectors, installed or built-in extensions, and standalone push or
subscription sources all compose through one capability-section detail shell (`web/src/views/settings/integrations/DetailShell.tsx`),
mounted stably by `(manager, kind, id)` across the 740 px split breakpoint so drafts and open disclosures stay intact.
Sections appear in canonical capability order (`connection`, `conversation_and_push`, `inbox_and_sync`, `external_sources`,
`extension_configuration`, `information_access`, and `lifecycle`), placing Feishu Bot's `ConnectorExternalSourceSettings`
after **Inbox & sync** to match extensions. Single-pane standalone source details include a same-assistant **Data flow**
entry when Inbox Sources is available while preserving single-source scope. Settings host navigation metadata for the
Integrations entry (`web/src/views/settings/integrations-registration.ts`) keeps its label, search keywords, visibility,
route resolution, legacy 4-tab compatibility mapping, and lazy boundary self-contained for future registry adoption.

Channel and extension editors keep their configuration in tab memory under the bound hub credential, assistant, resource
kind, and ID (#17762). The split breakpoint and legacy Extensions entry read the same drafts. Saves run in order for a
resource, and a refresh requested during a write reads again after it. The channel form checks the document revision
and sends only the named fields. Extension saves first load a fresh baseline for their full-config PUT, apply the
edited fields, and keep the entry-preserving mode for immediate machine switches. Overlapping changes and the hub's
`settings_moved` refusal keep the draft for review. If the save response is lost, the editor reads the same resource and
compares the submitted fields with the confirmed values before showing a receipt. Pairing again clears these drafts.

Graduation (making the new experience the default for at least one release with rollback kept) or removal is tracked in #14802.

**Terminal renderer** (`web/src/lib/labs-terminal.ts` over `web/src/lib/labs.ts`). Single pane terminals
(`views/session/terminal/feed.ts`) draw with xterm's DOM renderer (Standard, the default) or WebGL (`@xterm/addon-webgl`,
its own chunk, loaded only when chosen). Full view always uses the DOM renderer and is not affected. It is kept by this
browser (`localStorage`) because GPU support differs per browser and machine; it never reaches the hub, another browser,
device or user. Its document has one segmented choice with details for scope, activation and rollback. No request
leaves the page.
- Storage: the key `persona.terminal.webgl` with WebGL as `1`, the Terminal settings switch's from before Labs, so a saved
  choice keeps working and an older build reads the same value back. Standard writes nothing. A value this build doesn't
  recognize reads as Standard, is left in place and is named in a notice until a choice replaces it; storage the page
  can't read shows Standard with a notice. A write the browser throws on or doesn't read back fails with the module's
  message, which says only that the save couldn't be confirmed (the stored value may or may not have changed). The
  revision follows what is stored, so a choice made in another tab is a conflict for a stale page, and the page follows
  other tabs through `subscribe`.
- A terminal reads the choice when it is made (`rendererChosen`); a change in Labs leaves open terminals, and what was
  typed in them, as they are; the next terminal opened (or the page after a reload) uses it.
- Terminal settings has no WebGL switch of its own: its Renderer row says what draws this terminal (Standard, WebGL, or
  Standard after WebGL stopped) and has a Labs button. It opens the same Labs page in a dialog over the page (a sheet on a
  phone; `LabsDialog`, loaded on first open), as Edit shortcuts opens its editor, never Settings in place of the page:
  the chat beside the terminal stays mounted with its unsent draft and any open image editor.
- If WebGL cannot start or its GPU context is lost, that terminal disposes the addon, xterm repaints with the DOM renderer
  from its unchanged buffer, input keeps flowing, and the choice is set back to Standard so the next terminal does not fail
  the same way. A toast says so; if Standard could not be saved, it says that instead. A terminal that fell back stays on
  Standard until it is opened again.

### Adding, graduating and removing an entry

1. **Add** an entry that meets the admission criteria and link its tracking issue. Register its ID and enabled check in
   `labs-catalog.ts` and its source in `Labs.tsx` with scope, activation and rollback in `en`, `zh-Hans` and `ja`.
   Add a search entry and test both paths and the
   fallback. Preserve security fixes and keep the stable path available throughout the trial.
2. **Graduate** when the new path is ready for everyone: make it the default in a PR linked to the entry's issue, say so
   in the release notes, and keep the entry for at least one release so people can still go back.
3. **Remove** after that release: delete the catalog entry, the module's source, its words and the old path. Stop reading its key; leave
   stored values alone (they are ignored). An entry whose new path is abandoned is removed the same way with the old path kept.

## Modules

Persona Core and feature modules (#13430; the web foundation is #13434). Persona Core is the app without its optional
features; each optional feature is a **module** under `web/src/modules/<id>/` that reaches the shell only through what
it registers with the module host. The core never imports a module. `web/src/core/` holds the host and is otherwise a
classification label: existing core files stay where they are.

**The host** (`web/src/core/module-host.ts`). `registerModule(descriptor)` records a module; the shell reads the
registry back (`moduleRouteAt`, `enabledNavItems`, `moduleTitle`, `moduleNavKey`, `loadModule`, `useModuleStates`),
never a module's code. A descriptor is small and static: what the module contributes, plus a dynamic `import()` of its
code. Its fields use the names of the module contract in #13430 section 4, in camelCase:

| #13430 field | Descriptor field | Served by the web shell |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `id` (lower-case, hyphenated; the directory name) | yes |
| `api` | `api` (the module API it is written for; `MODULE_API`, 1, when absent) | yes: another version is refused |
| `feature` | `feature` (its hello feature flag, `module.<id>`; see "When a module is there") | yes |
| `needs` | `needs` (other modules it may import; ESLint holds it to them) | yes (guard) |
| `wants` | `wants` (modules it uses when they are there) | declared, not yet served |
| `shell_places` | `routes` (a page: a base segment, its aliases, its title), `extensionPages` (reserved `/extension/-<id>/…` pages the module draws, such as the health module's water and protein pages, #13176), `navItems` (a sidebar entry and the page it follows; `shown`, an optional condition read with each look at the sidebar, with its own `subscribe`), `kbKinds` (knowledge entry kinds whose page it adds parts to: the `kb.detail` slot) and `standalonePages` (pages it draws on their own, without the app shell: see **Pages of their own** below) | yes |
| `i18n_namespaces` | `i18nNamespaces` and `locales` (its catalog loaders) | yes |
| `settings` | `settingsTabs` (a Settings category in one of its groups) and `settingsRows` (rows in a section of a core Settings page, one of `SETTINGS_ROW_PLACES`: `connectors.lark`, drawn by `web/src/core/SettingsRows.tsx`) | yes (#13846, #13404) |
| `chat_card_kinds` | `cardRenderers` (pending-card kinds the core has no card for) | yes (#13846) |
| `composer_actions`, `chat_accessories` | `chatSlots`: `composer.trailingAction`, `chat.tail`, `chat.bar`, `interaction.asked` | yes (#13846) |

`registerModule` refuses a descriptor that fills a field the shell does not serve yet (`wants`) rather than dropping it
silently, and names what it refuses: a chat slot the shell does not have, a Settings category whose key is not the module's id or its id
and a suffix (a core category's key always wins in `views/settings/nav.ts`, and `modules/module-names.test.ts` fails on
a module named like one), a card kind the core draws (`CORE_CARD_KINDS`, kept the same as `Interaction.kind` by a test) or another module
renders. `loadModule` refuses code that leaves out a slot, category or card kind its descriptor names. It also refuses a
route that collides: a base that is one of
the core's first segments (`CORE_PATHS`, kept in step with `lib/router.ts` parse in both directions by its tests: every segment parse routes is
listed, and everything listed is routed or is one of the hub's own addresses beside the app), an alias that is a core
page or lies under a core address other than `/tracks/<slug>` (a space the module has its own page for), and a base or
alias that another module's base or alias starts, or that starts one of theirs. The rest of the contract (`hub_routes`,
`mcp_tools`, `prompt_sections`, `background_jobs`, …) belongs to the server.

**File previews.** A module claims file kinds in `filePreviews` and supplies a lazy `FilePreview` component.
The Office module previews documents and binary workbooks when opened. Turning it off in General or at the hub
leaves each file in its folder and opens the usual download card. CSV and TSV keep their text table viewer.

**The module list** (`web/src/modules/index.ts`) imports each module's descriptor (`modules/<id>/module.ts`) and
registers it. A descriptor the host refuses throws in development and tests, so it cannot land; in a production build
it is logged and that module is left out (absent), so one bad module does not stop the app from starting. It is the only place module ids appear outside their own directories. `App.tsx` imports it first, so the
modules are registered before any address is routed. Importing the list loads no module's code and none of its strings.

**When a module is there.** A module is *on* when the hub serves it and this browser has not switched it off. The hub
flag rule is the same on every client (agreed on #13844; `MODULES_FEATURE` and `moduleFeature` in `module-host.ts` are
the one place the names live): a module's `feature` is `module.<id>`; a hub that publishes module flags also announces
the marker `modules`; a module with a `feature` is off only when the hello has `modules` and lacks its flag. Each hub's
last module flags are remembered per hub (`localStorage` `persona.modules.hub:<origin><base>`, written only when they
change, removed when a hello lacks `modules` or on sign-out, #14431): on a reload, before the new hello arrives, the host
uses that remembered answer, so a module the hub switched off is never drawn and its chunk is never fetched while
waiting for the hello. A hub never seen before, and an older hub whose hello has no `modules`, keep every module on so
defaults never change and nothing waits on the hello to draw; a later hello that adds or drops a flag turns it on or off
at once. Otherwise it is *off*. Most off modules are absent:

- no sidebar entry, and no switch it could have left behind (the start page falls back as for a removed page);
- their addresses route as unknown ones (`not-found`), aliases included;
- neither their code chunk nor their catalog is requested. `loadModule` refuses an off module, and its page is a
  `lazyPage(…, { listed: false })`, which `loadPages` never preloads.

The built-in Health space is the default-panel exception required by #13430: with its module off, and in a core-only
build, `/health…` and `/tracks/health…` route to a read-only Health archive (`lib/health-archive.ts`,
`views/spaces/HealthReadOnlyData.tsx`). Existing conversations keep transcript reads and in-chat search; reports and
memory can be opened; no composer, new-chat, upload, edit, approval, archive or delete control is offered, and the
Health module chunk and catalog are still not requested. The enabled module keeps the full Health home and write
flows unchanged.

An on module's page is warmed as the built-in pages are (`core/ModulePage.tsx`, `lib/lazy-page.ts` `preloadOnIntent`):
when the pointer, the focus or a finger reaches a link to it (its sidebar entry); not with Data Saver on, and never for
an off module. Never at idle: that would make every browser fetch every module, outside `IDLE_TIER_BUDGET`. Otherwise it loads on its first render: its strings first (`i18n` `addCatalogs`; its code may call `t()` at module
scope), then its code. A module's namespace files (`<id>.json`, `<id>-*.json`) live under its own `locales/<lang>/`
or under `src/i18n/locales/<lang>/`. The catalog checks cover both locations. The build places those strings in
the module's own catalog (`?catalog=module-<id>`, `web/i18n-catalogs.ts`). A module's sidebar label, page title and feature description
are read before its strings load, so their keys live in shell namespaces such as `sidebar.json`, `app.json` and
`settings-features.json`.

**Chat slots, Settings categories and cards** (#13846, `web/src/core/ChatSlots.tsx`, `core/ModuleSettingsPage.tsx`).
A module's code (`ModuleCode`) fills what its descriptor names: `chat` for its chat slots, `settings` for its categories
by key, `cards` for its card kinds. The chat page hands every chat slot the same `ChatPageProps` (the conversation, its
session, who answers, whether it can send, the transcript and the cards on read, Stop):

- `composer.trailingAction`: mounted while the page shows the conversation (it may draw a dialog); it tells the page its
  `ComposerAction` (icon, name, tooltip, `primary`, click), which the composer draws in its own style: a tool button,
  or with an empty box and nothing to stop, a primary one round in the Send button's place.
- `chat.tail`: after the last message of the thread.
- `chat.bar`: drawn in the dock over the composer (`place: "dock"`) and where the composer is (`place: "composer"`);
  while one says `take(true)` (in a layout effect, so before the frame is painted) the composer hides with its draft
  kept and the Assistant's action rows give way, as they do for a live voice call.
- `interaction.asked`: in a pending card's kicker row, after its kind.

A module's Settings category is listed after its group's own (`views/settings/nav.ts` `navGroups`), opens by
`?tab=<key>`, is found by the search box, and draws the module's page, loaded on its first render. A pending card whose
kind a module renders is drawn by that module (`InteractionCard`), before the generic fallback. A slot loads its
module's code when a page first reaches it and draws nothing until it is in, and nothing at all while the module is
off, so with no module filling a slot every screen is as it was; a module's part that throws is left out, not the page.
Settings search opens the Optional features group in General or jumps to an individual module's switch.

**The switch.** Settings › General › Optional features uses `ConfigurationForm` with the registry-backed source in
`web/src/core/module-features.ts`. It lists every registered module, including modules switched off, and is omitted
from a core-only build. These are lasting browser preferences for shipped features. Each defaults to on. The browser
stores the ids switched off as a JSON array in `localStorage` under `persona.modules.off`
(`web/src/core/module-switch.ts`). Changes take effect in every tab of this browser. Hub availability still applies,
and a module the hub does not serve has a read-only switch with the reason.

**The guard.** `npm run lint` runs a second pass over all of `src` with `web/eslint.modules.config.mjs`:
`no-restricted-imports` and `no-restricted-syntax` (for `import()`) catch the spelled paths, and the config's own
`persona-modules/boundary` rule resolves every relative import, export and `import()` (a template literal by its static
start, refused when it could still reach `src/modules`) to where it lands. Together they keep files outside `src/modules` from importing a
module's files (the list is the way in; tests may reach a module's files to test them), keep `src/core` from importing
even the list, and keep a module from importing the list (`../`, `../../modules`, …) or another module its `module.ts` does not name in
`needs`. `web/src/core/module-boundary.lint.test.ts` holds the cases. Disables of
those rules are counted by `scripts/ci/web_module_boundary_ratchet.py` (`scripts/ci/guards.sh`); the baseline,
`scripts/ci/web_module_boundary_baseline.json`, started empty and can only shrink. `web/src/modules/module-names.test.ts`
fails when a module's id, route base or sidebar key appears in the `Route` union, the sidebar's built-in pages, their
colors or the Settings tabs, and when a module namespace is on the first screen.

**The core-only lane** (#13932). Persona Core is a product of its own, so CI builds and tests it with zero modules:
`npm run build:core-only` and `npm run test:core-only` (both in `scripts/ci/web.sh`) set `PERSONA_WEB_MODULES=none`, and
`web/core-only.ts` then resolves the module list to an empty one and fails the build, or the test file, when any file
outside `src/modules` reaches a module's file once its path is resolved (what the ESLint pass cannot read). The modules' own tests are left
out of that run. A core test that is about a module being there (the Health sidebar entry, its route) says which module
it needs (`MODULES.some((m) => m.id === "health")`) and skips that part without it; a test of a module's own code lives
in the module's directory.

**The `kb.detail` slot** (`web/src/core/ModuleKBDetail.tsx`). A module that names a knowledge kind in `kbKinds` adds parts
to the page of every entry of that kind (`views/knowledge/KBDetail.tsx`): buttons beside **Ask Persona**, sections first
in the body, sections after the entry's facts, sections after the code directories, dialogs, and whether the page leaves
its profile out. The page lays itself out as a function of those parts (`ModuleKBDetailParts`); the module's component
(`ModuleCode.KBDetail`) calls its hooks and hands the page its parts. Its code loads when an entry of that kind opens;
until it is in, or with no module on for the kind, the page draws with none. One module per kind. While a module is
off, an entry of its kind is absent: its address routes as an unknown one, an open one says it is not there, and the
lists and searches that would show it leave it out. Existing recordings are the exception: their data stays in Core,
so the default Knowledge panel keeps their routes, rows and search results and renders a read-only detail.

**Pages of their own** (#14404, `standalonePages`). A module may draw a page with no app shell (no sign-in flow, no
sidebar), named by its address' first segment: the screen-share module's `/screen/<machine>`. The modules that have
one are also listed in `web/src/modules/standalone.ts`, the part of the module list `main.tsx` loads before App
(`index.ts` takes them in). Its `standalonePage(address)` finds the module for the address: while it is on, it loads
the module's strings, then its code, and returns what `ModuleCode.Standalone(address)` draws, which `main.tsx` renders
as the whole page; that function takes from the address what must not stay there (the app's token in the fragment)
before App could read it, and returns null for an address that is not its page after all, which then opens the app.
Before it loads anything of the module it reads one hello on a socket of its own (`hubServesHere`, at most 2.5 s).
The hub's remembered per-origin/subpath flags apply while it waits and when none arrives in time; only a first-seen hub,
or an older one without the `modules` marker, defaults to on. While the module is off (this browser's switch, remembered
hub flags, or a hello with the `modules` marker and without its flag) the address is absent: its fragment is dropped, so
a token meant for the page is never taken for a sign-in, the app routes it as an unknown address, and the module's chunk
and strings are never requested. That file reaches the descriptors, the switch and the strings loader, never the host or the whole
list: what `main.tsx` reaches is split out of App's chunks, and the whole list made the first screen about 30 KB
heavier (so `moduleFeature` and `MODULES_FEATURE` live in `web/src/core/module-flags.ts`, which the host re-exports).
Inside the app the host serves the field like the others: `registerModule` refuses a segment that is a core address,
another module's page of its own, or a route of any module; `loadModule` refuses code without `Standalone`;
`standaloneAt(segments)` answers absent while the module is off; and the core's links to the page ask
`standaloneOn(base)`, which follows the hub flag like any module entry (the machine page's **View screen**). The code is
the module's `standalone.tsx`: the build (`vite.config.ts`, `src/startup-preload.ts` `standalonePages`) reads
`standalonePages` from each `module.ts`, preloads that file's chunks on its addresses (not while this browser switched
the module off or its remembered per-hub flags say it is off), and lets its import run without waiting for the rest of the catalog, as `main.tsx`'s own imports do;
so that file and what it imports statically may read only the first screen's core strings and the module's own (the
build checks it).

**The screen-share module** (#14404). The live screen of a computer (`web/src/modules/screen-share/`,
`docs/extensions/computer-use.md` "Live view"): the noVNC view, the video picture and its tiers, the Displays menu, the
stats overlay and the data-use meter, with their strings (`screen-share-screen.json`, `screen-share-screenview.json`,
`screen-share-video.json`, `screen-share-displays.json`), which no longer ship in every first screen's catalog. Its hub
flag is `module.screen-share`; off, the machine page has no **View screen** and `/screen/<machine>` is an unknown
address. Its Labs name and line are `sidebar.json`'s. `lib/computer.ts` (whether a Mac offers its screen, the page's
address) stays in core with the machine page.

**The lark module** (#13404, web half). The Messages page (`web/src/modules/lark/`,
`docs/extensions/lark-migration.md` "Entry point"): every Lark chat in one list (`Messages.tsx`, `lark-chats.ts`), its
sidebar entry right after Inbox and the "Show messages on home" row of Settings › Connectors › Lark (`LarkHomeSwitch.tsx`,
the `connectors.lark` place), with their strings (`lark-messages.json`, `lark-chats.json`, `lark-homeswitch.json`). The
entry keeps its old condition through `shown` (`home.ts`: this browser's switch, and a hub that reads Lark); the page
opens from its address whatever the switch says, as before. Its code entry (`lark-code.ts`) holds the row and the page as a
chunk of its own, so the Connectors page draws the row without loading the page. Its hub flag is `module.lark`; off,
there is no entry and no row, `/messages` is an unknown address, and the chunk and strings are never requested. The
Inbox's Lark chat view (`views/inbox/LarkThread.tsx`), its parts (`Chip`, `Count`, `LarkAvatar`), `lib/lark-history.ts`
(with the chat type), `lib/lark-accounts.ts` and the account its writes carry (`lib/lark-account.ts`, which the
module's lists keep current) stay in core.

**The recording module** (#13407, web half). A recording's parts of its knowledge page
(`web/src/modules/recording/`, `docs/assistant/meeting-minutes.md`, `docs/assistant/day-recap.md`): Rename and Hand to
Agent, the latest hand-off, its facts, the private mark, the minutes or an all-day recording's recap, the live view, the
conversation, the questions, the photos and the transcript, with their strings (`recording.json`,
`recording-handoff.json`) and the recording's view of its entry (`recording-view.ts`: its transcript lines, an all-day
recording's parts of the day, its meeting's room, follow-up and photos). Its switch's name and description come from
`sidebar.json`. It names the `recordings` kind. When switched off, the Meetings list and search keep existing
recordings, and `views/knowledge/RecordingReadOnlyDetail.tsx` renders their stored minutes, recaps, transcripts and
photos read-only, without importing the module or showing its write and live controls. When the hub marks an in-flight
recording with `paused: "module_off"` (decoded through `recordingPaused` in `lib/kb.ts`), the read-only detail shows a
quiet neutral note that minutes and transcription are paused while stored content stays readable, and ignores unknown
pause values without showing module-off wording (#15214). A photo list that is
unavailable (including a 404 from a hub before the list read moved into Core) hides only the photo section. Its hub
flag is `module.recording`: off on a hub that publishes module flags without it, or where a browser switches it off.
The recording settings (how long recordings and minutes are kept, Settings › Persona) stay in core for now.

**Mail** (#13434, #15995). Inbox readers can open, reply to and compose mail, and manage their connected accounts in
Settings. The `mailbox` contribution in `web/src/modules/mail/` provides the live client and UI. The host loads its
code and the current language's `mail.json` catalog on demand. The live reader, composer and account settings each
load when opened. Settings › General › Optional features controls this browser's switch. Hubs that publish module
flags must also advertise `module.mail`. Older hubs retain the default live reader.

With mail off on the hub or in the browser, or omitted from the build, Inbox keeps its historical items and account
filters. `views/inbox/StoredMailBody.tsx` reads the archived item from `GET /api/v1/inbox/{id}`.
`lib/mail-stored.ts` extracts the saved text, falling back to the list preview, and interprets the hub's
`mail_body_truncated` flag. The reader can display an already saved translation. Draft text, Hand to AI, Done,
folders and other Inbox actions remain available. Live account requests, message reads, attachments and sending
require the enabled provider.

**Source availability (#17399).** The Inbox reads the optional `stored_sources` from full, delta, refresh, and 304-held responses. The Lark chip and the source words in the caught-up hint follow the shared rule: the existing Lark extension capability or `hubServes(module.lark)` wins, then stored Lark items, with missing / `null` treated as unknown and visible. Mail wording follows `hubServes(module.mail)` and stored mail independently; the browser's optional-feature switch is not mistaken for hub availability. A hidden persisted Lark selection is cleared so it cannot filter invisibly. The fixed Mail *kind* chip (`KIND_FILTERS` key `mail`) follows the same mail decision through `visibleInboxKinds` (#17814), and a persisted `inbox.kind=mail` is cleared when it hides; the other kind chips stay. Per-account Mail source chips and all stored readers are unchanged. Shared cases: `spec/fixtures/inbox-sources/presence.json`; rendered coverage: `InboxList.source-availability.test.tsx`.

**The pilot: health.** The Health page (`web/src/modules/health/`, docs/assistant/health.md) is the first module. Its
route (`/health`, `/health/new`, `/health/<id>`, and `/tracks/health…`), its water and protein pages (the reserved
extension-page id `-health-intake`, which routes as unknown while the module is off), its sidebar entry (right after Inbox, pink with
Colored icons) and its `health` namespace come from its descriptor instead of the `Route` union, `App.tsx` and
`SidebarParts.tsx`. Its flag is `module.health`: every hub before #13844 publishes no module flags and keeps it on, as
the page always was, and a browser can still switch it off. Core code that needs one of its addresses writes the path (`/health/<id>`).
With the module off, that path does not become a dead link: the default-panel Health archive below reopens the stored data
read-only, including in a core-only build.

### Adding a module

1. Create `web/src/modules/<id>/` with `module.ts` exporting its `ModuleDescriptor`: the id (from #13430 section 2), its
   hub `feature` if the hub has one, `title` and `description` for the General switch, its `routes` and `navItems`, its
   `i18nNamespaces` with `locales: byLanguage(import.meta.glob("../../i18n/locales/*/_meta.json", { query: "?catalog=module-<id>" }))`,
   and `load: () => import("./Page").then((m) => ({ Page: m.Page }))`.
2. Move the feature's files into the directory and fix their imports; the shared helpers they use stay in core.
3. Rename or move its namespace files to `<id>.json` / `<id>-*.json` in every language (either under `src/i18n/locales/<lang>/` or the module’s own `locales/<lang>/`), and take them out of
   `src/i18n/startup-namespaces.json`.
4. Add the descriptor to `MODULES` in `web/src/modules/index.ts`, and remove the feature's hand-wired entries (its
   `Route` variant, its `lazyPage` line, its sidebar entry, its color in `lib/sidebar-icons.ts`).
5. Tests: the module's own `module.test.tsx` (on and off: entry, route, chunk and catalog requests), and
   `npm run lint`, which now covers it. `npm run build:core-only` and `npm run test:core-only` must still pass: the
   core may not need the module.

## Developing Persona (#9617)

Settings › About Persona's switch that records this browser's requests, socket frames, pages, errors and console lines
and exports them as one zip, sent to an Agent's chat or downloaded: [developing-persona.md](../operations/developing-persona.md).
It costs the first screen nothing (its chunks load only while it is on).

**The To-dos view's shadow (#10226).** With the switch on, the recorder also starts
`web/src/features/todos/model/view-shadow.ts` (a chunk of its own). While the hub lists `todo_view`, each row that
carries a `view` also goes through today's triage, and `view-legacy.ts` maps the view onto today's sections (Waiting is
Parked, Can wait is Needs you, To do with the Inactive mark is Shelved) and explains the differences the redesign decided
(`docs/assistant/todo-status-sop.md` "The hub's view"). Only what nothing explains is recorded, as ids and enum words
(`docs/operations/developing-persona.md`). The manager does not yet push when a run changes a view, so a row whose runs
moved after the list was read is counted apart and the list is read again. Independently of Developing Persona (#14583),
whenever the hub lists `todo_view`, the To-dos status list's sections, rank and filtered header counts draw from the
hub's `view` by default (`view-triage.ts`; a row without a `view` or with an unknown `phase`, `section` or `reason`
falls back row-by-row to local triage via `view-legacy.ts`). Setting `localStorage persona.todos.viewDraw` to `0` (then
reloading) reverts that browser to local triage. Each row's checkbox, Got it and line 2, the folder and Pinned
groupings, and the sidebar badge / tray / detail actions keep today's rules: a failed start the view files in To do
still shows a ticked checkbox (`Todos.view-draw.test.tsx` pins the default projection, rollback and fallback).

## Error reports (#5533)

The page reports its own errors to `POST /api/v1/error-reports` (`lib/error-reports.ts`, wired up in `lib/error-reports-start.ts`; format and rules in [protocol.md](../protocol/protocol.md) "Error reports"). No UI, no strings.

- **Captured**: `window` `error` events (not a cross-origin "Script error." with no error), `unhandledrejection` (not an `AbortError`), and what the two boundaries catch: `PageBoundary` reports a render crash as `fatal` and a chunk that still would not load after its one reload as `warning`; the first chunk failure, which only reloads (a redeployed hub), is not reported. `OverlayBoundary` reports a failed chunk as `warning`, anything else `fatal`. Both draw and close exactly as before. A boundary's report carries where it caught the error: the component stack (React's `ErrorInfo.componentStack`, `componentFrames` in `lib/error-reports.ts`) as an outer exception of type `ComponentStack` (value `caught by <boundary>`), one frame per component, innermost last, with file and position where React gives them and the name alone where it does not; the error itself stays the innermost (last) exception, which the hub fingerprints by. Each of these reports is `source: "web"`, `kind: "exception"`, a fresh UUID, `os` / `os_version` from the user agent (coarse), no `release` / `build` (the bundle has no version of its own) and no `device_model`; the stack becomes frames (V8 and Firefox / Safari formats), innermost last, `file` the script URL's path only, `in_app` for same-origin `/assets/` (`/src/` in dev).
- **A frozen page** (#1721, `lib/freeze-watch.ts`): once the hub is online and a hello's `features` has `error_reports`, a `PerformanceObserver` watches `long-animation-frame`, or `longtask` where the browser has no long-animation-frame. Where it has neither, nothing is sent. The observer asks for entries already buffered, so a block from after the document became interactive, earlier in that same page load, is included; before that hello, and after a hello that drops the feature, nothing is queued (a hello without the feature, or an `{"enabled": false}` answer, also drops a warning already kept). An entry that starts before DOMContentLoaded is the first load, not a freeze. Time a script spent paused (a debugger breakpoint, a modal or a synchronous request) does not count toward the 5 seconds, and neither does a jump of the wall clock that the monotonic clock did not see (the machine slept). A long animation frame counts its blocking time, not the whole frame, so a frame that only waited (a backgrounded window, a throttled scheduler) is not a freeze. An entry lasting 5 seconds of real work or more is one report for that page load and the observer stops. The report's time is when the block started. If that warning is still queued when the feature turns off, it does not use up the page's one report. The report is `kind: "anr"`, `level: "warning"`, message `Main thread blocked for <milliseconds>ms`, the breadcrumbs already kept, and `tags.mechanism` of the entry type. Script attribution is frames, innermost last, at most 8, the longest script last (that is the one the hub fingerprints by): a long animation frame's script URL and function name, or a long task's container URL, each cut to its path (`file` and `module`, `in_app` like a stack frame; the hub fingerprints an in-app frame by `module` and the function name, not by the file alone). No host, query, fragment, element id or name, and no `data:`, `blob:` or `javascript:` URL. A hidden tab sends nothing. An entry that overlaps the page being hidden or frozen is dropped (`visibilitychange`, and the page's `freeze` / `resume`), so a background tab and a gap from the machine sleeping are not an ANR. It then takes the same queue, scrubbing and retry as the other reports; the feature turning off drops it.
- **No user content**: an error's name, message and stack, or a freeze's script path, with URLs cut to their path and queries, fragments and e-mail addresses taken out (the hub scrubs again). The last 30 breadcrumbs: the route's name on navigation (never ids or query), and each failed hub request as `METHOD /path/:id status` (`0` / `network` when it did not get there; path segments that aren't the API's own words become `:id`; the reports' own requests are left out).
- **Gate**: sent only while the hub's hello `features` has `error_reports`. Before the first hello reports are kept; a hello without it (or a `{"enabled": false}` answer) drops what was kept, and nothing more is kept on that page.
- **Console**: whatever the hub's features say, an error a boundary catches is logged with its component stack (`createRoot`'s `onCaughtError`, `lib/caught-error.ts`; React's own handler logs the error alone). Production names are minified; the frames map back with a source-mapped build of the same commit.
- **Queue**: `localStorage` `persona.errorReports`, at most 50, none older than 7 days; what an earlier page load left is sent with `previous_launch`. Sent on the hello with the feature and 2 seconds after a new report, 20 a request; a 2xx removes them, a network failure, 5xx, 408 or 429 keeps them for the next try, any other 4xx drops them. The same message and top frame within 5 seconds is kept once. Reporting never throws, and an error while reporting is not reported.

## On computers

On a Mac, Windows or Linux computer, the hub-hosted web UI is Persona's interface, in a browser or in the Electron desktop app ([desktop.md](../desktop/desktop.md)).

- **In the browser**: open the hub's address and sign in.
- **As an app**: in Chrome or Edge, use **Install** in **Settings › General › This browser › Install as app** when the browser offers it, otherwise the browser's own install menu; these need https, or localhost.
  Safari on a Mac adds it with **File › Add to Dock**. Either way it opens in its own window with Persona's icon ("Install as an App" below).
- **Needs-you signals** (tab count, icon badge, alert sound, system notifications) work while a Persona page is open in some tab or window ("Attention signals" below). Once every Persona page is closed, only a browser that turned on **Settings › Notifications › When Persona is closed** still hears of cards, finished turns and alerts ("Web Push" below); on a computer where Persona Link or the desktop app already notifies, leave it off.
- **Opening the web app alone does not activate the phone's Phone Muted**: a plain browser does not register as a desktop client (`register_desktop`). In the Electron desktop app, an authenticated connection registers only while the desktop is active and system notifications are on. Locking, becoming idle or turning system notifications off sends `unregister_desktop`, so the phone gets alerts again without losing the chat connection. On a hub without the `desktop_unregister` capability, withdrawal closes the socket instead; becoming active or re-enabling notifications reconnects it so the next authenticated hello can register again. On a Mac running the Persona Link menu bar App in active mode while you are at it, **Phone Muted** holds back the "Needs you" cards whose notifications that App handed to Notification Center; other pushes still reach the phone ([link.md](../operations/link.md), "Presence").
- **Persona Link**, on a computer whose Agents the hub should reach, connects it to the hub and does what a browser cannot ([link.md](../operations/link.md), "On computers: Persona Link and its tray"). A computer you only browse from does not need it.

## Install as an App (PWA, #1772)

The web app can be installed on a phone's home screen / a computer's desktop and opens in its own window, with the same icon and name as the iOS App.

- **manifest** (`public/manifest.webmanifest`): `standalone`; `start_url` / `scope` are both `./` (relative to the manifest: `/` at the root path, `/<prefix>/` under a subpath); background and theme colors are the light `--page`.
  Shortcuts on long-pressing the icon: New chat, Inbox, Agents, Machines. The hub explicitly sets `application/manifest+json` for `.webmanifest` (Go's built-in table doesn't have it, and nosniff is on);
  it, `sw.js`, the icons and every other file beside `index.html` (not the licenses) are `no-cache` like `index.html` (`server/internal/hub/web.go`): checked again on each load, and a 304 while unchanged.
  The data directory's copy revalidates by `Last-Modified`; the copy built into the hub has no modification times, so each of those files carries an `ETag`, the first 128 bits of its content's SHA-256, worked out on its first request and kept (`index.html`'s covers the sub-path's `<base>`, and is weak when it goes gzipped).
- **Icons** are all scaled down from `AppIcon.appiconset`, not redrawn: `app-icon-192/512.png` (`purpose: any`; desktop installs use `mac-512@2x.png`, the Mac icon with rounded corners and margins);
  `app-icon-maskable-192/512.png` (Android's mask: the full-bleed `icon.png` scaled to 84%, the surroundings filled by extending its own edges, so the waving line falls inside the central 80% safe circle);
  `apple-touch-icon.png` (180, full-bleed `icon.png`; iOS adds the rounded corners itself).
- **iOS**: `apple-mobile-web-app-capable`, status bar `default` (content starts below the status bar, so in neither light nor dark mode does white text sit on a light background); when running standalone, `#root` leaves room for the bottom safe area and the side safe areas in landscape (`display-mode: standalone` in `styles.css`).
  The home-screen App's storage is separate from Safari's, so the first launch needs signing in again (paste the token or use a `?token=` link).
- **theme-color**: two `<meta name="theme-color">` tags (the light / dark `--page`), following the system. When Settings picks light or dark, the first-frame script in `index.html` and `views/theme.ts` change the matching tag's `media` to `all`, so the address bar / title bar color follows the page.
- **service worker** (`src/sw.ts`, built separately by Vite into `sw.js` at the root; rules in `lib/sw-routes.ts`, with unit tests):
  - Opening the page: it first waits for the hub's `index.html` (3.5 seconds); if it arrives it is used and a copy is stored. If the hub is slow or unreachable it uses the stored copy, the page starts as usual and shows its own "Can't reach the hub". When the server answers the page load with a redirect (an `opaqueredirect`, a 3xx or a followed redirect) or 401/403, such as an expired sign-in in front of the hub sending the browser to its login page, that answer goes to the browser instead of the stored copy, and a redirected page is never stored as the shell (`lib/sw-shell.ts`). The shell is stored under the single key `/`, so `?token=` links never enter the cache.
  - Hashed files under `/assets/`: cache first, fetched if missing; the most recent 400 are kept (about three builds, so a version change never deletes ones in use). Whenever the shell updates, it also fetches the scripts and CSS its first screen needs, so it can open during the next outage too.
    A lazy page's chunk is kept once this browser has fetched it (the page was opened, it is in the idle tier, or a link to it was reached; see "First screen"). One never fetched is not there during an outage: opening it then shows "This page didn't load" with **Reload** (`views/PageBoundary.tsx`), as with Data Saver on.
  - Icons and the manifest at the root: the hub's first, the stored copy if that fails. The worker's fetch goes through the browser's HTTP cache, so an unchanged icon costs a 304.
  - `/api/` (data, WebSocket, images) and `/admin` never go through it, so data is always live.
  - It only registers in a secure context (https or localhost). Opened over plain http on the intranet it is an ordinary web page; iOS can still "Add to Home Screen", but without the offline shell. Chrome / Edge need https to install (public TLS: see `docs/operations/network.md`).
    It doesn't register in development (`npm run dev`), nor under a reverse proxy subpath (see "Subpath" above).
  - New versions (#4331): the worker answers a navigation with the new shell, but a page that stays open never navigates, so it kept an old build for days. See "New versions" below.
- **Settings › General › This browser › Install as app** (`lib/pwa.ts`): when the browser offers an install prompt (Chrome, Edge) it is an "Install" button;
  on iPhone / iPad it points to "Add to Home Screen" in Safari's share menu, Safari on Mac to **File › Add to Dock**, other browsers on http explain that https is needed, and the rest point to the browser menu. Already in a standalone window, it shows "Installed".

## Sharing an Agent session (#3605)

The Agent chat's **⋯** menu has **Share…** (`src/sharing/`), a dialog over the server sharing contract (#3604):
the complete message catalog (paged, all history) with **All messages / From a message / Choose messages**, then
**Include future messages** and **Include work details** (both off by default) and a lifetime of 1, 3, 7 or 30 days
(default 3). Creating needs a sanitized preview and an explicit sensitivity confirmation; on an HTTP sharing origin the
server's transport warning is shown and needs a second confirmation. The link appears once with **Copy**; the dialog
lists existing links without tokens, narrows them (work details off, future off, shorter lifetime) without a new
preview, and revokes after a destructive confirmation. Create is never retried automatically, every request names its
manager with `X-Persona-Manager`, and responses that arrive after the session or manager changed are dropped.
Sessions on a computer reached through another hub of the group are not shareable from the web yet.

The public viewer is a separate document and build: `public-share/` with `vite.public.config.ts`, emitted to
`dist/public-share/index.html` and `dist/public-share/share-assets/` and served by the hub only on the configured
sharing origin. A build plugin fails when the emitted graph reaches anything outside `public-share/`, its own
catalogs and the shared palette, so it has no sign-in, store, API client, service worker, manifest or telemetry.
It renders escaped plain text (no HTML, links, images or cards), keeps work details collapsed, fetches with
`credentials:"omit"`, `cache:"no-store"` and rejected redirects, keeps one request in flight, polls every 15 seconds
(live) or 30 seconds (static), pauses in hidden tabs and hides old content until it revalidates, and clears on a
404 or at local expiry. It stores neither the link nor the content. The main app's service worker passes `/share`,
`/share-assets` and `/public-share` through untouched, so an installed app never answers a share link with its shell.

## Subscription usage (bottom of the sidebar, #2432)

At the very bottom of the sidebar (below the Agents list): one thin bar for each of the two subscription accounts with the least headroom left before their protection line, filled to what is left and labelled "N% left" (green, orange or red by `remainingTone`, #14690). Clicking opens a popover with one popover-level header (title, sort hint, and a display-only **Cards / Table** view toggle persisted per browser in `persona.usage.viewMode`, defaulting to Cards, #15848), provider cards taking up to three columns on wide viewports when single-column height exceeds a comfortable threshold (`docs/server/usage-windows.md`, "Provider cards and the reset timeline"), and a collapsible unified reset timeline at the bottom (defaulting to a one-line next-reset summary that truncates only the account name while keeping the window and countdown visible, expanded on click and persisted in `persona.usage.timelineOpen`). **With no data the whole block is not drawn.** Data comes from `GET /api/v1/usage/windows` (the manager groups samples from each computer's node and the hub forwards them),
refreshed once a minute, with no requests while the page is in the background. The pace and countdown algorithms, and how Claude's usage is hooked up, are in [usage-windows.md](../server/usage-windows.md).
Accounts come from files read on the computers and from the account-pool gateways the hub queries (#2595): in the popover, each account shows its normalized plan badge beside the name and its sources underneath ("MacBook · Relay": the computers that read it by name, then the gateways; with only one source it names that one); single-account provider cards whose account name matches the provider title merge their header to avoid repeating the title, and per-account sample ages omit duplicates that already match the card header unless stale. When a local-only row and an external row under the same provider share an active reset timestamp, a non-destructive overlap hint appears on the local row while keeping both rows intact; if that overlapping local reading is also stale, it collapses by default into a single expandable summary row.
Multi-window model pools (such as Antigravity's per-model groups) and usage-extension `group` blocks render once under their group heading instead of repeating the heading per window, while single-window per-model allowances alongside plan windows (such as `7d` + `Fable`) keep column 1 strictly to the window length and place the deduplicated model/title caption directly above the aligned meter track; extension `note` fields display quietly beneath the row. Table view aligns windows by duration (`5h`, `7d`, and `Other` when needed) with 3-state column sorting and low-interference inline pin toggles. When a gateway can't be read it says "these are its last numbers". The sidebar bar's tooltip also gives the source. Gateways are configured under "Usage sources" in the admin interface (`docs/operations/admin.md`).
A prepaid account with no rate-limit window (the official DeepSeek launcher, #11825) is a row of its own: the collapsed strip shows its name and the provider's amount and currency ("CNY 12.34"), without taking a bar from the two window accounts, and the popover lists it beside them. A genuine zero is shown as `CNY 0.00`; an unreadable balance shows `—` in the strip, and the popover says "Balance unavailable" and why, so it never becomes a zero; a failure after a successful read keeps the last amount and says so.
**Pinning chosen accounts and windows (#12418, #13870):** By default the collapsed strip shows the two window accounts with the least headroom plus live prepaid balance rows. Inside the popover, each live account (window or balance) and each individual `UsageWindow` row has a pin toggle to choose which account(s) or specific progress window(s) (such as Antigravity's per-model `7d` window) stay visible in the collapsed strip in pinned order, with a **Reset to automatic** action whenever custom pins are active. The selection is stored per browser in `localStorage` (`persona.usage.pinnedAccounts`) using plain account IDs for account-level pins (backward-compatible) and `window:<encoded-account-id>:<windowKey>` entries for specific windows, syncs across tabs via `storage` events, falls back cleanly to tab-local in-memory state when `localStorage` is unavailable, and is display-only (it does not affect launchers, models, sign-in state, scheduling, or backend polling). A pinned window renders its own remaining-quota meter bar (`remainingTone` colour and `"N% left"`) with the account/model title and non-truncating window length tag (`5h`, `7d`). The popover still lists every live account and window; if some pinned windows or accounts temporarily disappear, surviving pins remain shown, and if all pinned items are offline, expired, or hidden by an administrator, the collapsed strip falls back automatically to the default ranking rather than rendering empty.
Code: `lib/usage-windows.ts` (pure helpers and pinned-account/window store, with unit tests), `lib/usage-pace.ts` (popover pace calculation), `lib/usage-popover.ts` (popover-only plan normalization, window grouping sort, provider card, and axis helpers), `lib/usage-popover-model.ts` (popover-only window section grouping, table model, overlap hints, and browser-local view/timeline preferences), `lib/usage-timeline.ts` (the popover's unified timeline and pause rules), `views/UsageBars.tsx`, `views/UsagePopover.tsx`; the mock hub has `MOCK_USAGE=none` to simulate no data and `MOCK_USAGE=gateways` to simulate a mix of computer and gateway accounts.

## Model pill and model panel (#5032)

Who it serves: people working with coding Agents in the **Agents** chats, and everyone in a Persona chat (#5033), where it
reads as plain choices of a model. The user asked (2026-11-12) for this part of the chat page to match Cindy's model
selector; where Persona's earlier rules differ, Cindy's wins, built from Persona's tokens and components
(`docs/design/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md` 3.1).

- **Where**: an Agent chat's composer and a Persona chat's (the main chat, the others and the new-chat page), at the right
  of its bottom row, before voice / Stop / Send (`Composer`'s `trailing` slot, `views/chat/ModelPill.tsx`). The permission
  chip stays at the left; the thinking-effort chip, a Persona chat's launcher chip and an Agent's "launcher · model" text
  are gone, and the context bar below the composer does not name the model.
- **What the pill shows**: `[engine][model][effort][speed][⌄]`: the mark of the Agent the launcher runs, drawn once and first
  (#5497: `AgentMark`, as in the Agents list; an Agent with no mark of its own gets the generic `agent` icon, never a
  letter, unless its runtime names it, #8142), the model as its launcher's list names it (before that list is in, a short form of the ID such as `opus 5.5`),
  the thinking effort in the text colour, one filled bolt for Fast or two for Ultrafast, and the workflow mark while ultracode (or a
  Codex thread's ultra) is on. The pill, effort controls and settings use Minimal, Low, Medium, High, XHigh, Max and Ultra
  in all three languages. Explanations use the page's language. When the pill shows a tier, it drops the effort qualifier
  from the model name and retains context sizes. An Antigravity variant can supply the pill's tier from its catalog ID.
  No frame at rest; on hover and while the panel is open, a 1 px `--line-strong` capsule on `--hover`. Tooltip:
  "Claude Code · Opus 5.5 · gateway · High[ · Fast]". The accessible name also includes the speed when shown.
  One of Paseo's providers is its own engine (#8142): its mark, and its label in the tooltip ("Grok · Grok 4 · grok"),
  never `paseo`; the panel's rows, its Agent block and its reasons name it the same way.

  supported Claude Code sessions offer Standard / Fast. The selector and model rows use the same bolts as the pill.
  Standard has no mark. The selected speed follows session acknowledgment. Saved
  setups that used the old Fast flag still read as Fast, and saved setups without a speed read as Standard where
  the model offers it. Choosing a different model sends no speed request based on the previous model's tiers.
- **Widths**: the composer card is a container (`@container/composer`). From 600 px the pill takes 72–320 px; under 600 it

  audit 2026-11-14, item 50). It shrinks only when the row is short of room: the name gives way first, the engine mark stays, and the effort truncates only
  once the name has no room left. Under 520 px its text is 12 px and its marks a step smaller. Under 420 px the
  compact pill is 64 px for the engine mark and chevron, and grows to fit a speed mark or a waiting switch's clock.

  keeps its clock and current-to-next tooltip. Without an explicit launcher the earlier model-only label and compact
  fallback apply. Persona's pill is unchanged. This changes presentation only, never the model-selection payload.
- **States**: reading the list for the first time with no model known: a spinner and "Loading model…"; that read failed: a
  warning in the error colour ("Model loading failed" in the tooltip); a switch to another launcher waiting for the next
  message (`pending_switch` on the session, #5035): a clock first, then the setup the next message runs on: its engine's
  mark, the launcher's name before the model (gone when the pill is narrow; the engine's name instead when the engine changes, as in
  Cindy), the model as that launcher's list names it (none picked: its default) and the effort, with the tooltip
  "Current: …" / "Next message: …" and the accessible name "Select model. Next message: work · GLM 5.3, thinking effort:
  High"; a switch on its way: dimmed, no clicks. An Agent that can switch neither its model nor its effort (offline, a
  read-only source) gets the same words as a label, not a button; with no model known either, nothing.
- **Providers** (`lib/session-models.ts` reads them, `lib/session-panel.ts` builds the panel's data and what a pick

  each with the models its agent lists in its own /model menu (`GET …/launchers/{name}/models`, the list **New agent**
  uses). The pill reads the session's own list once (for the model's name); the panel, on each opening, shows the lists
  read before at once and reads every list again behind them, the session's own first, at most three at a time.
  A Persona chat's pill (and the main chat's other-agent notice) reads the computer's `?purpose=assistant` launchers,
  and Main chat's or the background supervisor's default, again when a push moves the conversation's `rev` (#6542), so
  a hub-side change reaches a page left open. `rev` moves with every write to the transcript, so a move while the
  conversation works waits for the turn to end and is read once then; a move while it isn't working reads at once
  (`useRevisionReread`, #12776).
- **Quota and prices** (#5056): the opening also reads each launcher's existing `GET /launchers/{name}/quota?machine=<mid>`

  nothing. A launcher summary shows the tightest weekly window's remaining percentage and bar and the reset
  time in its tooltip (warning at ≤ 30% left, critical at ≤ 10% or exhausted, matching `quotaTone`). An exact built-in
  catalog entry's global, standard USD reference price (without an input-size tier) gives the model row one to three `$`
  marks by output price (≤ 3 / ≤ 15 / > 15 per million tokens) and the flyout's "Per 1M tokens · Input · Output · Cache
  read" line. Unknown, inherited, malformed, regional-only and input-size-tiered prices draw nothing; a reference price is
  not a quote from the gateway and is never inherited by another model.

  mounted while it loads, and a failed chunk closes only the panel so opening it again retries.

  collapsed. A collapsed launcher takes two actions to pick a model, an expanded one one. There is no separate rail,
  eight-row cutoff or More launchers bucket. The existing model rows, family folds, setup controls and selection gates
  are reused. Unknown model defaults use the existing Default model wording, not an inferred first model.
  Search shows matching launcher rows first, then one flat model list; every model and typed-ID result names its
  launcher, including on phones and when a long model ID wraps. Selecting a matching launcher clears search and opens

- **Switching rules**: the session's own launcher switches its model at once. Its models stay under its launcher. On a hub with `launcher_switch` (#5035, docs/protocol/protocol.md "Switching a running
  Agent to another provider"), a Claude Code Agent in a terminal may also pick a model of another Claude Code launcher on
  its computer (never one a runtime runs, Paseo's: the node refuses it, so its other launchers stay off with why, #8142): the pick is recorded and the user's next message from this chat carries it out (the node quits the agent
  and resumes the same conversation through that launcher in the same terminal), so a pick never interrupts the agent.
  Only that message does: the composer sends it with `apply_switch: true` while the session shows `pending_switch`;
  every other sender's message goes on the launcher the agent runs on. A message sent while the agent works, waits on
  you or has background work goes there too, and the switch waits for a later one. Those launchers keep
  their own groups; one that fixes its own `--model` offers
  only its default entry. While a switch waits, the panel's list starts with a warning line: "Switches on your next
  message: the Agent restarts on work and keeps this conversation", and its target is the panel's `pending` setup.
  Picking the session's own launcher drops the waiting switch first. On an older hub another launcher of the same engine
  is listed with its rows off: "Switching providers in a running Agent isn't available yet". Another engine's models are
  pickable on a hub with `engine_switch` ("Switching an Agent between Claude Code and Codex" below); on an older hub, and
  for a chat that can't switch engines, they are off: "Switching from Claude Code to Codex needs a new conversation". A Codex thread keeps its model
  ("Codex can't change the model of a running session"), but the model it runs still opens its flyout, where the thinking
  effort and Fast apply at once. While the Agent works or waits on you, picks are off and the panel says why. A launcher
  of the session's own that fixes its `--model` says so and takes no pick. The search reads a row's name, ID, the model
  it stands for, the spellings folded into it (`aliases`: "sonnet" finds the gateway's one Opus 5.5 row) and its
  description. Claude Code and Codex take a model ID typed into
  the search ("Use “…”", #1644, `lib/model-id.ts`) in each launcher that can take a pick here, offered only when none of
  that launcher's models answers the search (a word that names a listed model is a search); IDs typed before are listed
  and can be forgotten.
- **Applying**: a pick on the session's own launcher sends `POST …/modes {"launcher": <own>, "from": <own>}` first when
  a switch waits (it drops it), then `{"model"}`, then `{"effort"}`, then (Codex) `{"service_tier"}`, each only when it
  differs from the session's. A pick on another launcher is one `POST …/modes {"launcher", "from", "model"?, "effort"?}`:
  the model unless it is that launcher's default entry, the effort the setup has; `from` is the launcher the panel saw
  the session on, so a pick on a session that switched meanwhile is refused (`switch_stale`). The model, the effort and
  the waiting switch are drawn at once and put back with a toast in the hub's words if it says no (`switch_config_dir`,
  `switch_model_locked`, `switch_pick_model` for a default entry whose model the computer cannot see…); a switch that
  was recorded is said by a toast: "Switch scheduled: your next message moves the Agent to work · GLM 5.3". The speed waits
  for the session's push (DESIGN_SYSTEM.md "Codex speed controls"). The panel closes once a pick applied and keeps the
  old setup when it did not. An Antigravity variant brings its own thinking level. `/model` Enter in the composer opens
  the panel (where the agent switches models). Claude Code's ultracode switch is in the flyout of the model that runs.
- **The message that carries a switch out**: when the node refuses it (`409` with a `switch_*` code and `delivered: "none"`:
  the launcher went, the agent did not quit, did not come up on the new launcher…), nothing was typed and the switch is
  dropped (the pill loses its clock with the session's push), so the words go back into the box with the hub's reason in
  a toast, as an edit's refused send does (`ChatView` `deliver`, `switchRefused` in `lib/session-models.ts`), not into a
  failed bubble. Sending again sends it on the launcher the agent runs on.
- **Kept in this browser**: favorites, the last five setups that applied (Recent) and per-model customizations (effort,
  Fast) live in `localStorage` (`persona.modelPanel.<base>.agent.*`, apart from a Persona chat's). The hub has no store for
  such preferences, so they do not follow you to another browser: a choice for this step.
